## 3. First-person ("FPS") camera for Demir and Ebru

Implementation (patch `cam.wdl`, `GenelAyarlar.wdl`; all **CONFIRMED** from script text):

- `STARTER fps_camera_control` runs every frame. Active only in a loaded level (`LY_AktifLevelID != 0`), when a player is controllable and `freeze_mode == 0`.
- **F5** toggles global `fps_cam_enabled`. For Inzar (`Player_Koruyucu`) it shows a fixed English subtitle "FPS Camera feature only for the demir and ebru characters" and does not toggle; switching to Inzar forces it off.
- On enable: `camera.arc = 70`; base distance/height values are set.
- Per frame while enabled: the camera is placed `dist_total` quants behind the player along `player.pan` (`dist_planar = cos(tilt_3rd)·dist_total`) at height `yuksek` (25–35 quants): Demir idle 2/35, walking 1/30; Ebru idle 2/30, walking 0/25; aiming 3/25 with `tilt = −5`; running forward −8/25 (camera moves 8 quants *ahead* of the origin). Tilt is clamped per state (−45…40 idle, −30…40 walking, −25…40 running). Mouse X turns `player.pan` (8·`mouse_force.x`·`time`), mouse Y adds to `camera.tilt`; `validate_view()`; the existing bomb-shake offsets still apply.
- Every legacy third-person/cutscene camera writer in `cam.wdl` is wrapped in `fps_cam_enabled == 0` guards (114 occurrences), so cutscene cameras keep working when it is off.
- The player model is not hidden and no first-person weapon model is used, so it is a close over-the-shoulder/eye-height camera rather than a true FPS view. **HIGH CONFIDENCE.** The repository's `oyun_icin_fikirler/fps_mode_cam/` (`demir_fps.mdl`, prototype `cam_code.wdl`, `k22_cam.cfg` tuning numbers) is an unused prototype of the same idea. **CONFIRMED** (not referenced by B).
- Turning the camera off does not restore the previous `camera.arc`; the next legacy writer that assigns ARC restores it. **HYPOTHESIS** (only some legacy paths assign ARC each frame).

Native status: runs unchanged when patch scripts are present (pure WDL on native builtins: `key_f5`, `camera.*`, `clamp`, `cos/sin`, `mouse_force`, `validate_view`). Not available for an ISO-only installation; no native re-implementation exists (policy: no patch scripts shipped). Test status: **not exercised** in this analysis (no in-level input run). **UNKNOWN** at runtime.

| Loading | WDL compile | `dil_degistir.wdl`: `txt_load` of all six `general.txt` into `TEXT` objects with `delimit_str = ""` (one string per line), then `subtitle_variables[i] = Parse_EscapeChar(line)` for the active language; item files loaded into three inventory `TEXT` objects; missing files → `error(...)` and exit | CONFIRMED |
| Escapes | literal script strings | `\n` etc. in files (≈ 600–700 `\n` tokens per `general.txt`), converted by the DLL because A6 `txt_load` does not | CONFIRMED |
| Encoding | single-byte Windows code pages | single-byte, no BOM, CRLF: TR = CP1254, EN/DE/ES = CP1252-compatible, RU = **CP1251**, PL = **CP1250** (Polish `general.txt` itself uses only `ó` plus quotes; item files use more) | CONFIRMED (byte census, `reports/summary.json` `language`) |
| Fonts | `Font0-3.pcx`, `DocFont0-3.bmp` in `yazi_<lang>.k22` | `_data\language\_resource\texture\{pcx,bmp}\` `n*` (Latin = original glyphs), `c*` (Cyrillic), `p*` (Polish). Atlases are 32×8 cells = 256 code points addressed by raw byte value (e.g. `nFont0` 352×144, 11×18 cells). `cFont0` differs from `nFont0` in 98 cells covering CP1251 letters `0xC0–0xFF` and specials; `pFont0` in 61 cells at CP1250 Polish positions (`0x8C/0x9C`, `0x8F/0x9F`, `0xA3/0xB3`, `0xA5/0xB9`, `0xAF/0xBF`, `0xC6/0xE6`, `0xCA/0xEA`, `0xD1/0xF1`, …); both redraw `$` | CONFIRMED (cell diff of decoded PCX) |
| Font selection | per resolution index `GA_Cozunurluk` | `load_language_fonts()`: RU → `c*`, PL → `p*`, else `n*`; subtitles use `DocFont1`, panels/menus `Font0` | CONFIRMED |
| Voices | 12 clips per audio language in `ses_<lang>.k22` | `_data\language\<lang>\sound\` 12 clips; EN = DE = ES byte-identical (English audio reused); TR/EN clips are the ISO clips; RU/PL new | CONFIRMED |
| Textures with text | language archive members | `_data\language\<lang>\texture\{tga,pcx}` (31–34 TGA, 7–11 PCX); 142 of 260 images are byte-identical ISO members | CONFIRMED |
| Cut-scenes | `vt*.k22` (TR) / `ve*.k22` (EN) chosen by `defses_*` | per-language `video\` folders (TR 22, EN/PL/RU 17; DE/ES none) re-encoded | CONFIRMED |

Native status:

- ISO-only: `--language tr|en|de`, `--audio-language tr|en` map to the original `defdil_*`/`defses_*` macros and archives (`native/main.cpp`), defaulting from `LC_ALL`/`LC_MESSAGES`/`LANG`. **CONFIRMED.**
- Patch scripts: `Engine::configure_language` sets `DD_Dil` from `--language` (0/1/2 only) and maintains byte 32 of the private `options.k22`; the script's own options loader then restores the saved choice (0–5). Spanish/Russian/Polish are therefore available through the in-game menu but not via CLI ([COMMUNITY_PATCH_ANALYSIS](COMMUNITY_PATCH_ANALYSIS.md) §7.3). **CONFIRMED.**
- Bitmap fonts are raw-byte indexed in native as in A6 (`CONTRACT.txt` §40: indexed PCX FONT keeps indices, active palette), so CP1251/CP1250 text renders with the patch atlases without transcoding; BMP fonts decode through the same bitmap path (`native/assets.cpp`, `.bmp`/`.pcx` branch). **HIGH CONFIDENCE**; Cyrillic/Polish rendering was not captured in this analysis — **UNKNOWN** at runtime.
- `Parse_EscapeChar` and `txt_load` with empty delimiter are native services (`native/engine.cpp:1207`, `CONTRACT.txt` §14). **CONFIRMED.**

`docs/CAMERA_SYSTEM.md`:

```md
# Camera System

Purpose: describe how the original Kabus 22 scripts drive the A6 `camera`, other VIEWs, cutscenes and mirrors; how the native engine turns those VIEWs into projections; and what has been verified, including widescreen.

Related: [Reverse-engineering index](REVERSE_ENGINEERING.md) · [Engine architecture](ENGINE_ARCHITECTURE.md) · [Gameplay systems](GAMEPLAY_SYSTEMS.md) · [Script system](reverse-engineering/SCRIPT_SYSTEM.md) · [Original behavior](reverse-engineering/ORIGINAL_BEHAVIOR.md) · [Data structures](reverse-engineering/DATA_STRUCTURES.md) · [Function map](reverse-engineering/FUNCTION_MAP.md)

Confidence labels follow [Gameplay systems](GAMEPLAY_SYSTEMS.md#conventions-and-sources). Script line numbers refer to `reverse/extracted/original/` (cam.wdl and efect2.wdl are byte-identical in the ISO edition, per `reverse/media/iso/script-comparison.json`). `CONTRACT.txt` means `reverse/decompiled/runtime/CONTRACT.txt`.

## 1. Model: one camera action per level, no camera-mode setting

- The original game has no camera-mode option and no first-person camera. **CONFIRMED** (no first-person action in the ISO `cam.wdl`; no camera option in `GenelAyarlar.wdl`). Community patch 1.8.5 adds an F5 first-person camera (`fps_camera_control`, patch `cam.wdl:77-170`). Native offers the same camera as an opt-in engine option for the original scripts, `--camera first-person` (§7.1). The default stays `original`.
- `cam.wdl` (7316 lines) holds 109 `action` blocks, roughly one per level or area (e.g. `start4_camera` :276, `level4_camera2` :422, `mekke_camera` :891, `sd_camera1` :1071, `boss_cam` :4345, `tnel*_camera` :4499-6220). **CONFIRMED** (`grep -c '^action'` = 109).
- Each action is attached to an entity placed in the level WMB. The `LV_*.wdl` level scripts never select a camera; source comment `cam.wdl:276` reads "attach it to fish.mdl". **HIGH CONFIDENCE** (no WDL assigns these actions; WMB entity action attachment is the A6 mechanism, see CONTRACT §24).
- Standard prologue of nearly every camera action: entity `invisible`/`passable`, `camera.pos_x/pos_y=0`, `camera.size_x/size_y=screen_size`, an authored `camera.arc` (60 most common; 62-80 observed, e.g. `cam.wdl:164`=80, `:211`=60, `:287`=62), `camera.visible=on`, then a `while(1) … wait(1)` loop rewriting `camera.x/y/z/pan/tilt/roll`. **CONFIRMED**
- Entity skills/flags parameterise the camera from the level editor: `Cam_No`=SKILL1, `Cam_Arc`=SKILL2, `Effect_Mesafesi`=SKILL3, `Max/Min_Yukseklik`, `Max/Min_Roll`, `Max/Min_Tilt` SKILL4-9, flags `Sapik_Cam`, `Sabit_Cam`, `Daire_Hareketi` (`cam.wdl:38-49`); path cameras `takip_uzunluk` etc. (`:51-55`). **CONFIRMED**

## 2. Camera behaviours found in scripts

| Behaviour | Examples | Mechanism | Status |
|---|---|---|---|

| Distance-blended look-at | `start4_camera2` :342, `level4_camera2` :422 | within `Effect_Mesafesi`, lerp height/roll/tilt between Max_/Min_; `vec_to_angle` aims at the player | CONFIRMED |
| Path-follow | `strt5_camera_init` :950 (`ent_path("path_cam")` :964), `level5_camera` :1759 (`path_oda`), `strt3_camera_init` :1125 | follows a WED path after the player spawns | CONFIRMED |
| Zone switch controllers | `Strt4_cam_kontrol` :393 sets `start4_cam_no` (:274); `LVL4_cam_kontrol1` :536 (`level4_cam_no` :419); `level5_camkontrol` :1942 (`lv5_camtip` :1756); `cami_cam_mod` :1503 | separate invisible trigger entities write the mode global read by the camera actions; these are the "trigger regions" | CONFIRMED |

## 3. Cutscene camera (`Video_Cam`)

- Declared `K22.wdl:102 view Video_Cam {}`. **CONFIRMED**
- Swap pattern (e.g. `cinematic.wdl:509-520`): set `Video_Cam.arc`, `size_x/y=screen_size`, `pos=0`, aim with `vec_to_angle`, `camera.visible=off`, `Video_Cam.visible=on`, hide HUD panels; reverse at `:561-562`. **CONFIRMED**
- Also used by puzzles and set pieces: `BUL_Board.wdl:507-530`, `BUL_Kordinat.wdl:312-353`, `BUL_Saat.wdl:395-445`, `Ornek_Yasin.wdl` (ARC 60-80), `boss.wdl:1375-1422`, `dinamik_modeller.wdl:831-1087` (`Video_Cam.clip_near=0` :851), `kotu_koruyucu.wdl:6214-6568`, `seytan.wdl:975-1014`, `cam.wdl:3301`. `cinematic.wdl:7642 kelkafa_camera` orbits then dollies. **CONFIRMED**
- Full-screen video cutscenes are separate: `media_play` with `media_layer`=900 in `LevelYonetim.wdl LevelYukle` (see [Gameplay systems §12](GAMEPLAY_SYSTEMS.md#12-level-management-and-story-flow)). `korku_sahneleri.wdl` uses no camera/VIEW writes. **CONFIRMED**

## 5. Original executable: VIEW layout and projection

## 6. Mirrors and water (portal VIEW)

- Script side: `efect2.wdl:1686 view mirror {}`; `init_mirror` loop (`:1688-1739`) links `camera.portal=mirror`, copies `genius=player`, `fog`, sets `noshadow/portalclip/nocull`, and reflects the pose itself: wall mirror `mirror.arc=-camera.arc`; water `mirror.aspect=-camera.aspect` and z mirrored about `portal_z`. Clears `camera.portal` at `:1736`, `LevelYonetim.wdl:755`, `Kabusdismenu.wdl:139`. **CONFIRMED**
- Binary side (`PORTAL_LAYOUT.txt:71-128`): frame loop `004500b0` (called from `004136b0`) renders the linked target VIEW into the owner viewport (`0044ed80`→`0044ec40` load target pose/ARC/ASPECT; `0044df20` owner viewport). Mirror surfaces are material flag 0x2000 (`00444eb0`), the FIRST processed axis-classifiable surface (|n|>0.9) wins, and the discovered PORTAL_X/Y/Z and PNORMAL are published for the NEXT frame. CPU clipping `0044bcc0` (hardware hook `0042b770` is a bare RET). **CONFIRMED** (static)
- Native: `Engine::tick` publishes `portal_x/y/z` and `pnormal_*` from `Renderer::portal_surface` (`native/render.cpp`) back into the VIEW each tick; `Renderer::portal_surface` selects the first visible eligible 0x2000-material triangle. **CONFIRMED** (code). Exact parity with original surface ordering/one-frame delay: **UNKNOWN**.
- Native GL portal clip-plane fix (every camera uploads its own plane, zero for unclipped views): `CONTRACT.txt:966-971`. **CONFIRMED** (llvmpipe consumer).

## 7. Native implementation

| Symbol | File | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `struct Camera` | `native/render.hpp` | per-view packet: position/angles, `horizontalFov`, `referenceAspect`(4/3), signed `pixelAspect`, `widescreen` flag, clip planes, portal fields |
| `camera_matrix` | `native/render_policy.hpp` | ARC is the horizontal FOV; vertical scale = horizontal / (`widescreen` ? `referenceAspect` : viewport aspect) × \|`pixelAspect`\|; negative ARC flips X, negative pixelAspect flips Y; throws unless 0<\|arc\|<179 |
| `Engine::make_frame` (lambda `camera_for`) | `native/engine.cpp` | builds a `Camera` for every visible VIEW and every hidden VIEW referenced as a portal; sets `widescreen=false`; applies `display_aspect`; a VIEW with `bmap` (render-to-bitmap) throws (unsupported) |
| `Engine::display_aspect` | `native/engine.cpp` | returns `1/(ASPECT*Q)` with `Q=H*320/(W*240)` only in native exclusive fullscreen, else `Q=1`; source comment cites original `0044e260/0044cd00` "screen-mode factor, not a patch-added Hor+ projection" |
| `Engine::configure_display` / `prepare_display` | `native/engine.cpp` | admitted only for the auto-selected original `K22.wdl`; recompute menu/HUD/text geometry and set the MAIN camera `size_x/size_y` to the window; other VIEW rectangles untouched |
| `video_switch` / `video_set` builtins | `Engine::service_builtin` | native display mode re-prepares display instead of switching modes; `--display authored` keeps the original preset table (cap 16384) |
| `vec_to_screen` builtin | `Engine::service_builtin` | uses the same `Camera` construction |
| `Renderer::project`, `Renderer::portal_surface` | `native/render.cpp` | projection/portal helpers shared by all backends |
| GL / Vulkan raster / Vulkan RT | `native/render_gl.cpp`, `render_vulkan*.cpp` | all call `camera_matrix`; winding flips when sign(ARC)≠sign(ASPECT) |

All symbols verified by grep in the current tree. There is no `Hor+`/`hor_plus` symbol in `native/`; the only "Hor+" text is the negating comment in `Engine::display_aspect`. Production paths set `widescreen=false`; the struct default `true` is used only by test fixtures. **CONFIRMED**

### 7.1 Optional first-person camera (`--camera first-person`)

| Item | Native behaviour | Evidence | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Source | patch `cam.wdl` `fps_camera_control`, ported as `Engine::update_first_person` (`native/engine.cpp:847-883`). It runs after scripts and physics each tick, so the scripts' own camera writes are overridden only while it is active | patch script | CONFIRMED |
| Activation | original campaign only (rejected for Bonus and for patched scripts, which have their own F5 camera). Active when Demir (`Aktif_Player` 0) or Ebru (1) is the player, a level is loaded, the player can be controlled (`oyuncu_pasif==0 \|\| koruyucu_pasif==0`), `freeze_mode` is 0, `camera.visible` is on and `Video_Cam` is hidden | patch guard `cam.wdl:80`, `:109` | CONFIRMED |
| Pose | per-state `dist_total`/`yuksek` and tilt clamps for standing, walking, aiming (tilt −5) and running; ARC 70, roll 0; bomb shake added | patch `cam.wdl:111-161` | CONFIRMED |
| Mouse | `player.pan -= 8*mouse_force.x*time`, `camera.tilt += 8*mouse_force.y*time`, exactly as in the patch. `mouse_force` is now the original A6 value (see `GAMEPLAY_SYSTEMS`/`BUG_FIX_PORTING` §5: mickeys·MOUSE_SENSE·10/max(TIME_FRAME raw, 50) plus the previous frame's term, y up, clamped to ±2) | `K22.exe 00422000` ASM | CONFIRMED |
| Buttons | while active, `key_pressed` reports the aim key `GA_Tuslar[4]` when the right mouse button is held and the fire key `GA_Tuslar[5]` when the left is held (patch `GenelAyarlar.wdl:120-121`) | patch script | CONFIRMED |
| Yield | when it switches off, camera fields the scripts did not rewrite go back to their last script values, so the level camera, pause/menu camera or cutscene takes over at once | `check_engine` `patch_option_contracts` | CONFIRMED |
| `validate_view` | omitted. With \|distance\| ≤ 8 the camera stays inside the player's own hull, so the patch's wall traces (from player.z+50, threshold 3) cannot trigger | code comment | HIGH CONFIDENCE |

Live verification (2026-10-09). Current tree, OpenGL on the RX 7900 XTX, 1280×720 windowed, private XDG with the Windows saves imported via `--import-saves`, driven by `--scenario`. Each run was repeated with `--camera original` for comparison. Montages: `reverse/wave2/EngineFixes2/fp-l5-montage.png`, `fp-fire-montage.png`, `fp-chars-montage.png`.

- Demir, Level5 (`load-save 0`). The camera sat 35.2 above the player and within 2 units horizontally (original: about 194 away, 101 above). Walking through `level5_camkontrol` still switched `lv5_camtip` 2→1→0, so the script triggers fire, while the camera stayed first-person (30 above, about 1 unit behind). Player positions after each waypoint and after holding forward into the end wall for 240 frames (482.376, 138.023, −82.969) were **identical** to the original camera run, so collision and movement are unaffected. **CONFIRMED**
- Mouse turn: a 100-pixel step turned `player.pan` by 4.28° on two consecutive frames (the force is clamped to 2, and the original keeps the previous frame's term), then stopped. In original mode the mouse did nothing. **CONFIRMED**
- Firing: with the right and left mouse buttons held, `Key_SilahKaldir` and `Key_Ates` went to 1 and rifle ammo (`S_Kursun_Sayisi[3]`) went 0 → 26 (reload) → 17. The keyboard S/D path in original mode gives the same sequence. In original mode the mouse buttons do not fire. **CONFIRMED**
- Takeover: the pause menu (`freeze_mode` 1, `STM_Acik` 1) brought back the script camera (−179/+74 from the player); closing it restored first-person (−1.8/+35). Inzar (`load-save 15`, Tnel24) has the same camera offsets as the original run (FP inactive). Ebru (`load-save 6`, Ev) is first-person at height 30. Walking into the same obstacle stopped Ebru at the same point (−47, −8, 40) in both modes. **CONFIRMED**
- Not exercised live: a `Video_Cam` cutscene (none starts within 1800 frames of loading any of the 27 saves, and the triggers found need inventory items or long routes), and a level-transition door (the Level5 `LY_Kapi` is beyond the reach of the scenario's greedy steering). The `Video_Cam` yield is covered by the unit test. **UNKNOWN** (live) / **CONFIRMED** (unit).
- Known script interaction, same in the patch: a few scripts read `camera.x/y` (e.g. `cinematic.wdl` `v_asker_ucurtma` `camera.y>333`). With the first-person camera those conditions follow the player's position instead of the level camera's. **HIGH CONFIDENCE**

## 8. Widescreen handling

## 5. Configuration

| File | Original (A) | Patch (B) | Label |
|---|---|---|---|
| `options.k22` | 31 one-byte values: 7 graphics, 2 blood, brightness+100, contrast+80, gamma+100, 3 volumes, 10 keys, 6 joystick buttons (`GenelAyarlar.wdl` `GA_AyarlariKaydet`) | same 31 + byte 32 = `DD_Dil` (0..5) | CONFIRMED (scripts; ISO file 31 bytes, Lutris file 32 bytes with byte 32 = 1) |

`K22.ini`'s comment states an engine limit of 1920×1200; the repo `exe/readme.txt` states the patch raised "1920×1080 to 3840×2160". The actual table in the executable changes 1920×1200 → 3840×2400 ([PATCH_BINARY_DIFF](PATCH_BINARY_DIFF.md) §2). **CONFIRMED.** The readme is inaccurate; the INI comment matches the original value.

Native mapping: `Engine::configure_language` accepts 31/32-byte records and appends/updates byte 32 (`native/engine.cpp:670-686`); `K22.ini` is parsed and normalized by `svc_ini_parse/svc_ini_load/svc_ini_normalize` into the private save root (`native/engine.cpp:1111-1138`). **CONFIRMED.** (Line numbers: working tree of 2026-10-09; other work is editing these files, so search by function name if they drift.)

## 7. Findings that imply native work (status updated 2026-10-09)

Each item: evidence → consequence. When this analysis was written, no `native/` code had been changed. Since then, items 1 (exit frame), 2 (archive order), 3 (ES/RU/PL CLI), 5 (modern-controller load list) and 6 (1024 art tier) have been fixed in native. Item 4 (Hor+) is deliberately not implemented. Current status: [BUG_FIX_PORTING](BUG_FIX_PORTING.md) §5.

1. **Exit-confirmation highlight frame is misplaced in native widescreen.** Original `CikisMenu.wdl:47` uses the absolute bottom `480*GA_ScaleOranlari[y]-DM_AltPay`, valid only when the scale table maps 480 lines to the full screen height (original 4:3 tables). Native feeds `H/720` (`Engine::prepare_display`, `native/engine.cpp:753`), so at 1920×1080 the target rectangle becomes y1 = `CMP_Soru.pos_y` = 1080−48−16−150 = 866 (`Cer_Kenar`=0) > y2 = 480·1.5−16 = 704 and renders as an empty box above the question. Observed at 1920×1080 and 2560×1080: `reverse/community/aspect/exitmenu-2300-xvfb-{1920x1080,2560x1080}.png`. The patch fixes it (`CMP_Soru.pos_y + 480*sy`, `DM_AltPay=0`). Native `prepare_display` re-anchors `Cer_*` only on resize (`native/engine.cpp:816-824`). **HIGH CONFIDENCE** (capture + arithmetic). Suggested fix: in native display mode, set the exit-menu `Cer_hY2` to the screen bottom minus the original 16-pixel margin, as the 4:3 original produces.
2. **Archive member precedence: corrected reading.** The original lookup (`K22.exe` `00420120`) for ordinary assets checks, in order: the in-memory buffer cache (table `00695eb0`), the loose file, the `PATH` directories, and finally the archive table `00665ea8`, where the **first** match wins (`0041fd20` appends members without de-duplicating). An earlier version of this item said "archives first, loose afterwards"; it mistook the memory-cache table for the archive index. `.WDL` scripts are read from archives only when flag `0062119c` is set (it is in both the ISO executable, 0x70aa, and the patch executable, 0xdf02). Native was already loose-first, but made the **last** mounted archive win. It is now first-mounted-wins, and `native/main.cpp` mounts the start-up archive first (K22Widescreen.wrs → K22.wrs → Kaynak.k22). With ISO + v1.8.5 data the only cross-archive duplicates are `PALETTE.RAW` (identical bytes) and `LY_Fade.bmp` (the patch copy wins). **CONFIRMED** (static + `check_assets`); see [BUG_FIX_PORTING](BUG_FIX_PORTING.md) §5.
3. **CLI cannot select the patch's Spanish/Russian/Polish languages.** `--language` accepts only `tr|en|de` (`native/main.cpp:83`, `Engine::configure_language` `native/engine.cpp:673`); indices 3–5 are reachable only through the in-game language menu (byte 32 ≤ 5 accepted, `native/engine.cpp:684`). **CONFIRMED.** Launcher/CLI gap, not an engine defect.
4. **No Hor+ option.** Both the patch and native produce horizontal-locked (Vert-) 3D at wide aspects and stretch 4:3 art non-uniformly ([WIDESCREEN_IMPLEMENTATION](WIDESCREEN_IMPLEMENTATION.md) §2, §4). The renderer already has `Camera::widescreen`/`referenceAspect` (`native/render.hpp:53-55`, `native/render_policy.hpp:35`) but the engine always sets `widescreen=false`. **CONFIRMED.** Enhancement candidate, not parity.
5. **Load menu has no controller navigation in original scripts** (patch adds `JOY_*` to `YukleMenu.wdl`). Relevant to the controller work. **CONFIRMED.**
6. **640-tier art is used at every resolution.** `prepare_display` pins `GA_Cozunurluk` to 0, so original branches such as `Kabusdismenu.wdl` (`if(GA_Cozunurluk<=1) DMP_Arka.BMAP=Diablo_640` → `kan_640.tga`) and `YeniMenu.wdl` (`load640_tr.tga` vs `load_tr.tga`) pick the low-resolution variants, upscaled to the window, although the ISO ships the 1024-tier files (`kan_1024.tga` in `yazi_*.k22`, `gozsag1024_*.tga` in `Kaynak.k22`). The patch instead ships a new 1366-wide background. **HIGH CONFIDENCE** (code); image-quality only. Choosing the higher tier would require matching its separate position/scale tables (`gozsag_pos_*[GA_Cozunurluk]`).

`docs/CONSOLE.md`:

```md
# Save anywhere and developer console

Native additions (`native/console.cpp`); the original game has neither. Both stay inert until a key or command uses them, so
ordinary play, the original save points and all rendering paths are unchanged.

Related: [Gameplay systems §10 Save and load](GAMEPLAY_SYSTEMS.md#10-save-and-load) · [Gameplay testing](GAMEPLAY_TESTING.md)

## Keys

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| F5 | Quicksave. With the community patch scripts (`K22Widescreen.wdl`) F5 belongs to their first-person camera (`cam.wdl` polls `key_f5`), so quicksave is **F8** there. |
| F9 | Quickload the newest save slot. |
| `` ` `` (the key left of 1, `SDL_SCANCODE_GRAVE`) or F10 | Open/close the console. F10 is for layouts where the `` ` `` key is awkward (Turkish Q prints `"` there; the key still works by position). |
| Escape | Close the console. |
| Up / Down | Command history. |
| Tab | Complete a command name. |
| Return | Run the line. |

The original scripts never read F5, F8, F9, F10 or `` ` ``: `K22.wdl:1027-1058` sets `on_f1`…`on_f12` and `on_grave` to `null`, and
no script polls those keys. Movement keys can be rebound in the original Controls menu; binding one of these keys there makes it
do both.

While the console is open the game receives no keyboard, mouse or pad input (time keeps running, so close it before a fight).
After it closes the game sees nothing until every key is released, so the closing key never reaches the scripts (Escape would
otherwise open the in-game menu).

## Save anywhere

A quicksave is an ordinary slot of the game's own save list. It runs the same three script functions as a save point
(`YukleMenu.wdl` `LV_LevelKaydeta`): `SLG_LevelKaydet` (load-menu label), `YD_OyunuKaydet` (`Yeni_Oyun_Deger.wdl`, the 2030-byte
`kayit<N>.sav` payload) and `SLG_Kaydet` (`kysd.sav` index). It also counts in `aktif_kayit_sayisi` like a save point. Slots follow
the game's own ring (`Aktif_SaveNo`, 99 slots, `SLG_MaxKayit`), so a quicksave never overwrites the newest save. The load-menu
label is `Quicksave` (`Hızlı Kayıt` with the Turkish scripts) with the character, date and difficulty like any other entry.

- **Where:** the save root (`${XDG_DATA_HOME:-~/.local/share}/kabus22`, or its `_data/saves/` with the patch scripts), with the
  usual atomic replacement and rotating `backups/`.
- **When:** only while a level is in play and the player has control: `LY_AktifLevelID` set, `level_yuklendi_ok`,
  `player_morph_ok`, no level change (`LY_HedefLevel`, `Yukleme_Yapilsin`), no game over or ending, no menu or puzzle
  (`freeze_mode`, `DM_Acik`), no full-screen video and `oyuncu_pasif`/`koruyucu_pasif` clear. Otherwise the save or load is
  refused with a message ("Cannot save now: a menu is open") and nothing is written.
- **Position:** the original format stores no position; a script save point always respawns at the level's `LV_*_G00`. A
  quicksave adds `position=LEVEL X Y Z PAN` to the slot's `kayit<N>.sav.meta` sidecar (the payload is never extended). Loading
  that slot, by F9, `load` or the original load menu (also after a restart), puts the player back at that spot once the level
  has loaded. Slots without the line (save points, autosaves, imported Windows saves) load exactly as before.
- **What is restored:** everything the original save holds (level, character, weapon, health, ammo, inventory, mana, story
  flags, difficulty) plus the position. Per-level state the original does not save (for example an enemy killed since the
  level was entered) is rebuilt by the level scripts as on any load.

**Quickload** (F9 or `load [SLOT]`) uses the original load: it performs the teardown of the in-game menu's "main menu" choice
(`Smartmenu.wdl:208-243`: stop sounds and video, hide subtitles and letterbox, close the inventory/energy panels,
`LY_AktifLevelID = 0`) and hands the slot to the original `Yukleme_Kontrol` starter exactly as the load menu does
(`YUM_Cursor`/`YUM_Kafa`, `Yukleme_Yapilsin`). The newest slot is the one before `Aktif_SaveNo`, whether it came from a quicksave
or a save point.

Messages ("Game saved (slot 27)", "Game loaded", refusals) appear at the top of the screen for three seconds and in the console.

## Console commands

Command names are case-insensitive. Output also goes to stderr (`kabus22: console] …`).

| Command | Effect |
|---|---|
| `help [COMMAND]` | List all commands, or one command's usage. |
| `save` | Quicksave (as F5). |
| `load [SLOT]` | Quickload the newest slot, or `kayitSLOT.sav` (0-98; the load menu shows slot N as entry N+1). |
| `god` | Toggle invulnerability: after every frame the active character's `ENERJI` (`SKILL1`) and health VAR are refilled (Demir `oyn_yaralanma` 100, Ebru `ebru_yaralanma` 100, Inzar `koru_yaralanma` 200, the new-game values). A hit can still play its flinch animation. |
| `noclip` | Toggle walking through walls and entities: the player gets `PASSABLE`, which the A6 mover treats as "move without collision". Gravity and floor tracing still apply, so it walks, not flies. |
| `give health` | Refill health as above. |
| `give mana` | Inzar's `koruyucu_mana` to 230. |
| `give ammo` | Fill the magazine (`S_Kursun_Sayisi`) of every carried weapon and add three magazines of reserve through the original pickup function `oyunici_kursun_al` (grenades and mines only get the magazine, as in `Silah_Al`). |
| `give weapons` | Demir only: add every weapon 1-7 he does not carry, with a full magazine, as `Silah_Al` does for a new weapon. |
| `give all` | All of the above. |
| `get NAME`, `get NAME[i]`, `get NAME.FIELD` | Print a WDL global, a VAR array element or a field of an object global (`get player.skill1`, `get camera.ambient`). |
| `set NAME VALUE`, `set NAME[i] VALUE`, `set NAME.FIELD VALUE` | Write a number the same way (`set OyunZorluk 1`, `set player.skill1 50`). Strings and objects are read-only. |
| `levels` | List the campaign level IDs and WMB files (`LVSL_Leveller`). |
| `level ID\|WMB`, `map ID\|WMB` | Go to a level through the original door transition (`LY_HedefLevel`, `LevelYonetim.wdl LY_YuklemeTakip`), as a door from the current level would. The level's own entry rules apply: an entry refused by the scripts shows their message, and a level without an entry point for the current level keeps the WMB's own player placement. |
| `pos` | Print the player position, `PAN`, level ID and WMB. |
| `tp X Y Z [PAN]` | Teleport the player. |
| `kill` | Set the player's `ENERJI` to 0: the original death and game over (also turns `god` off). |
| `fps` | Toggle a frame-rate counter (top right). |
| `timescale [FACTOR]` | Print or set `TIME_FACTOR` (0.1-10, 1 = normal). |
| `clear` | Clear the console. |
| `quit` | Exit immediately (no save). |

Cheats change live game state that the next save stores (for example `give weapons`). `god` and `noclip` themselves are not saved.

The console draws with the engine's own UI text path (system monospace font through fontconfig/FreeType), so it looks the same on
OpenGL, Vulkan and Vulkan ray tracing: captures in `reverse/console/` (local evidence).

The Bonus game (`--mode bonus`) has no campaign save system or level table: `save`, `load`, F5/F9 and `levels`/`level` report
that, and `god`/`give`/`kill` (campaign health and weapon variables) are campaign only. `get`/`set`/`timescale`/`fps`/`clear`/
`quit` work there; `noclip`/`pos`/`tp` need a `player` entity.

## Tests

- `tests/scenarios/quicksave1_roundtrip.k22s`: F5 in kizic2, walk away, change ammo, F9: position (±1), pan and ammo restored;
  F5 refused in the inventory menu.
- `tests/scenarios/quicksave2_restart.k22s`: after a restart the quicksave loads from the original load menu at its saved spot;
  `load 10` (a save-point slot) keeps the G00 spawn.
- `tests/scenarios/console_commands.k22s`: every command typed through the real toggle keys, SDL text input and Return, with
  their effects asserted (god undoes damage, ammo/weapons, get/set, timescale, noclip walks through the west wall that stops
  the same walk without it, tp, save, `level kizic`, F9 back across levels, kill, quit).
- `check_engine --input-saves` (CTest `input_saves`): the position line is written only for a quicksave, survives
  format/parse, arms the restore on read, is cleared by a save-point slot and is applied once the level reloads.
- `tests/scenarios/quicksave3_characters.k22s`: the same for Inzar (Tnel24, `koruyucu_pasif`, god keeps `koru_yaralanma` = ENERJI
  = 200) and Ebru (Ev, reached from Inzar by `load 6`).

```

# Engine architecture (native Linux port)

Purpose: module map, frame loop, threading, simulation/renderer split and backend policy of the C++20 reimplementation in `native/` and the GTK tools in `installer/`, as read from current source (2026-10-09).

Related: [REVERSE_ENGINEERING.md](REVERSE_ENGINEERING.md) (index/methodology) · [reverse-engineering/SCRIPT_SYSTEM.md](reverse-engineering/SCRIPT_SYSTEM.md) · [reverse-engineering/FUNCTION_MAP.md](reverse-engineering/FUNCTION_MAP.md) · [ASSET_FORMATS.md](ASSET_FORMATS.md) · [CAMERA_SYSTEM.md](CAMERA_SYSTEM.md) · [GAMEPLAY_SYSTEMS.md](GAMEPLAY_SYSTEMS.md) · [reverse-engineering/ORIGINAL_BEHAVIOR.md](reverse-engineering/ORIGINAL_BEHAVIOR.md)

Confidence labels: **CONFIRMED** (read in source, decompiled code or run evidence), **HIGH CONFIDENCE**, **HYPOTHESIS**, **UNKNOWN**. "Original" means K22.exe (A6 6.31.4 campaign) or the A7 `acknex.dll` used by Bonus mode (`Kabus 22 Mode/K22_mode.wrs`); "native" means this port. Source citations are `file:symbol` (line numbers are as of reading; the files have very long lines and are being edited concurrently).

## 1. Build targets and external dependencies

| Target | Sources | Links | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kabus22_core` (static lib) | `native/engine.cpp wdl.cpp assets.cpp render.cpp render_gl.cpp render_vulkan.cpp render_vulkan_raster.cpp render_vulkan_rt.cpp vulkan_loader.cpp media.cpp physics.cpp` + generated `render_vulkan_spirv.hpp` | SDL2, libepoxy (GL loader), libavformat/avcodec/avutil/swscale/swresample, FreeType, fontconfig, Threads, ODE (static), `dl` | `CMakeLists.txt` — **CONFIRMED** |
| `kabus22` (engine executable) | `native/main.cpp` | `kabus22_core` | `CMakeLists.txt` — **CONFIRMED** |
| Tests | `wdl_regression`, `check_assets`, `check_media` (media.cpp+assets.cpp with `K22_MEDIA_SELF_CHECK`), `check_engine`, `k22-render-check`, `check_physics` | `kabus22_core` | `CMakeLists.txt` (§9) — **CONFIRMED** |
| `kabus22-setup`, `kabus22_setup_core` | `installer/main.cpp`, `setup.cpp`, `media.cpp` | GTK3, libavcodec/avutil/swscale, libarchive, Threads | `installer/CMakeLists.txt` — **CONFIRMED** |
| `kabus22-launcher` | `installer/launcher.cpp`, `launcher_settings.cpp` | GTK3 | `installer/CMakeLists.txt` — **CONFIRMED** |
| `kabus22_layout` (static lib) | `installer/layout.cpp` | — (not yet linked by any executable at time of reading) | `installer/CMakeLists.txt` — **CONFIRMED**; see §10 |

- ODE: pinned upstream 0.16.6 (commit `a5fc0bc2…`), static, single precision, OPCODE trimesh, no GIMPACT/libccd (`cmake/KabusODE.cmake`) — **CONFIRMED**.
- Shaders: `native/shaders/*.{vert,frag,geom,comp}` are compiled by `glslangValidator --target-env vulkan1.2` at build time; `scene.frag` is compiled a second time with `-DK22_RAY_QUERY=1` into `scene.rt.frag.spv`; `native/embed_spirv.py` emits aligned `uint32_t` arrays in namespace `k22::vk22::spirv`. No shader files are read at runtime (`CMakeLists.txt`, `embed_spirv.py`) — **CONFIRMED**. These SPIR-V modules serve Vulkan only; the OpenGL backend carries its own inline GLSL strings (12 `#version` occurrences in `native/render_gl.cpp`) — **CONFIRMED**.
- Vulkan is a build dependency but not a link dependency: `native/vulkan_loader.cpp:load_vulkan` `dlopen`s `libvulkan.so.1` only when the Vulkan backend is constructed, with `VK_NO_PROTOTYPES` and an explicit entry-point table (`vulkan_loader.hpp:K22_VULKAN_FUNCTIONS`); a missing loader or entry point throws — **CONFIRMED**.

## 2. Module map

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  main["native/main.cpp<br/>CLI, options, main loop"]
  wdl["wdl.cpp / wdl.hpp<br/>Runtime: WDL compiler + VM + scheduler"]
  calls["native_calls.inc<br/>original native-call name tables"]
  value["value.hpp<br/>Value, Slot, Object, State"]
  engine["engine.cpp / engine.hpp<br/>Engine: builtins, entities, UI, tick, RenderFrame"]
  box["modern_box.hpp<br/>USE_BOX moving-feature rules"]
  physics["physics.cpp / physics.hpp<br/>Physics: ODE bodies (phent_*/ph_*)"]
  assets["assets.cpp / assets.hpp<br/>WRS archives, WMB, MDL, HMP, images"]
  pefont["pe_font.hpp<br/>engine FONT PCX extraction from PE"]
  media["media.cpp / media.hpp<br/>FFmpeg decode, SDL audio mixer, movies"]
  render["render.cpp / render.hpp<br/>Renderer front-end: SDL window, input, fonts"]
  policy["render_policy.hpp<br/>shared projection/lighting/pass rules"]
  gl["render_gl.cpp<br/>GLBackend (epoxy, GL 3.3 core)"]
  vk["render_vulkan.cpp<br/>VulkanBackend: device, swapchain, capture"]
  vkr["render_vulkan_raster.cpp<br/>raster pipelines"]
  vkrt["render_vulkan_rt.cpp<br/>acceleration structures, GPU pose"]
  loader["vulkan_loader.cpp<br/>dlopen libvulkan.so.1"]
  spirv["shaders/ + embed_spirv.py<br/>build-time SPIR-V header"]
  ode[("ODE 0.16.6")]
  sdl[("SDL2")]
  ff[("FFmpeg")]
  ft[("FreeType / fontconfig")]

  main --> wdl & engine & assets & media & render
  wdl --> value & calls
  engine --> value & assets & render & media & physics & box
  engine -. "Builtin callback" .-> wdl
  physics --> ode
  assets --> pefont
  assets --> media
  media --> ff & sdl
  render --> gl & vk & policy & sdl & ft
  gl --> policy
  vk --> vkr & vkrt & loader
  vkr --> spirv & policy
  vkrt --> spirv
```

Notes: `engine.hpp` includes `assets.hpp`, `render.hpp`, `media.hpp`, `physics.hpp`; `wdl.cpp` includes `native_calls.inc`; `assets.cpp` includes `pe_font.hpp`; `engine.cpp` includes `modern_box.hpp` (grep of `#include`) — **CONFIRMED**. The `assets --> media` edge is `decode_image`/`decode_bitmap_font`, declared in `media.hpp` — **HIGH CONFIDENCE** (declaration location confirmed; call sites not enumerated).

### 2.1 Per-module responsibilities

| Module | Responsibility | Key types / functions (verified by grep) | Depends on |
|---|---|---|---|
| `native/main.cpp` | Parses CLI (`--data`, `--mode campaign\|bonus`, `--script`, `--display native\|authored`, `--resolution`, `--window-mode`, `--language`, `--audio-language`, `--define`, `--renderer opengl\|vulkan`, `--ray-tracing on\|off`, `--headless`, `--frames`, `--capture`); validates combinations; mounts archives (`K22_mode.wrs` for Bonus; `K22.wrs`, `Kaynak.k22`, `K22Widescreen.wrs` if present for campaign); picks entry WDL; sets compiler macros (`defiae_d3d`, `defses_<audio>`, `defdil_<lang>`, Bonus `defmode_d3d`, `defanti_N`); builds Renderer/Media/State/Engine/Runtime; runs the frame loop (§3) | `main`, `private_bonus_locale`, `resolution`, `help` | everything below |
| `native/value.hpp` | WDL value model: 32-bit raw word tagged `Number/Object/Function/NativeText`; numbers are 22.10 fixed point (`from_int` = ×1024); `Slot`, `Ref` (bit-mask refs), `Argument`; `Object` with `Kind {Name,String,Vector,Bmap,Sound,Font,Entity,Panel,Text,View,Material,Window,Particle,NativeText}`; `State` = globals + object store with never-reused handles (`handles` tombstone table, `freePayloads` recycling), leases (`retain_object`/`release_object`), `SemanticProfile {CampaignA6,BonusA7}` | `Value`, `Object`, `State::create/retire/require`, `ProcessContext` | std only |
| `native/wdl.cpp/.hpp` | WDL front end (lexer, preprocessor incl. `DEFINE`/includes, parser to `Expr` trees and per-function `Instruction` lists `Eval/Jump/Branch/Declare/Return/Late`) and VM: `Process` records with `pc`, locals, my/you context, countdown; double-buffered scheduler; `wait`/`waitt`/`sleep`/`proc_late`/`proc_kill` intrinsics; everything else dispatched to the host `Builtin` callback | `Runtime::{load,load_text,start,enqueue,bootstrap,tick,kill_for_entity}`, `Runtime::Impl::{lex,preprocess,parse,initialize,run,tick}`, `native_call_name` | `value.hpp`, `native_calls.inc` |
| `native/native_calls.inc` | Generated sorted tables `commonNativeCalls`, `campaignNativeCalls`, `bonusNativeCalls` from original descriptor rows (campaign `0061c408..0061d7d8`, 317 names; Bonus `101a8200..101a9aa0`, 392 names); used by `native_call_name` to classify call names per profile | — | `reverse/decompiled/runtime/api-descriptors.json` |
| `native/engine.cpp/.hpp` | Host side of every original native call; entity/view/panel/text/material registries and their per-object native data; input → script globals; UI layout and buttons; level loading; legacy and modern collision (`c_move`, `c_trace` in `world_builtin`); particles; file/INI services; Discord-IPC emulation for the community-patch script (`discordSocket` members); builds the per-frame `RenderFrame` | `Engine::{builtin,service_builtin,world_builtin,tick,finish_frame,prepare,load_level,create_entity,remove_entity,collide,make_frame,update_input,update_ui}`; `EntityData`, `Engine::Hit`, `entities` map | value, assets, render, media, physics, modern_box |
| `native/modern_box.hpp` | A6 `00585f60` / A7 `100b2680` USE_BOX moving-feature rules (oriented affine-normalized sphere, not SAT box) | `k22::modern_box::inside` etc. | assets types |
| `native/physics.cpp/.hpp` | ODE world for `ph_*`/`phent_*` calls; fixed-step accumulator; contact collection/reduction; bodies mirrored to entities | `Physics::{builtin,step,load_world,remove_entity,query_body_geometry,near_callback}` | ODE, Engine (friend) |
| `native/assets.cpp/.hpp` | Loose files + WRS archive mounts (`Assets::mount`, `decompress`); decoders for WMB worlds (`World`, BSP/hull/lightmap data), MDL/HMP models (`Model`), images; native lightmap LUTs; engine font from PE | `Assets::{mount,contains,read,model,world,image,image_ptr,purge_*,release_level}` | media (image decode), `pe_font.hpp` |
| `native/pe_font.hpp` | Validates/extracts the embedded engine FONT PCX from a PE (fingerprinted length 17063, SHA-256 `a16eb595…`); shared with installer `setup.cpp:installFont` | `extract_engine_font`, `validate_engine_font`, `pe_font_detail::selfCheck` | std only |
| `native/media.cpp/.hpp` | FFmpeg demux/decode/resample (`swr_*`) of sounds into float PCM; SDL audio device + mixer callback; positional voices; movie decode with `sws_scale` to RGBA; image and bitmap-font decode | `Media::{sound_play,sound_play_at,sound_tune,master_volume,movie_play,movie_frame,update}`, `decode_image`, `decode_bitmap_font` | FFmpeg, SDL2 audio |
| `native/render.cpp/.hpp` | Renderer front-end: SDL video/controller init, window creation per backend, event polling into `Input`, window modes, FreeType/fontconfig font atlases, effect-file identification (SHA-256 check), static helpers `project`, `portal_surface`; forwards draw/capture to one backend | `Renderer::{poll,draw,capture,set_mode,font_atlas,identify_effect,project,portal_surface}`; data types `RenderFrame`, `DrawInstance`, `Camera`, `UICommand`, `Particle`, `RenderLight`, `Input` | SDL2, FreeType, fontconfig, backends |
| `native/render_policy.hpp` | Backend-independent rules shared by GL and Vulkan: camera/projection matrix, culling bounds, planar shadow projection, ambient/material light formulas, presentation limit/interval, UV scaling, tangent derivation | `camera_matrix`, `geometry_eligible`, `presentation_limit`, `presentation_interval`, `material_ambient_light` | render.hpp types |
| `native/render_gl.cpp/.hpp` | OpenGL 3.3 core backend via libepoxy | `GLBackend::{draw,capture,drain,invalidate,purge_model,purge_image}` | epoxy, render_policy |
| `native/render_vulkan.cpp/.hpp` | Vulkan 1.3 instance/device selection, swapchain, two command slots, render targets, sampler/image helpers, readback | `VulkanBackend::{draw,capture}`, `VulkanBackend::State` | vulkan_loader, raster, rt |
| `native/render_vulkan_raster.cpp` | Raster pipelines; when RT enabled binds `scene_rt_frag` and the RT descriptor set and submits per-frame geometry via `rt_scene` | `vk22::raster_create`, `raster_draw` | embedded SPIR-V, policy |
| `native/render_vulkan_rt.cpp` | Acceleration-structure build (`vkCmdBuildAccelerationStructuresKHR`), GPU pose deformation compute (`deform_comp`), texture table | `vk22::rt_create`, `rt_pose`, `rt_scene`, `rt_set` | embedded SPIR-V |
| `native/check_*.cpp`, `wdl_regression.cpp`, `check_modern_box.hpp` | CTest executables: `wdl_semantics`, `asset_boundaries`, `media_boundaries`, `engine_boundaries`, `material_boundaries`, `physics_boundaries` (last three need private fixtures) | — | `kabus22_core` |
| `installer/main.cpp` | `kabus22-setup` GTK/CLI front end (`--iso`, `--setup`, `--install-dir`, `--engine`, `--launcher`, `--extractor`, `--patch`, `--unattended`); worker thread for installation | `interrupted` atomic, worker `std::thread` | setup core |
| `installer/setup.cpp` | Install transaction: path safety, staging/rename, inventory verify, icon/font install, desktop launch | `k22::setup::{install,launch,previewArtwork,defaultPaths,selfCheck}` | media.cpp, pe_font.hpp |

| `installer/launcher.cpp`, `launcher_settings.cpp/.hpp` | `kabus22-launcher`: settings UI for campaign/Bonus options, renderer/display choices; spawns engine with `g_spawn_async_with_pipes` and watches its pipes/exit | `launcher::{Preferences,Settings,Controller,Updates,Capabilities}`, `parseCapabilities`, `validateCampaign`, `decodeBonus` | GTK3 |

## 3. Frame loop

### 3.1 Original reference (K22.exe)

| Fact | Evidence | Label |
|---|---|---|
| Main clock function `00414650` measures elapsed seconds via `00460030` (QPC, fallback timeGetTime), converts to raw ticks with 16 ticks/s and raw quantum 1/1024 tick | `CONTRACT.txt §3` (`:103-114`), `reverse/decompiled/runtime/clock-instructions/K22.exe.00414650.asm.txt:213-237,282-316` | **CONFIRMED** |
| TIME = TIME_FRAME (or 16/FPS_MAX when FPS_LOCK), clamped to [raw 51, 16/max(FPS_MIN,1)], × TIME_FACTOR, then smoothed by TIME_SMOOTH (default 0.5) | `CONTRACT.txt §3` (`:116-123`), `reverse/decompiled/runtime/clock/K22.exe.00414650.c:96-127` | **CONFIRMED** |
| `00414650` sleeps against FPS_MAX before publishing TIME_FRAME, independent of FPS_LOCK | `CONTRACT.txt §38` (`:1526-1534`) | **CONFIRMED** |
| 16 ticks = 1 second corroborated by historical A5 AUM (`waitt(16)`) | `CONTRACT.txt §7` (`:291-293`) | **HIGH CONFIDENCE** (external doc + binary) |
| Scheduler `00412080` double-buffers continuation queues; pass 1 runs functions without the PROC_LATE bit, pass 2 those with it; FREEZE_MODE raw 1024 stops `my!=NULL` records, 2048 stops all | `CONTRACT.txt §3` (`:125-142`), `reverse/decompiled/runtime/trace/K22.exe.00412080.c:35-65` | **CONFIRMED** |
| Continuations are heap records (44 + 12×locals bytes) holding resume statement, my/you, args, local snapshots; no OS threads/fibers | `CONTRACT.txt §2` (`:40-69`), `reverse/decompiled/runtime/trace/K22.exe.00410390.c` | **CONFIRMED** |

Details of script scheduling semantics belong to [reverse-engineering/SCRIPT_SYSTEM.md](reverse-engineering/SCRIPT_SYSTEM.md); addresses are indexed in [reverse-engineering/FUNCTION_MAP.md](reverse-engineering/FUNCTION_MAP.md).

### 3.2 Native loop (`native/main.cpp:main`)

All steps run on the main thread, strictly sequentially — **CONFIRMED** (`native/main.cpp`, `native/engine.cpp:Engine::tick` line 930).

1. **Pacing** (graphical only): period = `1000*1024*1024 / max(1024, FPS_MAX raw)` raw ms; `sleep_until(frameStart+period)`; re-anchor `frameStart` to the actual start (no catch-up debt). Headless runs are unpaced. Mirrors `CONTRACT.txt §38`; verified by `tools/check_frame_pacing.py` per §38 (`:1562-1571`) — **CONFIRMED**. `--graphics fps_limit=N|unlimited` replaces the period (`render_policy::frame_period_raw`, never shorter than the TIME floor raw 51 = 3.11 ms); `FPS_MAX` itself is untouched.
2. **Input**: `Renderer::poll(Input&)` (`native/render.cpp:123`) clears edge sets, measures `dt` with `SDL_GetPerformanceCounter`, drains `SDL_PollEvent` (keyboard, mouse, game controller, two legacy joystick slots). Headless sets `dt = 1/60` — **CONFIRMED**.
3. **`Engine::tick(runtime, input)`** (`native/engine.cpp:930`), in order:
   1. `time_frame = max(1 raw, dt*16)`; `total_ticks`, `total_secs`, `total_frames`, `fps` updated.
   2. `time` computed with FPS_LOCK/FPS_MIN clamp (raw ≥ 51), `time_factor` rounded multiply, `time_smooth` — same arithmetic as `00414650` (§3.1).
   3. `screen_size` from renderer metrics; native display re-layout (`prepare_display`) on size change.
   4. `update_input`: key/mouse/joystick/controller globals and `on_<key>`/`on_anykey`/`on_close` callbacks started via `Runtime::start`.
   5. `make_frame` (pre-script) to resolve portal surfaces into VIEW `portal_*`/`pnormal_*` fields.
   6. A6 only: `update_ui`.
   7. **`Runtime::tick(time, freeze_mode)`** — the WDL scheduler (§3.3).
   8. First tick only: `Engine::prepare` starts (A6) or enqueues (A7) actions of declared entities.
   9. Particles (when `freeze_mode < 1` and `debug_mode < 1`): legacy `my_*` callback particles and modern `function`/`lifespan` particles.
   10. Deferred level load: A6 runs `worldFrameEvents` then a pending `load_level`; A7 runs pending `load_level` then `update_query_actors`.
   11. A6 only: `Physics::step`.
   12. `Media::master_volume(sound_vol, midi_vol)`, `Media::update()` (movie decode), `Media::listener` from `camera`.
   13. `make_frame()` — final `RenderFrame` for this iteration.
   14. A7 only: `update_ui`; pending A7 exit sets `quit`.
4. **Draw**: `Renderer::draw(engine.frame())` → one backend (`native/render.cpp:81`).
5. **`Engine::finish_frame`** (`native/engine.cpp:951`): A7 runs `Physics::step` here, after the draw (comment in `engine.hpp`: "A7: after successful draw") — **CONFIRMED** in source; original A7 ordering evidence is cited in that comment only — **HIGH CONFIDENCE**.
6. Loop ends on `engine.quit` or `--frames N`; `--capture FILE` then calls `Renderer::capture` (§6).

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant M as main.cpp loop
  participant R as Renderer (+GL/Vulkan backend)
  participant E as Engine
  participant W as Runtime (WDL VM)
  participant P as Physics (ODE)
  participant A as Media
  participant T as SDL audio thread
  M->>M: sleep_until(frameStart + period(FPS_MAX))
  M->>R: poll(Input) — SDL events, dt
  M->>E: tick(runtime, input)
  E->>E: time_frame/time/total_* (16 ticks/s, 22.10 raw)
  E->>W: update_input → start(on_* callbacks)
  E->>E: make_frame (portal pre-pass), A6 update_ui
  E->>W: tick(time, freeze_mode) — resume due processes
  W-->>E: Builtin(name,args) calls (engine/world/physics services)
  E->>E: particles, deferred load_level
  E->>P: step (A6 only)
  E->>A: master_volume, update (movie frames), listener
  E->>E: make_frame → RenderFrame (spans into Engine vectors)
  M->>R: draw(engine.frame())
  M->>E: finish_frame (A7: Physics::step)
  T-->>A: callback → mix_voices (concurrent, under SDL device lock)
```

### 3.3 Native WDL scheduler (`native/wdl.cpp:Runtime::Impl::tick`, line 407)

| Behavior | Native implementation | Label |
|---|---|---|
| Coroutine model | Each running script is a `Process` (`pc`, `locals`, `bindings`, `snapshots`, `countdown`, `yielded`); `run()` interprets the function's `Instruction` vector until it yields, returns or is cancelled. No OS threads, fibers or `ucontext` (no `coroutine`/`swapcontext` in `wdl.cpp`) | **CONFIRMED** |
| Start | `Runtime::start` runs immediately to first yield and returns to the caller; `enqueue` defers to the next tick; `bootstrap` enqueues `main` then all `starter` functions | **CONFIRMED** (`wdl.cpp:439-442`) |
| Queues | `queued` is moved to a local `pending` list each tick; newly yielded processes go back into `queued` and are not re-run in the same tick | **CONFIRMED**; matches `CONTRACT.txt §3:136-137` |
| Passes | A6: 2 passes (PROC_LATE bit `schedulerFlags&2` clear, then set). A7: 3 passes (bit1, neither, bit2) per comment "A7 10016710" | **CONFIRMED** in source; A7 address cited from source comment |
| Freeze | `freeze_mode` re-read per record: ≥2048 returns/keeps all; ≥1024 keeps records with `my` | **CONFIRMED** |
| Wait | `wait`: countdown = clamp(n,1024,1048575) − 1024. `waitt`/`sleep` (sleep = n<<4): negative relative countdown vs current `time`. Wakeup: `c ≥ 1024` → `c−1024`, keep; `c ≤ −min(time,1024)` → add time, keep; else resume | **CONFIRMED** (`wdl.cpp:259-264`, `407-424`); matches `CONTRACT.txt §3:73-101` |
| Name dispatch | Call names found in `native_calls.inc` tables for the active profile are native; others resolve to script functions | **CONFIRMED** (`wdl.cpp:native_call_name`) |

## 4. Threading model

| Thread | Work | Synchronization | Evidence / Label |
|---|---|---|---|
| Main thread | CLI, WDL compile and VM, Engine, ODE stepping, asset decode, sound decode to PCM, movie decode (`Media::update`), all GL/Vulkan submission and presentation | none needed (single owner) | `native/main.cpp`, `engine.cpp:Engine::tick` — **CONFIRMED** |
| SDL audio callback thread | `Media::Impl::callback` → `mix_voices` over decoded float voices (`sample_rate = 48000`, stereo F32, 1024-sample buffer) | Main thread wraps voice mutation in `Media::Impl::Lock` = `SDL_LockAudioDevice`/`SDL_UnlockAudioDevice`; with no device (headless) `silent_advance` advances voices by wall time | `native/media.cpp:516-552` — **CONFIRMED** |
| FFmpeg internal codec threads | `native/media.cpp` never sets `thread_count`/`thread_type` before `avcodec_open2`; libavcodec's default `threads` option is 1, so decode should stay on the calling (main) thread | — | **HIGH CONFIDENCE** (absence confirmed by grep; FFmpeg default not re-verified here) |
| ODE | `dInitODE2`/`dAllocateODEDataForThread` on main thread; `dSpaceCollide` + `dWorldStep`/`dWorldQuickStep` called synchronously from `Physics::step` | — | `native/physics.cpp:47-48,386-403` — **CONFIRMED** |
| GPU driver threads | Owned by Mesa/driver; `CONTRACT.txt §38` (`:1553-1556`) observed high driver-thread kernel CPU in one misconfigured RPATH build | — | **CONFIRMED** observation, not engine-owned |
| Installer worker | `kabus22-setup` runs the install in one `std::thread worker_`; progress handed to GTK via `std::mutex mutex_` + dirty flag; cancellation via `std::atomic<bool>` | mutex/atomic | `installer/main.cpp:29,212-214,320-323` — **CONFIRMED** |
| Launcher child | Engine runs as a separate process (`g_spawn_async_with_pipes`, `g_child_watch_add`, `g_io_add_watch`) | GLib main loop | `installer/launcher.cpp:117-133` — **CONFIRMED** |

No `std::thread`, `std::async` or `std::mutex` occurs in `native/` (grep) — **CONFIRMED**.

## 5. Simulation / renderer separation

- **Snapshot by span, not by copy**: `RenderFrame` (`native/render.hpp`) holds `std::span`s over Engine-owned vectors (`draws_`, `shadows_`, `cameras_`, `ui_`, `particles_`, `lights_`, `skinBindings_`, `materials_`) plus scalar globals (fog, sun, gamma ramp `ColorAdjustment`, video frame). `Engine::make_frame` (`engine.cpp:2594`) rebuilds them; `Engine::frame()` returns a const reference — **CONFIRMED**. Validity: until the next `make_frame`; safe only because draw is synchronous on the same thread — **HIGH CONFIDENCE** (inferred from ownership and loop order).
- **Borrowed resources**: `DrawInstance::model`, `Particle::image`, `UICommand::image/font/text` and `RenderFrame::world` are raw pointers/views into `Assets` caches or Engine storage; level changes call `Renderer::release_scene` / `purge_model` / `purge_image` before assets are released (`engine.cpp` calls at lines 1225, 2317, 2360, 2485, 2519; `assets.hpp: release_level` comment "call only after scene/render teardown") — **CONFIRMED**.
- **Callbacks back into simulation during draw**: `RenderFrame::prepareEntityLight` and `cachedEntityShadow` are function pointers with `lightContext = this` (the Engine), set in `make_frame` (`engine.cpp:2605-2606`). The renderer therefore reads/updates Engine entity-light caches mid-draw — **CONFIRMED**. This couples renderer and simulation to one thread; parallel rendering would require copying that state — **HYPOTHESIS** (design consequence, not tested).
- **Renderer → simulation feedback**: `Renderer::metrics()` (screen_size), `Renderer::portal_surface` (VIEW portal fields), `font_atlas` (text metrics) and `Renderer::project` are queried by Engine during tick — **CONFIRMED** (`engine.cpp:Engine::tick`, `make_frame`).
- Rendering rules shared by both APIs live in `render_policy.hpp`; projection/camera specifics are documented in [CAMERA_SYSTEM.md](CAMERA_SYSTEM.md), entity/material/collision semantics in [GAMEPLAY_SYSTEMS.md](GAMEPLAY_SYSTEMS.md), model/world/image formats in [ASSET_FORMATS.md](ASSET_FORMATS.md).

## 6. Backend selection and no-silent-fallback policy

| Rule | Where | Label |
|---|---|---|
| Default backend OpenGL; `--renderer vulkan` selects Vulkan; anything else rejected | `native/main.cpp:main` | **CONFIRMED** |
| `--ray-tracing` only valid with Vulkan; Vulkan defaults to RT on (`rayTracing != "off"`) | `native/main.cpp:main` | **CONFIRMED** |
| `--headless` forbids Vulkan and `--capture` | `native/main.cpp:main` | **CONFIRMED** |
| Exactly one backend is constructed (`gl` or `vk` in `Renderer::Impl`); window created with `SDL_WINDOW_OPENGL` or `SDL_WINDOW_VULKAN` accordingly; GL requests 3.3 core, double buffer, 24-bit depth | `native/render.cpp:Renderer::Impl` constructor (lines ~30-50) | **CONFIRMED** |
| Missing `libvulkan.so.1` or entry point → exception | `native/vulkan_loader.cpp:load_vulkan` | **CONFIRMED** |
| RT requested but device lacks acceleration-structure / deferred-host-ops / ray-query extensions/features → device rejected; no suitable device → throws "No suitable Vulkan device … select --ray-tracing off for raster-only rendering" | `native/render_vulkan.cpp` (device selection, `:162`) | **CONFIRMED** |
| RT mode is hybrid: raster pipelines with `scene.rt.frag` (ray queries in the fragment shader) plus an extra descriptor set; not a ray-tracing pipeline | `native/render_vulkan_raster.cpp:70-71,136` | **CONFIRMED** |
| Errors propagate to `main`'s catch → `kabus22: <message>`, exit 1. No code path switches backend or disables RT on failure | `native/main.cpp:main` | **CONFIRMED** (no fallback branch found) |
| VSync: `RenderOptions::vsync` default true; failed `SDL_GL_SetSwapInterval` warns with SDL error rather than claiming success | `native/render_gl.cpp:332,400`; `CONTRACT.txt §38:1536-1538` | **CONFIRMED** |
| Frames in flight: `render_policy::presentation_limit` = 2 only in fullscreen with nonzero `triple_buffer` raw, else 1; GL enforces with `glFenceSync`/`glClientWaitSync`, Vulkan with two command `Slot`s | `render_policy.hpp`, `render_gl.cpp:383-405`, `render_vulkan.hpp:VulkanBackend::State::slots` | **CONFIRMED** |
| Bonus MSAA samples from `defanti_N`: {0,1,4,9}[N]; campaign default `RenderOptions::samples = 4` | `native/main.cpp`, `render.hpp:RenderOptions` | **CONFIRMED** |

README states the same policy ("Unsupported requested features fail instead of silently switching backends") and lists unsupported routes (nondefault stencil, software world light, VIEW render-to-bitmap) and the RT 1024 material-sampler ceiling (`README.md:9,13`) — **CONFIRMED** as documentation; the ceiling value itself was not re-derived here — **UNKNOWN** in source.

## 7. Capture path

- `Renderer::capture(path)` (`native/render.cpp:82`) forwards to the active backend and writes a binary PPM of the final post-processed frame — **CONFIRMED**.
- GL (`native/render_gl.cpp:GLBackend::capture`, line 1571): rejects capture before a completed frame or after a drawable resize; re-runs the existing final post pass (`post_state`, `post_draw`) into `GL_BACK`, then `glReadPixels` — because post-swap FRONT/BACK contents are not portable. Run evidence: llvmpipe FRONT read black while BACK/resolve held the frame (`CONTRACT.txt §26`, `:955-965`; `reverse/native-gl-material-diagnostic-window.png`) — **CONFIRMED**.
- Vulkan (`native/render_vulkan.cpp:VulkanBackend::capture`, line 462; `State::readback`): same precondition ("Vulkan capture requires a completed frame at the current drawable size") — **CONFIRMED**.
- Capture is only invoked once after the loop (`--capture`), so normal frames carry no readback cost — **CONFIRMED** (`native/main.cpp`).

## 8. Startup sequence

1. `Assets(data, bonus)` → archive mounts (§2.1) — `native/main.cpp`.
2. `Renderer(renderOptions)` unless headless; `Media(assets, !headless)` opens the SDL audio device; `State`, `Engine(assets, renderer, media, state)`.
3. `Runtime(state, builtin)` with the builtin lambda forwarding to `Engine::builtin`; `Runtime::load(entry, source, mount)` parses all includes (resource directives mount further archives).
4. `Engine::initialize_plugins`, `configure_language` (campaign), `configure_display` (original campaign entry only; native display overrides otherwise rejected).
5. Parse metrics/diagnostics printed; `Runtime::bootstrap()` enqueues `main` and starters.
6. Frame loop (§3.2). On exit prints `Native frames=… live_processes=… entities=… save_root=…`.

All **CONFIRMED** from `native/main.cpp`. Builtin dispatch order inside `Engine::builtin` (`engine.cpp:952`): inline cases, then `service_builtin` (`:1158`), `world_builtin` (`:2182`), `Physics::builtin` — **CONFIRMED** (`engine.cpp:1008-1009`).

## Conventions and sources

Confidence labels:

- **CONFIRMED**: direct evidence, such as script text, decompiled code, file bytes, or a recorded native run.
- **HIGH CONFIDENCE**: strong indirect evidence.
- **HYPOTHESIS**: plausible but not checked.
- **UNKNOWN**: the evidence needed to decide is missing.

Script references use `file.wdl:line identifier`. The scripts are proprietary, so this document reproduces only identifiers and short constants.

| Script set | Location | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Campaign (A6 6.31.4), reference copy | `reverse/extracted/original/*.wdl` (179 files) | Extracted from the Lutris-installed `K22.wrs` (804591 bytes, SHA-256 `5bae0b5e…`; `reverse/extracted/recovery.json`). All line numbers below refer to this copy. |
| Campaign, ISO edition (the edition the native port installs) | `reverse/media/iso/scripts/*.wdl` (182 files) | `reverse/media/iso/script-comparison.json`: 173 files are byte-identical to the reference copy and 3 are new. Nine differ: `K22.wdl`, `dil_ceviri_tr/en/de.wdl`, `sub_titles_en.wdl`, `kotu_koruyucu.wdl`, `cinematic.wdl`, `YeniMenu.wdl`, `Yeni_Oyun_Deger.wdl`. Line numbers in those nine files may not match. **CONFIRMED** |
| Community patch (Kabus22Patch `K22Widescreen.wrs`, 190 entries) | `reverse/extracted/patch/` | Most recorded campaign runs used ISO plus this patch (see [Verification](#verification-status-summary)). It is not shipped. |
| Bonus mode (A7, "Demolition Day") | `reverse/media/iso/mode/scripts/K22_mode.wrs/*.wdl` (23 files) | Packed inside `Kabus 22 Mode/K22_mode.wrs` of an installation. |

Native references name the C++ symbol. Line numbers in `native/engine.cpp` and `native/main.cpp` shifted while this document was written, because those files were being edited concurrently. Use the symbol name rather than the line.

## Architecture in one paragraph

All gameplay is written in WDL. The engine contributes only generic services: scheduling, entity movement and collision, tracing and scanning, animation, sound and movie playback, files, input and rendering. The campaign uses the legacy A6 API: `ent_move` driven by `move_mode`, `trace` driven by `trace_mode`, and `scan_entity` with `EVENT_SCAN`. It makes almost no use of the `c_*` API and none of ODE physics. **CONFIRMED**: `c_move` occurs once (`dinamik_modeller.wdl:1062`), and the campaign contains no `ph_*`, `phent_*`, `c_trace` or `game_save` calls (scout grep over the reference copy). The native side resolves these calls through `Engine::builtin`, which dispatches to `Engine::service_builtin` (sound, media, files, video, DLL and keys), `Engine::world_builtin` (create, remove, trace, move, scan, effect and level) and `worldModelBuiltin` (animation, paths and vertices), all in `native/engine.cpp`. The callable name set is the recovered A6/A7 descriptor table in `native/native_calls.inc`, consumed by `native_call_name` in `native/wdl.cpp`. **CONFIRMED** (grep).

## 1. Playable characters

Three characters share one `player` pointer. The global `Aktif_Player` selects which player action runs. **CONFIRMED**

| Item | Demir | Ebru | Inzar (internal name "Koruyucu") |
|---|---|---|---|
| Selector constant | `oyuncu2.wdl:14 Player_Demir`=0 | `:15 Player_Ebru`=1 | `:16 Player_Koruyucu`=2 |
| Player action | `oyuncu2.wdl:687 Oyuncu_Demir` | `oyuncu2_ebru.wdl:145 Oyuncu_Ebru` | `koruyucu.wdl:561 oyuncu_koruyucu` |

- Each player action starts with an `Aktif_Player==` guard (`oyuncu2.wdl:690`, `oyuncu2_ebru.wdl:148`, `koruyucu.wdl:565`). **CONFIRMED**
- **Switching characters is scripted, not a player choice.** Cinematics set `Aktif_Player` together with a target level `LY_HedefLevel`. Examples: `cinematic.wdl:3442` (→Ebru), `:3622` (→Demir), `:11084`/`:13554` (→Inzar), `seytan.wdl:1016`, `kotu_koruyucu.wdl:6327`. **CONFIRMED** in the reference copy. `cinematic.wdl` and `kotu_koruyucu.wdl` differ in the ISO edition, so those line numbers may differ there.
- Movement uses `ent_move(player_distance,nullvector)` with `move_mode` = IGNORE_PASSABLE + ACTIVATE_TRIGGER + USE_BOX + GLIDE (`oyuncu2.wdl:826-827`, `oyuncu2_ebru.wdl:273-274`). Ground probing and melee use `trace`; door search uses `scan_entity` (`PL_KapiTara` `oyuncu2.wdl:556`); footstep surface selection uses `trace` with `scan_texture`/`tex_flag1` (`adimsesi_turu` :356). **CONFIRMED**

**Native services:** `ent_move`/`c_move` and `trace`/`c_trace` in `Engine::world_builtin`, built on the shared legacy BSP/hull kernel. CONTRACT §48 records the source-qualified A6 query cutover (`reverse/decompiled/runtime/CONTRACT.txt:1979-2006`). Animation is handled by `worldModelBuiltin`, which supports vertex and sprite animation; skeletal animation throws (scout reading of `engine.cpp`, **HIGH CONFIDENCE**).

**Verification:**
- Demir **CONFIRMED** on the native port. CONTRACT second-numbered §42 (`CONTRACT.txt:2305-2324`) records a fresh New Game/Normal reaching `start4.wmb` with `PLAYER` model `demir_2007.mdl` running `oyuncu_demir`. Held A+Up movement, wall glide and two-plane corner behaviour were observed.
- Ebru and Inzar as playable characters: **CONFIRMED loading** from the user's original Windows saves through the original load menu (Ebru Ev/Sahil/Kanalizasyon/Tüneller, Inzar Tnel24/Tnel66/Tnel13/kotukoru_d). Ebru saves crashed until the A6 `vec_for_vertex` index clamp was fixed. Sustained play as Ebru or Inzar is not established. See [Gameplay testing](GAMEPLAY_TESTING.md).

Every enemy uses the same perception and steering pattern (**CONFIRMED**; examples from `klasik_yara.wdl`):

- Range gating with `vec_dist(my.x,player.x)` (:294, :417).
- Facing with `vec_to_angle` (:304).
- Movement with `ent_move` and `move_mode` = IGNORE_PASSABLE + IGNORE_PUSH + ACTIVATE_TRIGGER + GLIDE (:645-646).
- Melee hits by `trace` between two arm vertices (:1085).
- Ground snap by `trace` with USE_BOX (:231).

Other AI support:

- `yoldata.wdl` starter `DatYukle` (:22) loads `yoldata.DAT` into `YapayYol[117960]`, with per-level `LevelKutu`/`Atlama` offsets used by `YapayKutu` (`klasik_yara.wdl:1562`). **HYPOTHESIS**: this is a precomputed navigation box graph.
- `iletisim.wdl` (`yara_koordinat`, `yara_mesafeler`) spaces enemies apart; it is not dialogue. **HYPOTHESIS**, based on identifiers and code bodies.
- Spawning is done by `klasik_generate.wdl:300 yaratik_generate`.

**Native services:** `vec_dist`, `vec_to_angle`, `ent_move`, `trace`, `scan_entity` and `ent_path`/`ent_waypoint`/`ent_nextpoint`, in `Engine::service_builtin`, `Engine::world_builtin` and `worldModelBuiltin`.

**Verification:**
- Enemy entities were decoded and alive in the native port: Start4 had 184 decoded entities (`CONTRACT.txt:874-879`, `:907-910`). **CONFIRMED**
- Combat AI: **EXERCISED** at three locations: Kriz `atilgan_ai` divers (approach, damage, game over), Tnel10 `duma_yaratik` (activation through `vec_to_screen`, run-in, strikes, reaction, death, removal) and the Lain boss. Handheld firearms do not hurt `atilgan_ai` (only the AA gun does), and `atilgan_ai` respawns until `atilgan_sayisi` reaches 15 (`atilgan_yara.wdl:620-633`), so its despawn is not exercised.
- Engine fixes found by these runs (all A6, with regressions): `vec_to_screen` gated on the view VISIBLE flag, read with fixed-point scaling from raw flag bits, so it always failed on `camera`, so every `duma_yaratik` stayed frozen (K22.exe `00404020`→`0044ee20` tests only depth and view rectangle); the MDL resource box was the union of all animation frames instead of frame 0 (`00457d10`/`00457d70`/`00458500 +0x38`), which made `klasik_yercekimi` float dumas 69 quants above the floor; legacy `trace` always rewrites YOU (`004546f0`); `vec_*` on `my.skillN` addresses skillN..N+2 (`0043e390`); IF/WHILE conditions are the function result accumulator (`00410a80`).

## 7. Sound and music

- `Ses_Sistemi.wdl:1 sterio_ses3d` computes volume and pan from distance and angle in script, then calls `snd_play(sound, vol*Vol_Efekt, pan)`.
- `music_script.wdl`: starters `fonmuzikkodu_strtr` :42 and `fon_muzik_strtr` :127, using `snd_loop` with `snd_tune` fades.
- `SesMenu.wdl SM_Kernel` :130 adjusts `GA_Efekt`/`GA_Muzik` in steps of 5.
- Defaults: `GA_Efekt`=65, `GA_Muzik`=90, `GA_Dialog`=100 (`GenelAyarlar.wdl:27-29`).
- Engine calls used: `snd_play`, `snd_loop`, `snd_stop`, `snd_playing`, `snd_tune`, `snd_stopall`, `media_play`, `media_loop`, `media_playing`, `media_stop`. The scripts use no `ent_playsound`.

**CONFIRMED** for all of the above.

**Native services:**
- `Engine::service_builtin` forwards to `Media::sound_play`, `sound_playing`, `sound_stop`, `sound_stop_all`, `sound_tune`, `movie_play`, `movie_status` and `movie_stop` in `native/media.cpp` (FFmpeg decoding, SDL output).
- RIFF/WAVE files with format tag `0x674f` that contain Ogg/Vorbis are unwrapped by `media_payload` (`native/media.cpp`). CONTRACT §33-34 (`CONTRACT.txt:1358-1393`).

**Verification:**
- **CONFIRMED**: the wrapped-Vorbis Level4 door sound (`cinematic.wdl:848`, `v_tacikos_kapi`) blocked the campaign, and the replay got past it after the fix (`CONTRACT.txt:1480`).
- **CONFIRMED**: nonzero audio output from the game's own PipeWire stream (peak 32332, RMS 9587). The "no sound" user report was a persisted 4% per-application stream volume, not an engine defect (`CONTRACT.txt:2326-2331`).
- Parity with the original Windows mixer: **UNKNOWN**.

The video is clocked from the movie's audio voice (`Media::update`); decoded frames 283 and 963 arrived at 11.285 s and 38.49 s (expected 11.28 and 38.48), the movie ended at 40.279 s, and `VST_AltText` followed the `sub_cam_fx` frame windows (`world_cam1_padlock`).

## 10. Save and load

The original scripts never call `game_save`/`game_load`. Saves are written by hand through the `file_*` API. **CONFIRMED**

| Step | Identifiers |
|---|---|
| Slot index file `kysd.sav` | `YukleMenu.wdl:19 SLG_Yukle`, `:119 SLG_Kaydet`, `SLG_MaxKayit`=99 :6, label builder `SLG_LevelKaydet` :87 |
| Slot data `kayit<N>.sav` | `Yeni_Oyun_Deger.wdl:1554 YD_OyunuKaydet` (sequence of `file_asc_write` calls starting with `save_versiyon`=100, then `LY_AktifLevelID`, `Aktif_Player`, `Aktif_Silah`, …); loaded by `:873 YD_OyunuYukle` |
| Save points | action `save_tga` (`YukleMenu.wdl:362`, manual) and action `otosave_fish` (`:417`, automatic), both going through `LV_LevelKaydeta` :345 |
| Load at startup | starter `Yukleme_Kontrol` :318 → `YD_OyunuYukle` → `LY_HedefLevel` |

**Native:**
- `file_open_read`/`file_open_write`, `file_asc_*`, `file_var_*` and `file_str_*` are implemented in `Engine::service_builtin`. Paths are confined to `saveRoot`, which is `$XDG_DATA_HOME/kabus22` or `~/.local/share/kabus22` (set in the `Engine::Engine` constructor).
- The `game_save`/`game_load` names are listed in `native_calls.inc`, but `engine.cpp` contains no implementation. The original scripts do not use them. **CONFIRMED** (grep)
- Native addition, not in the original: quicksave/quickload (F5/F9) and the developer console ([CONSOLE.md](CONSOLE.md)). A quicksave runs the original `SLG_LevelKaydet`/`YD_OyunuKaydet`/`SLG_Kaydet` at any gameplay moment and adds the player position to the slot's `.meta` sidecar; a quickload goes through `Yukleme_Kontrol`. Save-point and imported slots carry no position and still respawn at `LV_*_G00`. **EXERCISED** for all three characters (`quicksave1_roundtrip`, `quicksave2_restart`, `quicksave3_characters`, `console_commands`).

**Verification:**
- The original save menu, writer and reader ran through the SourceAPI consumer in the native port: `campaign-save-load-result.json`, exit 0 (`CONTRACT.txt:1682-1685`). **CONFIRMED**
- A real saved checkpoint through reload: **CONFIRMED** on the native port (`world_save1_point`…`world_save4_restart`, [Gameplay testing](GAMEPLAY_TESTING.md)).
  - kizic2 `save_tga`, reached by walking after a level transition, wrote `kayit27.sav`. That file is byte-identical to the original `kayit10.sav` apart from the save counter.
  - After a restart, it reloaded through `YukleMenu` with the same level, weapon, HP and ammo. `kysd.sav` and `ftz.k22` persisted across restarts.
  - Two engine fixes were needed: A6 placed-entity Z lift (`004315d0`), without which every save icon sat ~130 quants under its spot, and `SYS_*` date update (`00414650`).
  - Save points exist in Level5, cam1, fiinis, kizic2, tnel66 and masso_lg (save inventory). `otosave_fish` is **EXERCISED**: after the Lain fight, Buyukes' `otosave_fish` (skill1 14) wrote `kayit27.sav` once `buyukes_koruses` granted `OSN_OtoSave_izin`, and that slot reloads (`inzar_lain_boss`, `world_otosave_reload`). Every original save already has its own level's `OSN_OtoSave_dizi` entry set, so an autosave only fires on reaching a later autosave level.
  - The save file does not store XYZ; a load uses `LV_*_G00` (`CONTRACT.txt:1880-1882`).
