## 2. ISO `K22.exe` → patch `K22.exe`

Section table: `.text` 1 896 448, `.rdata` 307 200, `.data` 135 168 raw bytes in both; `.rsrc` grows 4 096 → 196 608. PE checksum `0` → `0x26d99b`. `.rdata` identical. **CONFIRMED.**

### 2.1 Code (`.text`, 6 bytes at 3 sites)

| VA | Original | Patch | Context (original disassembly) | Meaning | Label |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `0x4139bb` | `0f 8c 23 0c 00 00` `jl 0x4145e4` | `eb 04 …` `jmp 0x4139c1` | after `call 0x41fc00` (start-up block / executable self-check, `reverse/decompiled/runtime/constants/K22.exe.0041fc00.c`) in start-up `00413990` | a negative result no longer aborts start-up | CONFIRMED (bytes); "self-check bypass" HIGH CONFIDENCE |
| `0x413a7e` | `e8 0d f4 00 00` `call 0x422e90` | `eb 03 …` `jmp 0x413a83` | `push 0x6c7688` (start-up script/archive base name, `K22.exe.00413990.c:37,60`) then `test eax,eax; jl abort` | call skipped; `eax` keeps the non-zero name byte, so the start-up archive check always passes | CONFIRMED (bytes); purpose HIGH CONFIDENCE |
| `0x42027e` | `e8 6d 2c 00 00` `call 0x422ef0` | `eb 03 …` `jmp 0x420283` | in file opener `00420120`, `cmp ebp,2` branch for protected `.WDL` sources whose error text is `"- script modified"` (`K22.exe.00420120.c:57-60`) | modified script files are accepted ("source code protection removed", repo `exe/readme.txt`) | CONFIRMED (bytes, string); purpose HIGH CONFIDENCE |

The repo `exe/K22*.exe` builds contain the last two sites but keep the original `jl` at `0x4139bb`. **CONFIRMED.**

### 2.2 Data (`.data`, 19 bytes)

| VA | Original | Patch | Meaning | Label |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `0x621190` (4 B) | `0x0deee922` | `0x0deee8b0` | start-up block field read by `0041fc00`; changes together with the embedded name | UNKNOWN (integrity value, HYPOTHESIS: checksum) |
| `0x62119c` (2 B) | `0x70aa` | `0xdf02` | non-zero selects archive-resource mode in `00420120` (`DAT_0062119c`) | HIGH CONFIDENCE (role); value semantics UNKNOWN |
| `0x621243` (10 B) | `"K22"` + NUL padding | `"K22Widescreen"` | start-up base name: engine opens `K22Widescreen.wrs` / `K22Widescreen.wdl` instead of `K22.*` | CONFIRMED |
| `0x621264` (1 B) | `0xbe` | `0x85` | start-up block field | UNKNOWN |
| `0x627ab8` (8 B: two int32) | `1920, 1200` (`0x780,0x4b0`) | `3840, 2400` (`0xf00,0x960`) | largest entry of the mode table read by `video_set`/`video_switch` (preceding entries `1400×1050`, `1600×1200` unchanged) | CONFIRMED (bytes; cap role per `CONTRACT.txt:2150-2151`) |

The repo `exe/K22.exe` has the same `0x621190/0x62119c/0x621264/0x627ab8` values as the patch but keeps the name `"K22"`; this explains why only the patch build needs the `0x4139bb` bypass (its name bytes no longer match the stored integrity value). **HIGH CONFIDENCE.**

### 2.3 Resources (`.rsrc`)

Original: resource section present but no resource entries. Patch: 6 `RT_ICON` (1 128 … 96 355 bytes) + `RT_GROUP_ICON "KABUS22"`. No manifest, no version resource. **CONFIRMED.**

## 3. Other variants

# Progress

Status of the native Linux port against the master objective. Each milestone lists confirmed discoveries, source changes, tests, build results, blockers and the next task. Evidence paths under `reverse/` are private (not published); docs cite them for reproducibility on the maintainer's machine.

Approach (CONFIRMED, unchanged since v0.1.0): `native/` reimplements the Acknex A6.31 (campaign) / A7.05 (Bonus) runtime and executes the **original WDL scripts and assets** from the user's own media. `docs/RAYTRACING.md`:

```md
# Ray tracing (Vulkan `vulkan-rt`)

## What is implemented

- **Backend**: Vulkan 1.3 with `VK_KHR_acceleration_structure`, `VK_KHR_ray_query`,
  `VK_KHR_deferred_host_operations`, buffer device addresses and descriptor indexing. It is selected
  by `--renderer vulkan` (ray tracing defaults on), `--graphics backend=vulkan-rt` or `--preset ultra`.
  Ray queries are issued from the ordinary raster fragment shader (`scene.frag` built with
  `K22_RAY_QUERY=1`). There is no ray-tracing pipeline and no SBT.
- **Geometry** (`native/render_vulkan_rt.cpp`): each displayed world/model pose is written by the
  `deform.comp` compute pass into a per-frame vertex buffer: position, normal, UV, lightmap UV and
  tangent, 13 floats per vertex. Animated frames, interpolation and mutable mesh overrides are
  resolved on the GPU. One BLAS is built per pose. The TLAS is rebuilt per camera from the admitted
  opaque and translucent draws in source order, with per-instance clip planes. The instance custom
  index is capped at 24 bits and enforced with an error.
- **Materials in hits**: one `RtMaterial` record per batch, carrying UV transform, tint, alpha,
  sprite frames, flags (overlay/flare/alpha test/additive/blend/explicit material/unlit/effect) and
  the prepared script-material terms. Hit textures come from a bindless `sampler2D[1024]` array,
  which is the texture-binding ceiling: a request on a device below 1024 samplers fails explicitly.
  With texture packs, hits sample the pack albedo because they share the raster texture cache.
- **Effects**:
  - *Visibility* (`shadows=rt` only): sun and dynamic-light shadow rays (`rtVisibility`) scale the
    native per-vertex dynamic lighting by the per-channel visible/unshadowed ratio. The sun is used only
    on non-lightmapped surfaces. Models with the original SHADOW flag also shadow lightmapped level geometry
    from the baked WMB lights, native point/spot lights and the sun ([actor shadows](#actor-shadows)), which replaces
    their fixed-direction A6 planar shadow (never drawn under `shadows=rt`); models are shadowed by themselves and other
    models and get ray-traced ambient occlusion ([model shadows and AO](#model-shadows-and-ambient-occlusion)). Without `shadows=rt` the ray-traced backend does not occlude any light:
    A6 point/spot lights and the sun are D3D9 fixed-function hardware lights (`D3DLIGHT` slots enabled
    with `LightEnable`, the sun as `D3DLIGHT` type 3; `reverse/decompiled/runtime/graphics-settings-source/a6-worldlight-contract.txt`),
    which never cast shadows; static shadows exist only in the baked lightmaps. Default RT lighting is
    therefore identical to raster.
  - *Reflections*: on mirror materials without an attached portal view, `rtReflection` traces one
    reflection ray, shades the hit with the legacy material model and mixes it by the original
    reflection weight.
- **PBR on RT** (`pbr=1`, preset `ultra`): the PBR path (`docs/GRAPHICS_ROADMAP.md`) applies the same
  visibility as the diffuse term to its sun and dynamic-light specular (RT signal mask, inline ray, or
  shadow maps); with shadows off, specular is unshadowed like the diffuse term.
- **No silent fallback**: an explicit RT request on unsupported hardware fails with the missing
  feature list. Only preset-chosen RT degrades to raster, and it prints a notice.

## Verified on this host

RX 7900 XTX with RADV, Mesa 26.2.4:

- `--list-capabilities` reports `vulkan-rt` available ("KHR ray query").
- The `k22-render-check FX --vulkan-rt` consumer suite passes. It checks that `shadows=rt` occludes the
  sun with an actor, that an actor's shadow on a lightmapped floor follows a baked light, that the planar shadow is never
  drawn (with no light in range the actor shadow falls toward the planar shadow's light instead), that models shadow
  themselves and receive ambient occlusion, and that the default RT path lights exactly like Vulkan raster.
- Default RT captures are byte-identical to Vulkan raster on the 2560x1377 Start4 test view and on
  imported original saves 1, 8 and 21 (no reflective surface in view). Before this fix the default RT
  Start4 test view had mean 4.36 against 13.66 in raster: the script light (60,40,20) sits inside a solid
  `blo02` pillar brush (faces at x=37/63, y=47, closed by the y=32 brush below), so every visibility ray
  toward the light center crossed the pillar shell. Neither the light's own model (hidden: still 4.36) nor
  ray origin bias (normal offset: unchanged) caused it.
- `--preset ultra` ran 600 campaign frames and a 120-frame Start4 view with a test pack.
- 60-frame Start4 test-view runs under `VK_LAYER_KHRONOS_validation` (VVL 1.4.363, loaded through
  `VK_ADD_LAYER_PATH`): Vulkan raster, RT, `shadows=shadowmap`, `--preset enhanced`, `--preset ultra`,
  `shadows=rt denoise=1`, `gi=1 denoise=1`, `reflections=rough denoise=1`, raster with every raster effect
  plus PBR, and the bathroom-mirror view with `reflections=rough` + PBR + a roughness pack. All report zero
  validation errors. Shadow-map configurations report one warning class,
  `Undefined-Value-ShaderOutputNotConsumed-DynamicRendering` (the depth-only caster pass reuses the scene
  fragment shader, whose color write has no attachment); it predates this change. As a positive control,
  enabling best practices reports warnings with the same setup.

## Wave-2 ray-traced effects (`shadows=rt`, `gi=1`, `reflections=rough`, `denoise=1`)

Screen-space signals of the primary view (`native/render_vulkan_raster.cpp` `rt_signals`,
`native/shaders/rt_signals.comp`, `rt_filter.comp`):

1. **G-buffer prepass**: world + opaque models with the forward pass's own (jittered) view-projection into
   a D32 depth + RGBA16F (octahedral normal, pack roughness, lighting flags) target. Forward fragments
   whose depth equals the prepass depth use the signals; others (translucent, MSAA edge samples) keep the
   original inline path.
2. **Signals** (compute + ray query, 1 sample/pixel/frame):
   - *Soft shadows*: one ray per contributing light to a random point on a sphere of radius
     clamp(0.03 range, 2, 12) units; sun inside a 0.02 rad cone; output is the shadowed/unshadowed ratio of
     the dynamic-light sum and the sun visibility. *Ambient occlusion*: one 40-unit cosine ray. On lightmapped
     pixels it sees models only (TLAS instance mask 2; level geometry is mask 1), so actors darken baked lightmaps
     (floor 0.3, as it scales the whole lightmap); on model and vertex-lit pixels it sees all geometry, the model itself
     included, and scales their ambient term ([model shadows and AO](#model-shadows-and-ambient-occlusion)). The TLAS
     already contains every visible non-view-space model; animated poses are re-deformed on the GPU and
     their BLAS updated (`rt_pose`/`rt_scene` version check) every frame. Without `denoise=1` the shadow
     signal is visibly 1-sample noisy (`ultra` enables the denoiser).
   - *Actor shadows* (lightmapped pixels, mask alpha): see [Actor shadows](#actor-shadows).
   - *Occluders* (soft shadows and the inline `shadows=rt` rays): judged as seen from the light, like the
     back-face-culled shadow-map caster pass. A one-sided face blocks only when its front faces the light,
     so a light inside a closed brush or emitter model is not self-occluded. Geometry within 16 units of a
     point/spot light (`rtLightClearance`, the shadow cube near plane) does not occlude it, and additive
     (glow) surfaces add light without blocking it. Ambient-occlusion rays are alpha-tested like the raster
     pass.
   - *GI*: one cosine ray (1500 units); the hit is lit from its lightmap (`RtMaterial.lightState.z`,
     only when `gi=1`) or native ambient plus unshadowed dynamic lights, linearized; misses return 0. The
     forward shader adds `albedo x irradiance` in linear space. Chosen over a DDGI probe grid because the
     BSP levels are thin-walled (probe leaking) and the lightmaps already hold the static term; one
     screen-space bounce gives dynamic-light and model color bleeding without a probe placement step.
     Measured (2560x1377, 120 frames): Start4 test view mean 13.66 -> 13.68, save 8 21.97 -> 22.04, save 21
     17.44 -> 17.45. The original levels are dark, so the bounce is small and colour bleeding is not visibly
     perceptible on these views; the signal itself is present (checked by displaying it directly).
   - *Rough reflections*: GGX half-vector sample with the pack roughness (0 = mirror), layered
     transparency as `rtReflection`, on the original reflective surfaces only, including unlit ones (the
     camtuvalet bathroom mirror, type 3, received no reflection before this fix). Checked on that mirror:
     roughness 0 matches the default inline reflection, roughness 0.35 (test pack, `pbr=1`) is noisy and
     blurred, and `denoise=1` smooths it.
   - *Shadow-terminator origin* (lit, non-lightmapped pixels, with or without `smooth_normals`): hit shading already
     interpolated vertex normals with the hit barycentrics (`hitRadiance`, explicit-material hits); with
     `smooth_normals=1` or `tessellation=1` (`docs/GRAPHICS_ROADMAP.md` Geometry upgrades) the pose buffers carry the
     smoothed normals. Shading a low-poly model with vertex normals while tracing against its flat triangles lets shadow
     and occlusion rays leaving a facet near the terminator re-enter the neighbouring facets (the shadow-terminator
     problem: dark triangle-shaped blocks, acne in self-shadow). `rt_signals.comp` therefore re-finds the base triangle
     under the pixel with a camera ray (within `max(4 bias, 0.4% distance)` of the G-buffer depth) and starts the rays
     from the surface its vertex normals describe (Hanika 2021: barycentric blend of the hit projected outward onto each
     vertex tangent plane), offset along the camera-facing geometric normal. With smoothing the G-buffer orients the
     stored normal by the camera-facing facet normal (from `worldPosition` derivatives) instead of flipping any normal
     facing away from the camera, which inverted smooth normals at model silhouettes. Tessellated PN surfaces are traced
     as their base mesh (the BLAS is not tessellated): a tessellated pixel whose base triangle lies within the camera-ray
     window starts its rays from that triangle's lifted surface; where the PN bulge exceeds the window (large patches
     close to the camera) the pixel keeps the previous origin, offset along its shading normal. Lightmapped (world)
     pixels keep the previous origin.
3. **Denoise** (`denoise=1`): temporal accumulation (reprojection with the previous unjittered
   view-projection, or with the per-pixel motion vector where a moving/animated entity is visible; rejected on
   >5% view-depth change or normal cosine < 0.9; history clipped to the current 3x3 raw signal mean +- 2 sigma
   so a shadow or bounce does not linger where its caster left; alpha max(1/(n+1), 0.15 shadows/reflections,
   0.06 GI)), then three a-trous B3 iterations (strides 1/2/4) with depth/normal edge stopping; mirror-smooth
   reflections and the lightmapped actor-shadow alpha are not blurred (model-pixel alpha is, among model pixels).
4. **Motion vectors** (`taa=1`, or `denoise=1` with signals): after the G-buffer, entities whose transform
   (keyed by entity id, previous frame only) or GPU-deformed pose (the same actor's pose in the other frame
   slot, `rt_previous_pose`) changed are drawn again (scene pass 3) into an RGBA16F target: previous-minus-current
   UV, view depth, previous view depth. The world and unmoved entities keep camera reprojection, so nothing is
   drawn when nothing moves. TAA and the denoiser use it; with both off the pass and its images do not exist.
   `k22-render-check --vulkan|--vulkan-rt` renders a moving, vertex-animated actor under a following camera
   with the full temporal stack and compares the frame reached through motion with the same frame held still:
   visibly different pixels (any channel > 24) of 57600 went from 6043 (RT) / 2278 (raster) with camera-only
   reprojection to 819 / 790 (remaining: TAA softening of moving edges).

Wall-clock per-frame cost, RX 7900 XTX (RADV, Mesa 26.2.4), Start4 test view 2560x1377 (window-manager
clamped from 2560x1440), MSAA 4, present mode immediate, (t(600 frames) - t(100 frames)) / 500, best of two.
These include CPU time. Run-to-run noise is about +-0.5 ms. Shadow-map casters are recorded once per frame and
replayed by all seven depth passes: Vulkan pushes each face's view-projection as a push constant, and OpenGL
groups the world's WMB batches (about 3000 on Start4) into one multi-draw per alpha-rejection state.

All cheap configurations measure about 4.2 ms in this build, so costs below about 0.3 ms are not resolved.
The previous table had `shadows=shadowmap` at 22.83 ms (Vulkan) and `--preset ultra` at 30.32 ms.

| Configuration | ms/frame |
| --- | --- |
| OpenGL default | 4.24 |
| + `shadows=shadowmap` | 4.21 |
| Vulkan raster default | 4.24 |
| + `shadows=shadowmap` | 4.86 |
| + `ssao=1` | 4.28 |
| + `volumetric_fog=1` | 4.49 |
| + `bloom=1` | 4.54 |
| + `taa=1` | 4.21 |
| + `fxaa=1` | 4.22 |
| `--preset enhanced` | 5.85 |
| Vulkan RT default | 4.15 |
| + `shadows=rt` | 8.06 |
| + `shadows=rt denoise=1` | 7.57 |
| + `gi=1 denoise=1` (full resolution) | 7.83 |
| + `reflections=rough denoise=1` | 5.88 |
| `--preset ultra` (no shadow maps: fog is unshadowed under `shadows=rt`) | 15.08 |

`texture_upscale=1` and `sharpen=1` (see `GRAPHICS_ROADMAP.md`) work the same on `vulkan-rt`: ray-query
material hits sample the same upscaled image views as raster, and CAS runs after TAA in the shared
composite. On Demir level5 at 1920x1080 with the user-style RT setup (PBR, `shadows=rt`, GI, rough
reflections, denoise, bloom, SSAO, FXAA, TAA, fog) the mean luma gradient of the frame rises 1.75 -> 2.19
(upscale alone 1.79), mean luma unchanged (21.21 -> 21.19).

## Actor shadows

The original's only actor shadow is the A6 planar shadow: the caster flattened onto its floor plane along a fixed
`SUN_ANGLE` direction (`frame.shadowSun`), drawn only where the floor light scalar exceeds `shadow_threshold`. Levels are
lightmapped and their WMB lights reach the renderer as baked records, so before this change `shadows=rt` changed
nothing visible on them: Demir in level5 with the user's `ultra` setup differed from Vulkan raster by a mean 0.18/255,
and level5's floor is too dark for the planar shadow, so he had no shadow at all.

With `shadows=rt` (`rt_signals.comp` `actorShadow`, in the alpha of the shadow signal):

- **Casters**: models with the original SHADOW flag (`DrawInstance::shadowRequested`, the planar-shadow casters: the
  player, enemies, some props) get TLAS instance mask 4 in addition to 2.
- **Lights**: `render_policy::actor_shadow_lights` picks the baked WMB lights and native point/spot lights (entity
  lights such as `ev`'s wall lamp, a D3D light the lightmap does not hold) whose range contains a caster, deepest first,
  up to 31, plus the hardware sun. They are appended after the 32 shading records, whose upload is unchanged (level5 has
  45 baked lights).
- **Receivers**: lightmapped pixels. Each light weighs luma x N.L x falloff (baked: linear 1 - d/range, as the squared
  `enhancedBaked` falloff left a standing actor's lamp shadow beyond the lamp's bright disk at under 3% of the light
  there; native: its D3D attenuation and cone; sun: 1), at most 1. Per pixel and frame the dominant light, one other light
  picked in proportion to its weight (standing for all the others) and the sun are traced against the casters, toward a
  point jittered within clamp(0.005 range, 0.5, 2) units: lamps are small, and the 2-12 unit soft-shadow sphere blurred a
  body's shadow away a few metres from it. A blocked baked light counts only where the level geometry lets it reach the
  receiver (otherwise the lightmap holds none of it); native lights shine through walls like the D3D lights they are
  (and `ev`'s sits inside its wall fixture). The sun counts only where the level lets it through, so indoor levels get no
  sun shadow.
- **Darkness**: SHADOW_ALPHA/100 x min(occluded weight / strongest weight, 1). Blocking the dominant light darkens the
  surface exactly like the original planar shadow (`rgb *=` the factor after lighting, PBR and GI, before fog: the planar
  shadow is black alpha-blended over the lit surface); a weaker light gives a proportionally lighter shadow, several
  lights several shadows. The signal is accumulated over frames like the other shadow signals but not blurred spatially
  (the a-trous blur halved a body's shadow strip).
- **No light**: where the strongest weight is below 0.02 (no traced light in range, or too faint), the shadow blends
  into one cast at SHADOW_ALPHA toward the planar shadow's own light (`render_policy::planar_light_direction`, from
  `frame.shadowSun`: the direction along which `planar_projection` flattens the caster), against the casters only, like
  the planar shadow that ignores the level. So every caster has a shadow, in the original's direction where nothing
  else lights the floor.
- **Planar shadow**: never drawn under `shadows=rt`, in any view, and its shadow-LOD poses are not prepared. (0.4.0
  removed it only after the GPU reported at least 64 shadow pixels per caster, read back two frames later, so a caster
  without a light in range, or with a small shadow, showed the original fixed-direction shadow, and it flickered as the
  count crossed the threshold.)

Unchanged: default ray tracing, Vulkan raster, `shadows=shadowmap` and OpenGL draw the planar shadow as before. Lamp-walk
captures (level5, save slot 01, 4 positions) are byte-identical between 0.3.0 and this build for OpenGL default, Vulkan
raster (`original`), Vulkan RT default and Vulkan raster `shadows=shadowmap`.

Measured with the user's launcher setup (`ultra`, `vulkan-rt`, `shadows=rt`, GI, rough reflections, denoise, PBR,
MSAA 2, FSR quality, 1920x1080) against the same setup on `vulkan-raster` (RT off: `shadows=shadowmap` plus the planar
shadow). Darkness = 1 - frame / the same frame without that shadow (display luma, pixels darkened by at least 0.1;
mean includes the soft edges, p90 is the core). The planar shadow is 0.50 by construction (SHADOW_ALPHA 50).

| View (save) | RT actor shadow: pixels, mean, p90 | Raster planar shadow: pixels, mean, p90 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| level5 spawn (01) | 86433, 0.30, 0.50 | 40007, 0.47, 0.54 |
| level5 north of lamp | 194151, 0.36, 0.50 | 60344, 0.44, 0.54 |
| level5 west of lamp | 118761, 0.39, 0.53 | 52107, 0.45, 0.53 |
| level5 north-east of lamp | 98413, 0.31, 0.50 | 51046, 0.47, 0.54 |
| ev (06) | 72155, 0.40, 0.50 | 8483, 0.47, 0.50 |
| kriz (09) | 8834, 0.32, 0.49 | 565, 0.41, 0.49 |
| tnel24 (15) | 119313, 0.46, 0.54 | 2, - , - |
| cam1 (01) | 23282, 0.43, 0.52 | 7773, 0.49, 0.53 |

The level5 counts include chairs and desks (also SHADOW casters). In `ev`, Ebru's shadow from the wall lamp (a native
light 30 units from her) now falls from her feet across the floor toward the television, where the planar shadow was a
blob in the fixed sun direction; in level5 Demir's shadow points away from the 5-light lamp cluster and turns as he walks
round it; tnel24's floor was too dark for any planar shadow and now shows the player's. Captures (private, game assets):
`reverse/rt-actor-shadows/*-{raster,rt}.png`, `*-crop-raster-vs-rt.png` and `darkness-maps-*.png` (raster/RT frames
above, planar/actor darkness below). `k22-render-check --vulkan-rt` checks it on a lightmapped floor with one baked
light: the floor 22 units beside the caster drops from 255 to 126/128 on the side away from the light and the shadow
changes sides with the light; the planar control shadow (128 by default RT, from a copy placed so it falls on the other
side) is never drawn; with the light out of range the floor on the planar light's far side drops to 125/252 (actor shadow
toward `shadowSun`) while the planar control's side stays 252.

Cost (`K22_GPU_TIMING=1`, level5 bench, `ultra`, two runs each): `rt_signals` 0.76 -> 0.99-1.00 ms, GPU frame
3.17-3.18 -> 3.34-3.38 ms, 307 -> 289-292 FPS. Tracing every weighted light instead of the dominant one plus one sampled
light cost 1.10 ms (305 -> 275 FPS).

## Model shadows and ambient occlusion

Every campaign model carries a script material (A6 assigns `mat_model`, `mat_sprite`, `mat_terrain` to entities
without one; `engine.cpp`), so it is lit as an *ordinary* D3D material: Gouraud vertex lighting from the material's
ambient x the floor-light ambient (the A6 lightmap sample under the entity), the sun (`materialSunStrength`) and the
native lights; baked WMB lights do not light it. 0.4.0 marked these pixels unlit/explicit (G-buffer flag 4), so no RT
signal reached any character. They now have their own flag (16):

- `rt_signals.comp` computes the dynamic-light (D3D attenuation) and sun visibility for them against the SHADOW-flag
  models only (instance mask 4: actors, and the receiver itself when it is one, so an arm shadows the torso). In the
  original those lights shone through the level and every prop, and only SHADOW models cast shadows; the level's static
  shadow already reaches them through the floor light they sample. Tracing the level took the sun off every character
  indoors; tracing all models let curtains and radiators block a sun that passes through the walls.
- Ambient occlusion sees all geometry (level and models, the model itself) within 40 units: occlusion =
  1 - (1 - d/40)^2 for a hit at distance d (full darkness at contact, little from distant geometry).
- `scene.frag` `ordinaryOcclusion` takes the occluded light off the vertex lighting: ambient x (1 - AO), the sun x
  (1 - its visibility), other native lights x (1 - their visibility). Where nothing is occluded the original vertex
  lighting is unchanged. Ray origins use the terminator origin above, which keeps self-shadow free of acne.
- Models without a script material (Bonus/A7 profile) and non-lightmapped level surfaces use the per-pixel model
  lighting: the ambient term x AO, the sun and native lights as before, and the baked WMB lights (`enhancedBaked`, the
  model light loop) x their visibility (`bakedVisibility`: the dominant baked light and one other picked by weight,
  traced against all geometry, in the mask alpha, blurred among model pixels only).

`k22-render-check --vulkan-rt` renders a floor model at z=2 under the actor-shadow fixture's camera. With an overhang in
the same model, the floor point in its shadow drops from 78.9 to 27 (luma; the lit side 149.9 -> 149.5) for a baked lamp
(per-pixel model lighting) and from 199.4 to 0 for a native lamp on an ordinary material (SHADOW-flag model); a wall
5 units beside a floor point lowers it from 127 to 90 (per-pixel ambient) and from 128 to 100 (ordinary material).

In the game (`--preset ultra`, `vulkan-rt`, 1920x1080, original saves 01 and 07): Demir in level5 drops from mean luma
27.7 to 26.6 over his body column, Ebru in `ev` (standing by the radiator, under the wall lamp) from 49.3 to 43.6, with
the darkening under the arms, between the legs, at the collar and the hands. Cost (`K22_GPU_TIMING=1`, level5, 900
steady frames per run, two runs each, 0.4.0 -> this): `rt_signals` 1.01-1.03 -> 1.13 ms, scene 0.52-0.53 -> 0.56 ms
(`ordinaryOcclusion`), GPU frame 3.33-3.38 -> 3.49-3.51 ms; the planar shadow draws are gone.

Lightmapped surfaces keep the models-only occlusion term: their lightmaps already hold the level's occlusion.

## Performance

Measured 2026-10-10 on an RX 7900 XTX (RADV, Mesa 26.2.4): Demir in level5 (original save slot 01), standing,
1920x1080, `--preset ultra` (MSAA 4, PBR, RT shadows/GI/rough reflections, denoise, bloom, TAA, volumetric fog,
smooth normals, tessellation), immediate present, nested in a headless gamescope. `K22_GPU_TIMING=1` writes Vulkan
timestamps between the renderer's passes and CPU frame times to stderr, averaged over 300 frames (`K22_FRAME_TIMING=FILE`
writes one line per frame on any backend: frame, poll+scenario, tick, draw and finish_frame microseconds, live particles). GPU ms per pass:

| Pass | RT before | RT `fsr=off` | RT `fsr=quality` (ultra) | raster before | raster `fsr=off` | raster `fsr=quality` |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| BLAS refit + TLAS (`as_build`) | 0.21 | 0.21 | 0.21 | 0.00 | 0.00 | 0.00 |
| G-buffer prepass | 0.26 | 0.27 | 0.22 | - | - | - |
| RT signals (`rt_signals.comp`) | 1.61 | 1.65 | 0.77 | - | - | - |
| denoiser (`rt_filter.comp`, 4 passes) | 1.42 | 1.44 | 0.62 | - | - | - |
| scene draws | 0.89 | 0.87 | 0.58 | 0.51 | 0.50 | 0.45 |
| shadow maps | - | - | - | 0.11 | 0.11 | 0.12 |
| depth effects (volumetric fog) | 1.63 | 0.47 | 0.23 | 1.51 | 0.45 | 0.29 |
| composite (bloom, tone map, TAA) | 0.27 | 0.25 | 0.02 | 0.28 | 0.26 | 0.02 |
| FSR 3.1 (reactive + upscale) | - | - | 0.34 | - | - | 0.37 |
| GPU frame total | 6.44 | 5.30 | 3.12 | 2.56 | 1.47 | 1.40 |
| CPU recording | 1.55 | 1.46 | 1.54 | 1.17 | 1.17 | 1.27 |
| frame time (ms) / FPS | 8.22 / 122 | 5.52 / 181 | 3.27 / 306 | 3.92 / 255 | 2.36 / 424 | 2.47 / 405 |

Root causes found and fixed:
- **CPU/GPU serialization.** The frame-latency limit (1 in a window, `TRIPLEBUFFER` fullscreen 2) waited for the
  previous frame's fence before recording the next frame, so CPU recording (1.2-1.6 ms) and GPU work never overlapped
  (RT: 8.2 ms frames for 6.4 ms of GPU work). The limit now bounds submissions only: the next frame records into the
  other, idle slot while the previous one runs, and `finish()` waits before submitting. Alone: RT 122 -> 154 FPS,
  raster 255 -> 380 FPS, same queue depth.
- **Full-resolution volumetric fog** (24 steps x up to 32 lights per pixel) was the second-largest pass on both
  backends. It now marches at half resolution (alpha keeps each sample's depth) and is added with a depth-aware
  bilinear upsample (`effects.frag` modes 4/14): 1.6 -> 0.47 ms.
- **Per-pixel RT cost at display resolution**: signals and denoiser scale with pixels. `ultra` now runs FSR 3.1
  quality (2/3 per axis, 0.44x pixels), which halves them; the ultra preset is CPU-bound afterwards.
- Not a cause: acceleration structures are already refit (BLAS update for changed poses, TLAS update when the instance
  count is unchanged; 0.21 ms), there are no per-frame queue/device waits, readbacks or descriptor-set rebuilds
  outside the per-slot arenas.

## Limits

- Sun shadows (`shadows=rt` and `shadows=shadowmap` alike) make non-lightmapped models indoors much darker
  than the original. The sun is the main light on those models, and ceilings occlude it, for example the
  bed in save 8 and the pit grate in save 26. In the original the sun was never occluded. Ordinary-material models
  (D3D-lit, flag 16) are exempt under `shadows=rt`: only SHADOW casters occlude their sun.
- A light placed inside solid level geometry (as in the Start4 test scene) is still occluded by
  `shadows=rt` for receivers whose path crosses another brush toward it.
- One bounce, one sample per pixel; reflections hit with legacy shading.
- The TLAS is rebuilt per camera when its instance count changes (else updated), BLAS refit for changed poses, without compaction.
- Particles, view-space entities and billboards are not in the acceleration structure.
- With `tessellation=1` the BLAS still holds the base mesh: ray-traced shadows, GI and reflections see model
  silhouettes without the PN bulge.
- Actor shadows on lightmapped surfaces come from SHADOW casters only. Ordinary-material models (every campaign model)
  are shadowed only by SHADOW casters (themselves included) from their D3D lights; props without the flag occlude only
  their ambient (AO). Decal models (the level5 blood pool) take actor shadows as models do, not as the floor below.
- Mirror/portal views have no actor shadows (the planar shadow is not drawn there either; the game sets `noshadow` on its
  mirror view); SHADOW entities that are themselves invisible are not in the acceleration structure and cast none
  (the scripts turn SHADOW off with INVISIBLE). Translucent and MSAA-edge pixels keep the inline path without actor
  shadows or AO. A baked light inside solid geometry casts no actor shadow (its level ray is blocked).
  `shadows=shadowmap` has no actor shadows from baked lights (one cube map for one dynamic light).
- Ordinary materials subtract the occluded light from their clamped Gouraud lighting, so a vertex saturated above 1
  darkens less than the occluded share; their specular is not shadowed.

```

`docs/RELEASE_PROCESS.md`:

```md
# Release process

How Kabus22 Linux versions are numbered, built, signed, published, updated and rolled back.
Original game media is **never** part of any release artifact (see [What never ships](#what-never-ships)).

## Versioning

- Semantic versioning `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH[-PRERELEASE][+BUILD]`.
- Single source: `project(... VERSION X.Y.Z)` in both `CMakeLists.txt` and `installer/CMakeLists.txt`
  (keep them equal). CMake passes it to every native and installer target as `K22_VERSION="X.Y.Z"`;
  `--version` of `kabus22`, `kabus22-launcher`, `kabus22-setup` and `kabus22-updater` reports it.
- Git tag `vX.Y.Z` (stable) or `vX.Y.Z-rc.N` / `-beta.N` (experimental). The release workflow refuses
  a tag whose `X.Y.Z` differs from the CMake project version.

## Channels

| Channel | GitHub release | Signed manifest `channel` | Offered to |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `stable` | normal (not prerelease) | `stable` | everyone (default) |
| `experimental` | prerelease | `experimental` | users who set `channel=experimental` |

Drafts are never offered. A stable-channel updater additionally refuses a manifest whose **signed**
channel is not `stable`, so the unsigned GitHub prerelease flag alone cannot push experimental builds
to stable users.

User settings: `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-~/.config}/kabus22/updates.ini`

```ini
[Updates]
repository=sergen213/kabus22-linux
channel=stable
```

## Installation layout

```
<root>/game/                    original extracted assets — never touched by updates
<root>/versions/<v>/{bin,lib,share}/   immutable per-version payload (+ .kabus22-payload.json inventory)
<root>/current -> versions/<v>  relative symlink, swapped atomically
<root>/bin|lib|share -> current/…      compat symlinks (desktop entries use <root>/bin/kabus22-launcher)
<root>/versions/.state          active=<v> / previous=<v>
```

`installer/layout.{hpp,cpp}` (`k22::layout`) is the only code that changes this layout. It only creates,
moves or deletes `bin`, `lib`, `share`, `current` and entries inside `versions/`; saves (`kayit*.sav`),
options and every other root entry stay untouched, even when the root is also the engine save root.
Activation is crash-safe: a temporary symlink is created inside `versions/` and `rename(2)`d over
`current`; `.state` is written afterwards by temp-file + `rename(2)`; a crash between the two is
detected (`current` wins). Legacy flat installs (real `bin/lib/share` directories) are migrated into
`versions/<updater version>` on the first `--apply`; migration is idempotent and resumable.
Only the active and previous version (plus the version the updater runs from) are retained.

## Update artifacts and signing

Every release carries three update assets:

| Asset | Content |
| --- | --- |
| `kabus22-update.json` | `{"format":1,"version","channel","min_glibc","payload":{"name","sha256","size"},"components":[…]}` |
| `kabus22-update.json.sig` | base64 of the raw 64-byte Ed25519 signature over the exact JSON bytes |
| `kabus22-<v>-linux-x86_64.tar.gz` | deterministic `bin/ lib/ share/` tree for `versions/<v>` |

Tools (`tools/release/`, require Python 3 with `cryptography`):

```sh
# Payload + manifest from an assembled/extracted AppImage AppDir (or --tree DIR with bin/ lib/ share/)
python3 tools/release/make_update_manifest.py --appdir AppDir --version 0.2.1 --channel stable --output-dir dist
# Sign (key file or env KABUS22_UPDATE_SIGNING_KEY = base64 raw 32-byte seed)
python3 tools/release/sign_manifest.py dist/kabus22-update.json --key ~/.local/share/kabus22-release-keys/update-ed25519.key
python3 tools/release/sign_manifest.py --public-key --key KEYFILE      # print the matching public key
python3 tools/release/sign_manifest.py --generate-key NEWKEYFILE       # new 0600 key; prints public key only
```

`make_update_manifest.py` refuses anything but regular files, directories and in-tree relative
symlinks under `bin/ lib/ share/`, setuid/setgid bits, and game-asset-like files (`.wrs`, `.wdl`, `.sav`, …).

`kabus22-updater` verifies, in order: HTTPS transport (libcurl, TLS peer/host verification, HTTPS-only
redirects, size limits, timeouts) → Ed25519 signature with the public key compiled in from CMake cache
variable `K22_UPDATE_PUBLIC_KEY` → manifest fields, version equals the release tag, signed channel,
`min_glibc` → payload size and SHA-256 → safe extraction (no absolute/`..` paths, no escaping links,
no hard links, devices or setuid bits; only `bin/ lib/ share/`) into a private stage inside `versions/`
→ atomic activation. Any failure leaves the installation unchanged.

### Key custody and rotation

- Development/project key: `~/.local/share/kabus22-release-keys/update-ed25519.key` on the maintainer
  workstation (mode 0600, outside the repository, never printed or committed). Public key (default
  `K22_UPDATE_PUBLIC_KEY`): `2mfjUSeWRcSIPa4B3uaLUWxnBFPWulQYvdq1uv4PVVM=`.
- CI signing uses the repository secret `KABUS22_UPDATE_SIGNING_KEY` (same base64 seed). The release
  workflow aborts if the secret's public key differs from the embedded default.
- Keep an offline backup of the key file. Losing it means no further update can be verified by
  existing installations; they must reinstall from a new AppImage.
- Rotation: generate a new key, set the new public key as the `K22_UPDATE_PUBLIC_KEY` default, and ship
  one release **signed with the old key** whose payload contains the updater with the new key. After
  users have updated past it, replace the CI secret with the new key. A compromised key cannot be
  revoked remotely: publish an advisory and require a manual AppImage reinstall.

## CI

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (push/PR, Ubuntu 24.04): builds the native engine and installer/launcher/
  updater with distro packages, runs asset-free CTests (fixture-dependent tests self-skip in a public
  checkout), `tools/check_wrs2.py` and the packaging policy self-check.
- `.github/workflows/release.yml` (tag `v*`): acquires the pinned innoextract helper and uruntime (hash
  and signature checked), builds the pinned toolchain image from `tools/Dockerfile.ubuntu24` (stdin, no
  build context), runs `tools/build_kabus_baseline.sh`, extracts the AppImage SquashFS, builds and signs
  the update payload, and creates a **draft** GitHub release with the AppImage, its report and
  dependency-source bundle, native source archive, update assets and `SHA256SUMS`.

## Publishing a release

1. Bump `VERSION` in both `project()` calls; update README/changelog.
2. Run the local test suites (native and installer CTest, including `updater_end_to_end`).
3. Tag `vX.Y.Z` (or `vX.Y.Z-rc.N`) and push the tag.
4. Qualify the draft release artifacts (install from ISO, launcher, OpenGL/Vulkan startup, update from
   the previous version on a private copy of an installation).
5. Publish the draft (prerelease flag set automatically for experimental versions). Only then do
   updaters see it.

Local equivalent of steps 3–4 without CI: follow README "Optional AppImage assembly", then extract the
AppImage (`unsquashfs -o <squashfs_offset from report> …`) and run the two `tools/release` commands.

## AppImage assembly

`tools/package_kabus_appimage.py` requires `--engine`, `--installer`, `--launcher` and `--updater`
(release build only; it refuses the `-testhttp` test build). It bundles the updater's libcurl/OpenSSL
closure with distro notices and corresponding sources, and records the compiled-in header-only
nlohmann/json package notice. The installed and update payload (`versions/<v>/bin`) contains `kabus22`,
`kabus22-launcher`, `kabus22-setup` (spawned by the launcher's Installation page), `kabus22-updater`
and the `innoextract` helper; the updater and `make_update_manifest.py` require the first four.

## Rollback

```sh
kabus22-updater --install-dir ~/.local/share/kabus22 --rollback   # previous <-> active
kabus22-updater --install-dir ~/.local/share/kabus22 --status     # {"active","previous","installed"}
```

The launcher exposes the same actions. Rolling back only swaps `current`; saves and options are untouched.

## Testing the updater

`installer/check_update.cpp` (CTest `updater_layout_signature_archive`) covers layout migrate/commit/
rollback/crash recovery with save files present, semantic-version/channel selection, signature
acceptance/rejection and hostile archives. `installer/check_updater_e2e.py` (CTest
`updater_end_to_end`) drives the real CLI against a local `http.server` fixture through
`kabus22-updater-testhttp`: a test-only executable (built only with `BUILD_TESTING`, define
`K22_UPDATER_TEST_HTTP`) that additionally accepts `http://127.0.0.1:PORT` and reads the API base and
public key from `KABUS22_UPDATER_TEST_API` / `KABUS22_UPDATER_TEST_PUBLIC_KEY`. The shipped
`kabus22-updater` contains neither hook; the E2E test and the AppImage packager both check that.

## Private qualification notes — 0.2.0 candidate (2026-10-10, not published)

The primary evidence ledger is `reverse/decompiled/runtime/CONTRACT.txt` (numbered sections; cited as `CONTRACT.txt §N` or `CONTRACT.txt:LINE`). Paths under `reverse/` other than `reverse/scripts/*.java` are a private workspace and are not in the public repository (`.gitignore` lines 12-25, 512-513), because they contain decompiled proprietary code, extracted scripts and media.

## Confidence labels

All reverse-engineering documents use: **CONFIRMED** (direct evidence: bytes, decompiled code plus instructions, or recorded native runs), **HIGH CONFIDENCE** (strong indirect evidence), **HYPOTHESIS** (plausible, untested), **UNKNOWN** (not established; what is missing is stated). Native-port observations are never presented as observations of the original Windows game. Since 2026-10-09 the unmodified ISO `K22.exe` (SHA-256 `cc193c6b…4ebd`) has also been executed under Wine 11.19 (wined3d) as a reference tool only (see Dynamic analysis); before that, it had never been executed.

## Dynamic analysis (original under Wine)

`tools/wine-reference/wineref.py` (`setup` / `run`) extracts the ISO payload with innoextract into a private scratch tree, creates a private Wine prefix (X11 driver, drive `K:` mapped to the game copy, original saves copied in) and runs `K22.exe -nc -diag -d defiae_d3d -d defdil_en -d defses_en` windowed at the authored 1024×768 (`options.k22` byte 0 = 2, no `deftam_d3d`). It replays the same `tests/reference/*.k22s` cases the native engine runs (keys by X keysym through XTest, `#wine:` lines for timing) and captures the exact window with `ffmpeg -f x11grab -window_id`. Findings: the ISO `K22.exe` fails A6's own executable checksum (`0041fc00`/`00422af0`: stored 233761058, actual byte sum 233546425) and stops with `Error E356: Startup failure`; `-nc` is the stock A6 option that skips that check (`00412b90` sets `0x644848`), no binary is patched. A6 also stalls in its compile loop while its window is unfocused, so the driver re-activates the window. Nothing in the native build or runtime uses Wine; captures stay in `reverse/wine-reference/` (private).

## Inputs (read-only)

| Input | Use |
|---|---|
| `Kabus-22_Win_TR-EN-DE_ISO-Version/Kabus 22.iso` | ISO edition "Kabus 22 Multi 3" (Inno Setup 5.2.1); only source for native installs |
| `setup.exe` + `setup-1.bin` | different "Kabus 22 Test" build (Inno 5.1.10); not used for engine analysis |

| `~/.local/share/kabus22/game/` | native installation's verbatim ISO data |

Originals are never modified; mutation tests use private copies; `objcopy` must not be pointed at originals (it rewrites its input when no output is given).

## Methodology

1. **Acquire and fingerprint.** List the ISO, extract the Inno payload into a private directory with innoextract, hash every executable/archive and compare size+MD5 with the installer's own checksums (`reverse/media/iso/list-exact.txt`). Results: [EXECUTABLE_ANALYSIS](reverse-engineering/EXECUTABLE_ANALYSIS.md).
2. **Identify the engine** from embedded version strings and imports before reading code ([ENGINE_IDENTIFICATION](reverse-engineering/ENGINE_IDENTIFICATION.md)).
3. **Targeted static recovery.** Seed Ghidra exports from strings (e.g. `RESOURCE`, `WRS2`, `EXECUTE`), plugin handshakes (`A6_DLLAPI` resolver) and cross-references; export decompiled C **and** instruction listings, because the decompiler is sometimes wrong (example: the anisotropy sampler argument at `0x0043dc70` is a float bit pattern the decompiler printed as `0`, `CONTRACT.txt` §23). Every export run writes a manifest of candidates, timeouts and omissions (`reverse/decompiled/*/…recovery.txt`); timeouts are never presented as recovered code (`reverse/decompiled/RECOVERY.txt` lines 22-24).
4. **Script recovery.** Original game logic is WDL source inside WRS archives; the archive index/LZSS codec was recovered (`FUN_0041fd20`, `FUN_00414bc0`) and scripts were extracted to `reverse/extracted/original/` (Lutris build) and `reverse/media/iso/scripts/` (ISO build). Script names are cited as `file.wdl:identifier`; script text is not reproduced in documentation.
5. **Contracts.** Each recovered behaviour is written as a numbered section in `CONTRACT.txt` with the original address, the native symbol that implements it, and the exact verification performed. Later sections supersede earlier ones where stated.
6. **Native implementation and verification.** The C++20 engine in `native/` executes the original scripts; contracts are guarded by CTest suites and bounded real runs (`--frames N`, `--capture FILE.ppm`, private `XDG_*` directories, input ledgers). Evidence images/logs are kept under `reverse/` (e.g. `reverse/campaign-checkpoint-*.png`, `reverse/native-gl-bonus-*-evidence.txt`). These prove native behaviour, not original Windows parity.
7. **Boundaries.** No Wine/Proton at runtime; no redistribution of game assets, scripts or decompiled output. No clean-room or legal guarantee is claimed by these documents.

## Reproducing the Ghidra exports

Run from the repository root. All runs are `-readOnly -noanalysis` against the existing project, so the project database is not changed.

```sh
GH=/opt/ghidra/support/analyzeHeadless
# Baseline export of all three programs (RecoverKabus.java args: OUT [MAX_FUNCTIONS] [TIMEOUT_SECONDS] [ADDRESS ...])
"$GH" "$PWD/reverse/ghidra" Kabus22 -process '*' -noanalysis -readOnly \
  -scriptPath "$PWD/reverse/scripts" -postScript RecoverKabus.java "$PWD/reverse/decompiled/final" 180 20

# Loader follow-up (WRS index, resource registration, script loader, parser, version string)
"$GH" "$PWD/reverse/ghidra" Kabus22 -process K22.exe -noanalysis -readOnly \
  -scriptPath "$PWD/reverse/scripts" -postScript RecoverKabus.java "$PWD/reverse/decompiled/loaders" 120 20 \
  0041fd20 0041ff20 00420490 00419cb0 00419b10 00402d60 0041e180 0061ddb4

# Plugin escape helpers in the community kabus_dll.dll
"$GH" "$PWD/reverse/ghidra" Kabus22 -process kabus_dll.dll -noanalysis -readOnly \
  -scriptPath "$PWD/reverse/scripts" -postScript RecoverKabus.java "$PWD/reverse/decompiled/final" 180 20 \
  1008e240 1009ca20 1009cac0

# Embedded PCX (built-in font) export; args: OUT IMAGE_ADDRESS [POINTER_ADDRESS [PE_FILE ...]]
"$GH" "$PWD/reverse/ghidra" Kabus22 -process K22.exe -noanalysis -readOnly \
  -scriptPath "$PWD/reverse/scripts" -postScript ExportEmbeddedPcx.java /tmp/k22-font 0062130c 00627310

# Runtime follow-up (private script; args: OUT MAX_FUNCTIONS SEED_ADDRESS ...)
"$GH" "$PWD/reverse/ghidra" Kabus22 -process K22.exe -noanalysis -readOnly \
  -scriptPath "$PWD/reverse/decompiled/runtime" -postScript RecoverRuntime.java /tmp/k22-runtime 40 00414650
```

Commands 1-3 are recorded in `reverse/decompiled/RECOVERY.txt` lines 11-18; command 4 in the header of `reverse/scripts/ExportEmbeddedPcx.java`. A7 Bonus analysis uses private `reverse/decompiled/runtime/bonus-core/*.java` and `bonus-physics/*.java` scripts against a separate project containing `Kabus 22 Mode/acknex.dll` (SHA-256 `f96c7645…227b`). Expected outputs are Ghidra approximations that do not compile and are not engine source.

`docs/TEXTURE_RESTORATION.md`:

```md
# Texture restoration (optional high-resolution packs)

Kabus 22 ships 2006-era textures (mostly 256 px and below, many 8-bit palettised). The native engine can
overlay a **texture pack** on top of the original textures. Packs are optional, live outside the game
directory, and never modify original assets: without a pack the engine renders exactly the original data.

`tools/texture-upscaler/upscale.py` turns the engine's own texture dump into such a pack.

## Techniques investigated

| Technique | Kind | Strengths | Problems for this game |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Real-ESRGAN** (`realesrgan-x4plus`, ncnn/Vulkan build) | GAN super-resolution, trained on synthetic real-world degradations | Convincing detail on photographic surfaces (concrete, rock, foliage, sky); runs on any Vulkan GPU without PyTorch | Hallucinates structure: invents letters, rivets, symbols; can shift colours; tiles get seams unless padded; native model is 4× only |
| **ESRGAN** (original + community models) | GAN super-resolution | Many game-texture-specific models exist | Same hallucination risk; most community models have unclear licences and need PyTorch; no reproducible baseline |
| **SwinIR** | Transformer restoration (PSNR and GAN variants) | PSNR variant is the most faithful learned upscaler; little hallucination | PyTorch + large GPU memory, slow on thousands of textures; GAN variant has the same issues as ESRGAN |
| **Lanczos (+ mild unsharp mask)** | Classical resampling | Deterministic, never invents content, exact colour statistics, fast | Softer than learned methods; ringing on hard edges |
| **Nearest** | Classical | Bit-exact (box-downscale reproduces the original), keeps alpha-test coverage exactly | Blocky |
| **Scale2x / EPX ("xbr-like")** | Pixel-art edge-directed scaling | Smooths diagonal staircases while only ever emitting colours that already exist in the source | Only for flat/low-colour art; repeated for 4× |

Learned models are optional because they cannot be redistributed with the project and are not needed
for a correct game. The tool calls an external `realesrgan-ncnn-vulkan` only when it is on `PATH`; it
is reported as unavailable otherwise (and `--method realesrgan` then fails instead of silently falling
back). SwinIR/ESRGAN were not integrated: they add a PyTorch dependency for no safety benefit over the
guarded Real-ESRGAN path.

## Policy per category

Categories come from the engine dump (`index.tsv`).

| Category | `--method auto` | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `ui`, `font` | Scale2x (`xbr-like`) | Turkish text, digits and HUD symbols must stay exactly as drawn; never AI, never blurred |
| any texture with ≤16 distinct colours, or listed via `--protect FILE` | Scale2x | Treated as text/signage/flat art |
| `world`, `sky` | Real-ESRGAN if available, else Lanczos + mild unsharp; wrap-padded so tiling stays seamless | Photographic surfaces |
| `model` | Real-ESRGAN if available, else Lanczos + mild unsharp; edge-padded (UV atlases do not tile) | |
| `sprite` | Real-ESRGAN if available, else Lanczos; **alpha always nearest** | Alpha-test coverage must not change |
| `other` | Lanczos | Unknown content, stay conservative |

An explicit `--method lanczos|nearest|xbr-like` applies to every texture; `--method realesrgan` still
never touches `ui`/`font`/protected textures.

## Safety rules (enforced by the tool)

* **Pure integer scale.** Output is exactly `original × s` (`s` = 2 or 4; reduced per texture to stay
  ≤ 8192 px). No crop, pad or aspect change in the result, so UVs, lightmaps, collision and gameplay
  are unchanged — packs only change sampled colours, never geometry.
* **Consistency guard.** Every result is box-downscaled back to the original size and compared with the
  original pixels. If the mean absolute error exceeds `--max-error` (default 6/255) or any channel's mean
  shifts more than `--max-shift` (default 1.5/255), the result is discarded and the next method is tried:
  AI → Lanczos → nearest (nearest is exact by construction). This rejects hallucinated symbols, invented
  text and colour drift. Only visible texels (alpha > 0) count for RGB.
* **Alpha.** For Lanczos/Real-ESRGAN alpha is nearest-scaled, so alpha-test coverage is identical at every
  threshold. Before resampling, visible colours are bled a few texels into fully transparent texels, so
  colour-key RGB (e.g. magenta) never fringes visible edges; straight alpha is kept (premultiplying and
  dividing was tried and amplified noise in soft-alpha effect skins, failing the guard).
  Scale2x scales whole RGBA texels, so alpha only takes values present in the original.
* **Key check.** Each `<key>.png` is re-hashed from its decoded pixels; a mismatch with the filename (or
  with `index.tsv` dimensions) excludes that texture and makes the run exit 1.
* **Path safety.** Pack paths are always `textures/<key>[_suffix].png`; the validator rejects absolute
  paths, `..`, and symlinks that resolve outside the pack. `--force` only replaces a directory that is
  already a texture pack; the pack is written to a temporary sibling and renamed into place.
* **No redistribution.** Packs are derived from the original game art; the default licence line says
  personal use only. Do not publish packs built from the commercial textures.

## Optional PBR maps (`--pbr`)

For `world`/`model` textures (not protected ones) the tool derives conservative maps from the upscaled
albedo:

* `normal`: Sobel gradient of a lightly blurred luminance height field, strength 2, tangent space,
  OpenGL convention (+Y up: green > 128 means the surface faces up the texture), wrap sampling.
* `roughness`: 0.75–1.0 from local luminance contrast (mostly rough; no fake gloss).
* `ao`: subtle cavity term (at most 20 % darkening).
* `metallic`: not written; the engine's default is 0.

These are approximations from colour, not measured materials; leave `--pbr` off for the original look.

## In-engine `texture_upscale` (Vulkan, no pack needed)

`--graphics texture_upscale=1` (Vulkan raster and RT; presets `enhanced`/`ultra`) applies the same
non-AI `--method auto` policy at texture upload, on the CPU, without writing anything to disk:

* Only world and model material skins with both sides ≤ 512 px, 2× (`k22::upscale_texture_2x`).
  Lightmaps, sky strips, UI, fonts, particles, dynamic/turbulent images and textures that a pack
  replaces keep their original upload. UV policy keeps the original dimensions.
* ≤ 16 distinct colours: Scale2x. Otherwise separable Lanczos-3 plus the tool's mild unsharp mask
  (35 %, threshold 2); world textures wrap (tiling), model atlases clamp to the edge.
* RGB is resampled after the same 4-texel colour bleed; alpha is always nearest-scaled, so alpha-test
  coverage is identical at every threshold (also for Scale2x, unlike the offline tool's whole-texel
  Scale2x).
* Mipmaps are generated from the upscaled level 0. PBR normal/ORM maps only come from packs, and a pack
  hit skips the upscale, so derived maps always match their albedo.
* Cost (RX 7900 XTX host, Release, row bands on all cores): all 1792 dumped world/model textures
  ≤ 512 px take 3.9 s in total, 2.2 ms mean, 10 ms worst. Demir level5 (`kayit0.sav`) load to first
  frames goes from 3.50 s to 3.58 s on Vulkan RT and raster (three and two runs). The result is not
  cached on disk; it lives as long as the image's GPU texture.

`k22-render-check --policy` checks exact 2×, coverage at alpha 1/3/128/255, that a magenta colour key
never reaches visible texels, the box-downscale guard (≤ 6/255 mean error, ≤ 1.5/255 shift) and that
Scale2x emits only source colours.

## Usage

```sh
# 1. dump the original textures (decoded RGBA, lossless) from your installed game
kabus22 --dump-textures /tmp/k22-dump --data ~/.local/share/kabus22/game
# 2. build a 2x pack into ${XDG_DATA_HOME:-~/.local/share}/kabus22/packs/hd2x
python3 tools/texture-upscaler/upscale.py /tmp/k22-dump --name hd2x --scale 2 [--pbr] [--method auto]
# 3. validate (also checks the integer-scale rule against the dump)
python3 tools/texture-upscaler/upscale.py --validate ~/.local/share/kabus22/packs/hd2x /tmp/k22-dump
# 4. play with it
kabus22 --texture-pack hd2x
```

`kabus22 --list-capabilities` lists installed packs with `valid` and a reason; the launcher's graphics
page selects packs the same way. Several `--texture-pack` options may be given; the first pack that
contains a key supplies all of that texture's maps (kinds are not mixed across packs). `--preset
enhanced|ultra` without `--texture-pack` uses every valid installed pack, in directory-name order.
Requirements: Python 3, Pillow, numpy; optionally `realesrgan-ncnn-vulkan` with its `models/` directory.
Other options: `--output DIR`, `--display-name`, `--license`, `--protect FILE`, `--jobs N`, `--force`.

## Pack format (summary of the engine contract)

```
kabus22-texture-pack 1
name\t<display name>
license\t<text>
<key>\t<albedo|normal|roughness|metallic|ao>\t<relative/path.png>
```

`key` is lowercase 16-hex FNV-1a-64 (offset `0xcbf29ce484222325`, prime `0x100000001b3`) over the
width (LE uint32), height (LE uint32) and the engine-decoded RGBA8 bytes, top row first. Reference
values: 0×0 image → `a8c7f832281a39c5`; 1×1 RGBA (0,0,0,0) → `7e1ef442cd317605`. Files are PNG, at most
8192 px per side and 64 MiB, sized `original × s` with `s ∈ {1,2,4,8}` and the same `s` for every kind
of one key. Normal maps are RGB tangent space (+Y up); roughness/metallic/ao use the red channel.

Tests: `python3 tools/texture-upscaler/test_upscale.py` (also registered in CTest as `texture_upscaler`).

```

`docs/WIDESCREEN_IMPLEMENTATION.md`:

```md
# Widescreen: community patch mechanism and native implementation

Labels: **CONFIRMED** / **HIGH CONFIDENCE** / **HYPOTHESIS** / **UNKNOWN**. Related: [COMMUNITY_PATCH_ANALYSIS](COMMUNITY_PATCH_ANALYSIS.md) · [PATCH_BINARY_DIFF](PATCH_BINARY_DIFF.md) · [CAMERA_SYSTEM](CAMERA_SYSTEM.md) · [BUG_FIX_PORTING](BUG_FIX_PORTING.md).

Short answer: the community patch is **not Hor+**. It raises the engine's mode cap, lets `K22.ini` choose any resolution ≥ 1280×720, and re-scales 2D art and HUD with separate X/Y factors (non-uniform stretch). The 3D projection is untouched: the engine keeps the horizontal FOV (`camera.arc`) and derives the vertical extent from the window, so wider windows show **less** vertically (Vert-) in windowed/borderless mode, while exclusive fullscreen keeps the 4:3 vertical extent and stretches the image horizontally. The native engine reproduces the same model for the original scripts; it adds no Hor+.

## 1. How the patch does it

| Layer | Mechanism | Evidence | Label |
|---|---|---|---|
| Executable | largest mode-table entry 1920×1200 → 3840×2400; start-up archive `K22Widescreen.wrs` | `.data 0x627ab8`, `0x621243` ([PATCH_BINARY_DIFF](PATCH_BINARY_DIFF.md) §2.2) | CONFIRMED |
| Projection code | unchanged (`.text` differs only at three start-up/integrity sites; `.rdata` identical) | `CONTRACT.txt:2147-2163`; `reverse/community/reports/pe-compare.json` | CONFIRMED |
| Resolution choice | `dbg_screen_reset(0)` in `K22Widescreen.wdl`: `Screen:Mode` 0/1/2 from `K22.ini` via `INI_GetVariable`; `X`/`Y` = INI values, or `sys_metrics(0/1)` when 0 or borderless; rejects < 1280×720 with an error and exits; `video_window(...,16|0|1,title)` + `video_set(W,H,depth, mode 2|1|2)`; `GA_Cozunurluk` pinned to 0 and `GA_Cozunurlukler[0..1]=W,H` | `reverse/community/wrs/patch-K22Widescreen/K22Widescreen.wdl` lines 626-668 | CONFIRMED |
| 2D scale families | `GA_YeniScaleOranlari`=(W/1366, H/768) main-menu background `kan_1366.tga`; `…2`=(W/1024, H/768) loading/intro panels; `…3`=(W/640, H/480) inventory/pause backgrounds, fades, cinematic bars, boss bar, map fade; X and Y independent → non-uniform stretch | same file 648-656; consumers `Kabusdismenu`, `YeniMenu`, `Envantermenu`, `Smartmenu`, `cinematic`, `kotu_koruyucu`, `LevelYonetim`, `BUL_Kordinat` (`reverse/community/diffs/*.diff`) | CONFIRMED |
| HUD/menu/text state switching | main loop: in gameplay `dbg_screen_reset(1)` sets `GA_ScaleOranlari{,2}`=(W/640, H/480); in menus/game-over/pause `dbg_screen_reset(2)` sets them and `GA_FontOranlari` to (W/1280, H/720) and `(3)` rescales ~40 TEXT objects, fades, subtitle Y = H − H/16 | `K22Widescreen.wdl` 672-770, 838-878 | CONFIRMED |
| Camera/FOV | no `camera.arc`/`camera.aspect` assignment added for widescreen (arc writes 155 → 156, the extra one is the F5 camera `arc=70`); viewport already `screen_size` in original `cam.wdl` | `reports/script-identifier-counts.json`; `diffs/cam.wdl.diff` | CONFIRMED |
| View-space weapon preview | `SilahPanel` default `Y=-70,Z=-37.5`; `Z=-52` if `Screen:Mode==1` (fullscreen); cinematic crate variant −40/−30 | `diffs/silah.wdl.diff`, `diffs/cinematic.wdl.diff` | CONFIRMED |
| Blood bursts | particle size forced to 0 (`kan_blood_scale=0`, scaled formula commented out) | `K22Widescreen.wdl:690`, `diffs/efect2.wdl.diff` | CONFIRMED |

### 1.1 Resulting 3D field of view

A6 projection (recovered, `CONTRACT.txt:2156-2163`; native `native/render_policy.hpp:33-38`): ARC is the horizontal FOV; vertical half-tangent = tan(ARC/2) · H/W · |pixelAspect|, with pixelAspect = 1/(ASPECT·Q), Q = (H·320)/(W·240) in exclusive fullscreen and Q = 1 otherwise; scripts keep ASPECT = 1.

Vertical FOV in degrees for representative ARC values (derived from that formula; **CONFIRMED** as arithmetic over the recovered contract, not measured in a Windows run):

| Aspect | ARC 60 windowed/borderless | ARC 80 windowed/borderless | any ARC, exclusive fullscreen | fullscreen horizontal stretch |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4:3 | 46.8 | 64.4 | = 4:3 value | ×1.000 |
| 5:4 | 49.6 | 67.7 | = 4:3 value | ×0.938 |
| 16:10 | 39.7 | 55.3 | = 4:3 value | ×1.200 |
| 16:9 | 36.0 | 50.5 | = 4:3 value | ×1.333 |
| 21:9 (64:27) | 27.4 | 39.0 | = 4:3 value | ×1.778 |
| 32:9 | 18.4 | 26.6 | = 4:3 value | ×2.667 |

So: windowed/borderless = **vertical cut (Vert-)**, square pixels; exclusive fullscreen = 4:3 vertical extent displayed across the wide screen = **anamorphic horizontal stretch**. **HIGH CONFIDENCE.** Independent corroboration: the patch's weapon-preview offsets are −37.5 (windowed/borderless: less vertical room, entity raised) and −52 (fullscreen: same vertical room as 4:3, essentially the original −50). **HIGH CONFIDENCE.**

The patch's default `K22.ini` is `Mode = 1` (exclusive fullscreen), i.e. the stretched variant. **CONFIRMED** (file).

### 1.2 UI positioning

Background art and full-screen panels are scaled to fill the window independently in X and Y; menus/HUD use the 1280×720 or 640×480 basis per state; subtitles sit at H − H/16. Nothing is pillar-boxed and no aspect-correct anchor exists. **CONFIRMED** (formulas above).

## 2. How native implements it

Native applies a recovered equivalent of the patch's display model to the **original ISO scripts**, without shipping patch scripts, art or DLLs (`CONTRACT.txt:2214-2223`). When the user's game directory contains `K22Widescreen.wrs`, native runs the patch's own scripts and leaves display handling to them.

| Element | Native code (working tree 2026-10-09) | Label |
|---|---|---|
| Admission | `Engine::configure_display` (`native/engine.cpp:693-749`): only the auto-selected original campaign `K22.wdl` whose `GA_Cozunurlukler`/`GA_ScaleOranlari{,2}`/`GA_FontOranlari` tables match the authored values and which lacks `dbg_screen_reset` (i.e. not already patched) | CONFIRMED |
| Mode/size | default borderless at desktop size; `--resolution` 1280×720 … 16384×16384; `--window-mode windowed|fullscreen|borderless`; `--display authored` restores original resolution services | CONFIRMED (`native/main.cpp` help text) |
| Art tier (`GA_Cozunurluk`) | Unlike the patch (which pins `GA_Cozunurluk` to 0), native owns slot 2 of the authored tables. The original scripts pick 1024-tier art when `GA_Cozunurluk>1` (`Kabusdismenu` `kan_1024`/eye positions, `YeniMenu`, `K22.wdl`, `PlayerEnerji`, `KoruView`, `kotu_koruyucu`), and every native size is ≥ 1280×720, so native sets `GA_Cozunurluk`=`GM_CursorCozunurluk`=2. `docs/WRS_FORMAT.md`:

```md
# WRS resource archive format (3D GameStudio A6/A7, as used by Kabus 22)

Labels: **CONFIRMED** / **HIGH CONFIDENCE** / **HYPOTHESIS** / **UNKNOWN**. Related: [ASSET_FORMATS](ASSET_FORMATS.md) §2 · [reverse-engineering/RESOURCE_FORMATS](reverse-engineering/RESOURCE_FORMATS.md) · [COMMUNITY_PATCH_ANALYSIS](COMMUNITY_PATCH_ANALYSIS.md) · [COMMUNITY_CREDITS](COMMUNITY_CREDITS.md).

Implementations compared: `tools/wrs2.py` (this project, Python), `native/assets.cpp` `Assets::mount`/`Assets::decompress`/`Assets::read` (this project, C++), iseeeva `kabus_tools` (`reverse/community/iseeeva-kabus22/kabus_tools/src/index.ts` + QuickBMS script `src/external/gamestudio.bms` by Luigi Auriemma), and the original engine file opener `K22.exe` `00420120` (`reverse/decompiled/K22.exe.00420120.c`).

## 1. Layout

```
offset 0   char[4]  magic        "WRS2" (A6 campaign) | "WRS3" (A7 Bonus)
then, repeated until end of file (no directory, no count, no trailer):
  +0       u8[32]   name         each byte XOR key; terminated by a raw 0x00, remaining bytes 0x00 (not XOR-ed)
  +32      u32 BE   packed size  bytes of LZSS stream that follow
  +36      u32 BE   output size  decoded size
  +40      u8[packed] LZSS stream
```

| Property | Value | Evidence | Label |
|---|---|---|---|
| Name key | `0xA5` for WRS2, `0xB5` for WRS3 | `gamestudio.bms`; `native/assets.cpp:258-265`; `tools/wrs2.py` | CONFIRMED |
| Byte order | big-endian sizes (unusual for an x86 engine) | all three implementations; every Kabus archive decodes | CONFIRMED |
| Empty member | packed = output = 0; mixed zero/non-zero rejected by both project readers | `tools/wrs2.py`, `native/assets.cpp:267` | CONFIRMED (readers); engine behaviour UNKNOWN |
| Name length | ≤ 32 bytes; longest observed 27 (`Kaynak.k22`) / 21 (`K22Widescreen.wrs`) | `wrs2.py list --json` | CONFIRMED |
| Separators | names are flat in every Kabus archive (no `/` or `\`); readers still normalise `\` → `/` and refuse `..`, absolute, device names | `tools/wrs2.py:safe_name`, `native/assets.cpp` `safe_name` | CONFIRMED |
| Integrity | none: no checksum, no signature, no encryption of member data; the name XOR is the only obfuscation | format above | CONFIRMED |

Other GameStudio variants handled only by QuickBMS (none occurs in Kabus 22): version byte `< '2'` derives a one-byte key from the first name assuming a 4-character `.ext` (`key = name[len-4] ^ '.'`); `"WRS4"` stores a big-endian index offset after the magic, an LZSS-compressed index of `{name[32]^0xAA, packed, size}` entries, and member data packed from offset 8. **CONFIRMED** (script text), unverified against real files.

## 2. Compression (LZSS)

Okumura LZSS, per member, no shared dictionary:

| Parameter | Value | Label |
|---|---|---|
| Ring buffer | 4096 bytes, initialised to `0x20` (space) | CONFIRMED |
| Initial write position | 4078 (= 4096 − 18) | CONFIRMED |
| Flag byte | 8 tokens, least-significant bit first; 1 = literal byte, 0 = reference | CONFIRMED |
| Reference | 2 bytes `lo, hi`: absolute ring position `lo | (hi & 0xF0) << 4`, length `(hi & 0x0F) + 3` (3…18) | CONFIRMED |
| Termination | stream ends when the packed byte count is consumed; output must equal the declared size | CONFIRMED |

Evidence: `tools/wrs2.py:decode_lzss`, `native/assets.cpp:278-295`; every member of all seven ISO archives (`K22.wrs` 182, `Kaynak.k22` 3 005, `yazi_{tr,en,de}.k22` 52 each, `ses_{tr,en}.k22` 14 each), the patch `K22Widescreen.wrs` (190) and the Lutris `K22.wrs` (179) decoded to the declared sizes with `tools/wrs2.py` during this analysis (`reverse/community/reports/wrs-index-*.txt`, `reverse/community/wrs/`). Compression ratio: `Kaynak.k22` 2 251 119 916 → 976 156 068 bytes; `K22Widescreen.wrs` 8 264 697 → 2 185 549. **CONFIRMED.**

## 3. Engine use

| Operation | Original A6 (`K22.exe`) | Label |
|---|---|---|
| Start-up archive | the executable's embedded base name (`.data 0x621240`: `K22`, patched `K22Widescreen`) selects `<name>.wrs` holding `<name>.wdl` | CONFIRMED (bytes + `0041fc00`) |
| Mounting | WDL `resource "file";` statements register more archives, in source order (`K22.wdl` line 1: `kaynak.k22`, then `yazi_xx.k22`, `ses_xx.k22` under `IFDEF defdil_*/defses_*`) | CONFIRMED (scripts) |
| Lookup | `00420120`: for non-`.WDL` names, a case-insensitive (`_stricmp`) scan of the registered table (entries of 32-byte name + data pointer, stride 0x24, `DAT_00695eb0`, count `DAT_006bb1c0`) returns the **first** match; only if none matches is a loose file opened (`_findfirst`) | HIGH CONFIDENCE (decompiled control flow) |
| Scripts | `.WDL` names take a separate branch controlled by start-up flags `0x62119c`/`0x621268` (archive mode vs protected loose sources, `"- script modified"`) | HIGH CONFIDENCE |

Native (`native/assets.cpp`, `native/main.cpp`):

| Operation | Native | Difference | Label |
|---|---|---|---|
| Loose files | every regular file under the data root is indexed case-insensitively at start (`Assets::Assets`, symlinks ignored) | — | CONFIRMED |
| Mount | `Assets::mount` scans headers, validates names/sizes/padding, rejects duplicates inside one archive and file/directory conflicts, then `insert_or_assign` (campaign) → **later archive wins**; Bonus uses `try_emplace` (first wins) | campaign precedence is the reverse of the original | CONFIRMED |
| Read | loose file first, archive entry second (`Assets::read`) | original: archive first | CONFIRMED |
| Mount order | `K22.wrs`, `Kaynak.k22`, `K22Widescreen.wrs` (each if present), then script `resource` statements (idempotent) | — | CONFIRMED |
| Observable today | duplicates across ISO + v1.8.5 archives: `PALETTE.RAW` (byte-identical in all six ISO archives) and `LY_Fade.bmp` (the patch copy wins in both models); no loose file shadows a member | none | CONFIRMED |

## 4. Tool comparison

| Capability | `tools/wrs2.py` | native `Assets` | iseeeva `kabus_tools` |
|---|---|---|---|
| List | yes (`list`, `--json`) | internal | via QuickBMS (`export` only) |
| Extract | yes, streaming, exclusive create, symlink-safe, 128 MiB default member cap | n/a | QuickBMS `-o` (overwrites) |
| Pack | no | no | yes: WRS2 only, flat directories only, names XOR `0xA5`, BE sizes, LZSS via QuickBMS `lzss_compress` |
| Versions | WRS2 | WRS2, WRS3 | read WRS1…4, write WRS2 |
| Validation | magic, truncation, padding, duplicates (casefold), unsafe paths, LZSS bounds | same class + per-asset size limit | none |
| Platform | any Python 3 | Linux build | Windows (`quickbms.exe`), Node ≥ 18 |

Observations on `kabus_tools` (all **CONFIRMED** from source unless noted):

- `import` runs QuickBMS with `-o` on each input file, writing the compressed result back over the **input file in the source directory**, then reads it from there: packing destroys the unpacked tree it was given. **HIGH CONFIDENCE** (QuickBMS writes `FNAME` into the output folder, which is the input folder).
- The name-length check rejects > 32 bytes but the message says "36 bytes or fewer"; a 32-byte name is written without terminator (both project readers accept it).
- An empty directory produces a zero-length file without magic.
- QuickBMS `lzss_compress` output compatibility with the engine's decoder is assumed by the author's workflow; no project test covers it. **HYPOTHESIS.**

Decision: no new Linux tool was added. The only capability missing from `tools/wrs2.py` is packing, and the native engine does not need repacked archives — loose files under the game root already take precedence over archive members (`Assets::read`). **CONFIRMED** (code); see [COMMUNITY_PATCH_ANALYSIS](COMMUNITY_PATCH_ANALYSIS.md) §7.2 for the precedence caveat.

## 5. Verification run

```
$ python3 tools/check_wrs2.py
WRS2 checks passed            (exit 0, 2026-10-09)
```

`tools/check_wrs2.py` covers LZSS literal/reference decoding, space-initialised window, truncated/oversized streams, magic, padding, duplicate and case-folded names, unsafe paths and exclusive extraction. **CONFIRMED.**

```md
# Recovered Data Structures

Purpose: in-memory and on-disk layouts recovered from K22.exe (A6 6.31.4), the A7 Bonus engine and the game scripts, with their native counterparts.

Related: [REVERSE_ENGINEERING.md](../REVERSE_ENGINEERING.md) (index) · [SCRIPT_SYSTEM.md](SCRIPT_SYSTEM.md) · [FUNCTION_MAP.md](FUNCTION_MAP.md) · [RESOURCE_FORMATS.md](RESOURCE_FORMATS.md) · [../ENGINE_ARCHITECTURE.md](../ENGINE_ARCHITECTURE.md) · [../ASSET_FORMATS.md](../ASSET_FORMATS.md)

Conventions:
- Addresses are VAs in the analysed patched `K22.exe` (image base `0x00400000`, SHA256 `1a6a0dbc…7bed`). See [`CONTRACT.txt:1-10`](../../reverse/decompiled/runtime/CONTRACT.txt).
- Decompiled paths are relative to `reverse/decompiled/runtime/` unless they start with `../`.
- Offsets are hexadecimal bytes.
- **Native does not reproduce these byte layouts.** `native/value.hpp` stores objects as named field maps (`Object::fields`, `CaseLess` keys). Native columns therefore name the equivalent symbol, not an offset.

## 1. Archive (WRS) tables

Source: [`RECOVERY.txt:37-67`](../../reverse/decompiled/RECOVERY.txt); [`../loaders/K22.exe.0041fd20.c`](../../reverse/decompiled/loaders/K22.exe.0041fd20.c), [`../loaders/K22.exe.0041ff20.c`](../../reverse/decompiled/loaders/K22.exe.0041ff20.c).

### 1.1 Entry table `0x00665ea8` (stride 0x30, limit 0x1000 entries)
| Offset | Size | Type | Meaning | Evidence | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| +0x00 | 0x20 | char[32] | XOR-decoded member name, NUL-terminated | `0041fd20.c` copy loop into `&DAT_00665ea8 + count*0x30` | CONFIRMED |
| +0x20 | 4 | int | Archive slot (index into the handle table) | `(&DAT_00665ec8)[i*0xc] = param_1` | CONFIRMED |
| +0x24 | 4 | long | Payload file offset (`ftell` after the header) | `(&DAT_00665ecc)[i*0xc] = ftell` | CONFIRMED |
| +0x28 | 4 | u32 | Stored (packed) length, read big-endian; also the seek distance | `(&DAT_00665ed0)[i*0xc]` | CONFIRMED |
| +0x2c | 4 | u32 | Decoded length, read big-endian; `0xffffffff` ends the index | `(&DAT_00665ed4)[i*0xc]`; loop `while(uVar7!=0xffffffff)` | CONFIRMED |

| Address | Size | Type | Meaning | Evidence | Confidence |

Native also accepts a `WRS3`/0xB5 variant and loops to EOF instead of stopping at the 0xffffffff marker (CONFIRMED by code reading). On-disk format: [RESOURCE_FORMATS.md](RESOURCE_FORMATS.md).

### 5.2 Member descriptor tables
`member-descriptors.json` (consumer `004015c0`, stride 20; constructors `005ce400` …) covers 8 kinds. Each row holds a name, byte offset, value type code, flags, and mask or index bound. Type codes seen: 16 numeric member and 17 bit property (mask in last word), both CONFIRMED (§6 `:255-256`). The pointer-typed codes are inferred from member names (HIGH CONFIDENCE): 1 entity, 5 string, 6 function, 7 font, 8 bmap, 11 panel, 18 view, 19 material. Separately, type 3 means local/array values resolving to `+0x10` (§11 `:414`). Full rows are in [`member-descriptors.json`](../../reverse/decompiled/runtime/member-descriptors.json). The JSON preserves offsets as recovery evidence; it is **not** a native ABI (§6 `:257`).

#### VECTOR, numeric array, STRING
- VECTOR (`0x00620b88`): X/PAN/BLUE `+0x4`, Y/TILT/GREEN `+0x8`, Z/ROLL/RED `+0xc`.
- Numeric array (`0x00620c80`): header word `+0x0` (info `0x01000000`, nsave `0x10000000`), length `+0xc`, elements from `+0x10` (X..W/A up to `+0x1c`). Its element offsets match the local objects in §4.
- STRING (`0x00620dac`): INVISIBLE is mask `0x2` at `+0x14`.
- **CONFIRMED.** Native maps these to `Object::Kind::Vector` `array[0..2]` via `core_alias` (`native/engine.cpp`).

Native: no PE ABI. `Engine::initialize_plugins` and `svc_plugin_open` set `pluginNative`/`pluginGamma`, and `iniValues` holds the K22.ini map.

## 8. Persistence formats (as consumed by scripts)

All game files below are written through WDL `file_*` calls, not engine save APIs. No `game_save`/`game_load` call appears in the extracted original scripts (grep, CONFIRMED). `file_asc_write` emits one byte per value. Native (`Engine::service_builtin`) writes the low byte of `raw>>10`, and `file_asc_read` returns 0..255 or −1 at EOF. Native files live under `$XDG_DATA_HOME/kabus22` (default `~/.local/share/kabus22`; `Engine` `saveRoot`) via `svc_private`. Reads fall back to read-only archive/game assets.

### 8.3 Bonus `mode_ayarlar.k22` (5 text lines)
Reader `K22_mode.wdl` (ISO, `reverse/media/iso/mode/scripts/K22_mode.wrs/K22_mode.wdl:428-442`) uses `txt_load` + `str_to_num` per line. Row 0 is `GA_Cozunurluk`. Row 1 is `GA_Shader_Seviyesi`. Row 2 is anisotropy (1→2 → `d3d_anisotropy`). Row 3 is `muzik_cal_ok`. Row 4 is brightness, used as `cbt_ekran_parlaklik = value-50`. **CONFIRMED** (script). The shipped `game/Kabus 22 Mode/mode_ayarlar.k22` bytes are `2\r\n2\r\n0\r\n1\r\n50` (xxd, CONFIRMED). Native validator: `installer/launcher_settings.cpp` `decodeBonus` (ranges 0..3/0..2/0..1/0..1). Observed native consumption: second-series CONTRACT §42 `:2383-2385` (rows `2/2/0/1/55`).

### 8.4 `K22.ini` (patch plugin)
An INI map owned by `kabus_dll.dll`. Native: `svc_ini_load`/`svc_ini_parse`/`svc_ini_save` (`native/engine.cpp`) store `section:key` in `Engine::iniValues` and normalise `Screen:Mode` (≤2), `Screen:X` (≤3840) and `Screen:Y` (≤2160). The native normalisation is CONFIRMED by code. Original plugin semantics are in `RECOVERY.txt:102-104` (CONFIRMED); the bounds come from the native code only (HIGH CONFIDENCE they mirror patch expectations, not independently recovered).

## Script provenance caveat

The WDL scripts used for most citations in `reverse/extracted/original/` were extracted from the Lutris install's `K22.wrs`, not the ISO `K22.wrs` (`c9e32008…`); ISO copies live in `reverse/media/iso/scripts/` and `reverse/media/iso/script-comparison.json` reports 173 of 182 files identical. **CONFIRMED** (comparison file). The native port ships no scripts; it reads them from the user's installed ISO data.

- **UNKNOWN**: the exact engine build of `setup.exe` ("Kabus 22 Test") — different `K22.exe` MD5, not analysed.
- **UNKNOWN**: what the `.data` fields changed at `0x621190` by the community patch control.
- **UNKNOWN**: A6 consumer of the statically linked zlib.
- **HYPOTHESIS**: Kabus22.exe (Multimedia Builder) launches `K22.exe`; the packed launcher was not unpacked.
