```md
# Executable analysis

Static PE facts for the original Kabus 22 ISO edition and the community patch, with SHA-256 values computed for this document (2026-10-09).

Related: [REVERSE_ENGINEERING index](../REVERSE_ENGINEERING.md) · [ENGINE_IDENTIFICATION](ENGINE_IDENTIFICATION.md) · [FUNCTION_MAP](FUNCTION_MAP.md) · [RESOURCE_FORMATS](RESOURCE_FORMATS.md) · [ENGINE_ARCHITECTURE](../ENGINE_ARCHITECTURE.md)

Confidence labels: **CONFIRMED** (file bytes / decompiled code), **HIGH CONFIDENCE**, **HYPOTHESIS**, **UNKNOWN**. Paths under `reverse/` are private workspace evidence (only `reverse/scripts/*.java` is published, see `.gitignore`). No original executable was run; all facts below come from reading bytes.

## Method (reproducible)

1. ISO members were listed with `7z l "Kabus-22_Win_TR-EN-DE_ISO-Version/Kabus 22.iso"` and copied into a private temporary directory (deleted afterwards).
2. Inno Setup payload was inspected and selectively extracted with the pinned helper `packaging/helper-innoextract/bin/amd64/innoextract` (innoextract 1.9): `-i JPN-K22.exe`, `--list --list-sizes`, `--extract -I app/K22.exe …`.
3. PE headers, sections, imports/exports, Rich header and version resources were parsed with Python `pefile` 2024.8.26; hashes with `hashlib.sha256`. `objcopy` was never run on originals.
4. Integrity check: MD5 and size of every hashed file were compared with the installer's own checksums recorded in `reverse/media/iso/list-exact.txt` (innoextract `--list-checksums`). **CONFIRMED** 79/79 match.

## Edition identification

| Item | Value | Confidence / evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Disc image | `Kabus 22.iso`, 2,089,629,632 data bytes in 76 files; volume id `K22_Y_K_MG`, App Id `NERO BURNING ROM` | CONFIRMED: `reverse/media/iso/iso-volume.txt`, `7z l` |
| ISO SHA-256 | `0fb722388128a9c2ebd7e15849ec0392eab752b5622dd4375ff0580a336b5df1` | CONFIRMED (computed) |
| Distribution zip SHA-256 | `Kabus-22_Win_TR-EN-DE_ISO-Version.zip` `e303ed28e86934bbd920ee5480a77dfca5ba17bb720f240ab7ce48cca420550e` | CONFIRMED (computed) |
| Installer | Inno Setup "Kabus 22 Multi 3", setup data version 5.2.1, languages english/german/turkce | CONFIRMED: `reverse/media/iso/info.txt`, `data-version.txt` |
| Installer build dates | ISO members dated 2008-03-08 (`JPN-K22*.bin/.exe`); bundled DirectX redistributable cabs up to `JUN2007_*` | CONFIRMED: `7z l` |
| Copyright string | `KABUS 22 © 2008 SON ISIK LTD.` in `Kabus22.exe` version resource | CONFIRMED (pefile) |

ISO installer sources (computed):

| ISO member | Size | SHA-256 |

Role notes:
- `K22.exe` is the campaign engine itself (`A6 engine` / `6.31.4` strings, see [ENGINE_IDENTIFICATION](ENGINE_IDENTIFICATION.md)). It has no version resource (`.rsrc` virtual size `0x10`) and no debug directory. **CONFIRMED**. Its entry `0x5bb38b` is the MSVC CRT start-up exported as `reverse/decompiled/K22.exe.005bb38b.c` / `reverse/decompiled/runtime/K22.exe.005bb38b.c`. **CONFIRMED**.
- `Kabus22.exe`: `UPX0/UPX1` sections, `2.01\0UPX!` marker, version resource `Comments="Created with Multimedia Builder version 4.9.7.8"`, `FileVersion 6.11.0000.1`, `CompanyName SON ISIK LTD.`. **CONFIRMED** packed menu/autorun launcher, not the engine. That it starts `K22.exe` is **HYPOTHESIS** (packed code not unpacked; `reverse/decompiled/RECOVERY.txt` "Engine version" paragraph explicitly does not generalise to it).
- `Kabus 22 Mode/Kabus22_mode.exe` (`FileVersion 1.0.4.0`) is the same Multimedia Builder/UPX family; its zlib overlay at file offset `0x7f618` decodes to launcher records that start `<SrcDir>\K22_mode.exe`. **CONFIRMED**: `reverse/decompiled/runtime/bonus-core/entry/entry-contract.txt` lines 7-14.
- `K22_mode.exe` `WinMain 0x00401000` calls `engine_open`, loops `engine_frame`, then `engine_close`, imported from `acknex.dll` (IAT `0x004050c4/c8/cc`). **CONFIRMED**: imports above + `entry-contract.txt` line 13.
- `K22_0.dll`: sections `CODE/DATA/BSS`, linker 2.25, timestamp `0x2A425E19` (1992-06-19) — the fixed Borland Delphi stamp; exports `A5_DLLAPI`, `HTTP_Create/Free/Get/IsWorking/Post/Results/SaveToFile`. **CONFIRMED** exports; Delphi origin **HIGH CONFIDENCE**. Online Bonus features use it; the native port implements no network path (`entry-contract.txt` line 30).
- `RenkAyar.dll` and `Kabus 22 Mode/K22_1.dll` are byte-identical (SHA-256 `9c9e9ea6…a09a3e`); exports `A6_DLLAPI`, `dl_PaKaGa`, `dl_Reset`. **CONFIRMED**. Behaviour: `reverse/decompiled/RenkAyar.behavior.txt`.
- `OggDS0995.exe` (2002) is the third-party OggDS DirectShow filter installer shipped for Ogg playback. **HIGH CONFIDENCE** (filename; not unpacked).

DirectX evidence for `K22.exe` (**CONFIRMED** unless noted):
- Only `Direct3DCreate9` from `d3d9.dll`, `DirectInput8Create` from `DINPUT8.dll`, `DSOUND.dll` ordinals 1/2 (`DirectSoundCreate`/`DirectSoundEnumerateA` by ordinal — **HIGH CONFIDENCE** ordinal mapping).
- D3DX9 is statically linked: strings `Microsoft (R) D3DX9 Shader Compiler 5.04.00.2904`, `Microsoft (R) D3DX9 Shader Assembler 5.04.00.2904`, `Direct3DShaderValidatorCreate9`, shader profiles `vs_1_0…vs_2_0`, `ps_1_0…ps_3_0`; no `d3dx9_*.dll` import. Mapping of D3DX 5.04.00.2904 to a specific DirectX SDK release is **HYPOTHESIS** (2004-era DirectX 9.0c SDK).
- String `DirectX 9.0c` present. Joystick via WINMM `joyGetPosEx`/`joyGetDevCapsA` and DirectInput8; CD/MCI via `mciSendCommandA`; timing via `timeGetTime`/`timeSetEvent`/`timeBeginPeriod`. **CONFIRMED** imports.
- `WSOCK32` (`gethostbyname`, `gethostname`, `inet_ntoa`) for the engine's multiplayer/session layer (`Acknex Session` string). Not used by the native port. **CONFIRMED** imports; use **HIGH CONFIDENCE**.
- zlib `inflate 1.1.4 Copyright 1995-2002 Mark Adler` is statically linked (`zlib error` strings). Its consumer inside the engine is **UNKNOWN** (WRS payloads use LZSS, not zlib: [RESOURCE_FORMATS](RESOURCE_FORMATS.md)).
- ODE strings `ODE INTERNAL ERROR %d` (file offset `0x20dcd0`) and `ODE Message` plus `ph_setgravity`, `ph_setautodisable`, `ph_selectgroup` script-API names. **CONFIRMED** strings; that A6 physics is built on the Open Dynamics Engine is **HIGH CONFIDENCE**.
```

```md
- K22.exe PE sections (parsed from the analyzed file): `.text` 0x00401000–0x005cf7bd, `.rdata` 0x005d0000–0x0061a976, `.data` 0x0061b000–0x00733938, `.rsrc` 0x00734000–. Addresses in `.text` are code; `.rdata`/`.data` addresses are listed under [Globals/data addresses](#3-globals--data-addresses). **CONFIRMED** (PE header read; hashes from `K22.exe.recovery.txt:5`, `kabus_dll.dll.recovery.txt:5`, `RenkAyar.dll.recovery.txt:5`, `runtime/bonus-physics/api-descriptors.json`).
- All 179 K22.exe manifest/report header blocks and all 293 acknex.dll header blocks under `reverse/decompiled/` carry the single hashes above. The ISO `K22.exe` (`cc193c6b…`) is not packed and differs from the analysed patched build only in six `.text` bytes at `0x4139bb`, `0x413a7e`, `0x42027e` (start-up/archive branches) plus `.data`/resources; `.rdata` is identical, so addresses below apply to the ISO build (**CONFIRMED**, [EXECUTABLE_ANALYSIS](EXECUTABLE_ANALYSIS.md#community-patch-binaries-not-part-of-the-iso), `CONTRACT.txt:2147-2154`). Only the UPX-packed launchers `Kabus22.exe`/`Kabus22_mode.exe` are unanalysed (**UNKNOWN**).
- All DLLs share preferred base 0x10000000, so a `10xxxxxx` address is ambiguous without the Binary column.
- Evidence paths are relative to `reverse/decompiled/` (e.g. `runtime/trace/K22.exe.00404b60.c:8-17`). `CONTRACT §N (Lx)` = [`runtime/CONTRACT.txt`](../../reverse/decompiled/runtime/CONTRACT.txt) section N, line x; `§39b`–`§42b` are the second numbering starting at line 2139. `RECOVERY.txt` = [`reverse/decompiled/RECOVERY.txt`](../../reverse/decompiled/RECOVERY.txt). Native paths are relative to `native/` unless prefixed.
- **Parameters** = Ghidra signature (`u`=undefined, `pN`=param_N). Ghidra omits register arguments (`CONTRACT.txt:9`), so arity is approximate.
- **Callers/Callees** are computed only from `FUN_xxxxxxxx` references inside the exported `.c` files (2278 exports), so they are partial: absence means "not seen in exports", not "none". `—` = no export for that address.
- **Native** names a symbol only when verified by reading current source (comment citing the address, or matching behavior noted in the cell). Line numbers are omitted because `native/` is being edited concurrently. "behavioral substitute" = same observable contract, different mechanism.
- Confidence: **CONFIRMED** (decompiled C/ASM, file bytes, or descriptor table), **HIGH CONFIDENCE** (strong indirect), **HYPOTHESIS**, **UNKNOWN**.

Coverage: 253 distinct addresses cited in CONTRACT.txt (all appear below: 188 function rows incl. RECOVERY.txt/DLL exports, 24 instruction sites, 105 data rows); 2278 distinct decompiled export addresses (K22.exe 823, acknex.dll 1314, kabus_dll.dll 129, RenkAyar.dll 7, K22_mode.exe 5); those not annotated in §1 are listed in §5.

## 6. Gaps and discrepancies found while building this map

- `0055c152` (system-error-name mapping) never decompiled: every run timed out (`final/K22.exe.recovery.txt` status FAILED timed_out=true). **CONFIRMED** gap.
- `00402530` (action-name resolver) and `00470a50` (modern trace hull builder) are cited in CONTRACT.txt but have no `.c` export; their parameters are **UNKNOWN**.
- `0044b770` (frame step skipped under FREEZE_MODE>=1) has an export but its purpose is not described anywhere. **UNKNOWN**.
- FLOATR `00406fe0` and FLOATD `00407010` are recovered handlers whose names are present in `native/native_calls.inc`, but no native implementation branch was found in `engine.cpp`/`wdl.cpp`. **CONFIRMED** by search of current source.
- Native fixed-point `/` and `%` throw on a zero divisor (`wdl.cpp` `Runtime::Impl::evaluate`), whereas `0040aba0` emits an unguarded IDIV (x86 divide exception; engine policy unrecovered, `CONTRACT.txt:184-185`). **CONFIRMED** difference.
- Native `str_clip` throws on negative counts; original `00404780` has no clamp (undefined memory behavior, `CONTRACT.txt:562-568`). **CONFIRMED** difference (deliberate).
- Native `Assets::mount` accepts WRS2 (0xa5) and WRS3 (0xb5) only; original `0041fd20` also accepts a legacy 12-char/XOR-0 index. WRS3 is the Bonus archive format (`Kabus 22 Mode/K22_mode.wrs` begins with bytes `WRS3`; campaign `K22.wrs` begins `WRS2`, read from the extracted install); the acknex.dll loader that uses the 0xb5 key is not mapped here. **CONFIRMED** difference; A7 loader address **UNKNOWN**.
- CONTRACT §18 (L705-709) records native gaps (VECTOR allocation, left-to-right call args) that current source has closed: `Engine::service_builtin` uses a 64-entry `vectorTemps_` ring and `Runtime::Impl::evaluate` evaluates call arguments from last to first. **CONFIRMED** by reading current source.
- acknex.dll (A7) has 1314 exports, mostly unannotated here beyond directory topic; their contracts live in the per-directory `contract.txt`/manifest files.
- Callers/callees are export-local; a full call graph would need a new read-only Ghidra pass.


```

`docs/reverse-engineering/ORIGINAL_BEHAVIOR.md`:

```md
# Original Behavior Catalog

Purpose: catalog what is known about the behavior of the original Kabus 22 game and what the native port has actually been observed doing when it runs the original scripts. Each item keeps **Observed**, with an evidence path, separate from **Assumed**.

Related: [Reverse-engineering index](../REVERSE_ENGINEERING.md) · [Engine architecture](../ENGINE_ARCHITECTURE.md) · [Gameplay systems](../GAMEPLAY_SYSTEMS.md) · [Camera system](../CAMERA_SYSTEM.md) · [Script system](SCRIPT_SYSTEM.md) · [Executable analysis](EXECUTABLE_ANALYSIS.md) · [Function map](FUNCTION_MAP.md)

## How to read this catalog

Until 2026-10-09 the original Windows executable was never run for this project; since then the unmodified ISO `K22.exe` has been run under Wine as a reference tool (rows labelled **Original observed (Wine)**, evidence under `../../reverse/wine-reference/`, method in [REVERSE_ENGINEERING](../REVERSE_ENGINEERING.md#dynamic-analysis-original-under-wine)). Everything stated about the original binary (`K22.exe`, Acknex A6 6.31.4, campaign; and the A7 runtime behind Bonus mode `Kabus 22 Mode/K22_mode.wrs`) comes from three kinds of source:

- **Static analysis.** This covers read-only Ghidra exports and paired C/ASM files under `../../reverse/decompiled/`, summarized in [`CONTRACT.txt`](../../reverse/decompiled/runtime/CONTRACT.txt). The contract's own header states: "No game execution … runtime observation". Static analysis was done on the patched `K22.exe` (SHA-256 `1a6a0dbc…`). The digest-qualified ISO `K22.exe` (`cc193c6b…`) differs from it only in 6 startup/archive-path bytes of `.text` (`CONTRACT.txt:2147-2149`).
- **Original script text.** The reference copy is in `../../reverse/extracted/original/`. The ISO edition is in `../../reverse/media/iso/scripts/`, and 173 of its 182 files are byte-identical to the reference copy.
- **Community material.** Kabus22Patch 1.8.5 and a third-party repository are inventoried under `../../reverse/community/` (reports in `../../reverse/community/reports/summary.json`). Their behavior was not independently executed on Windows either.

"Native observed" means a recorded run of the Linux native engine against original game data. Most walked campaign runs used an **ISO + Kabus22Patch** installation, whose entry archive is the patch `K22Widescreen.wrs` (`../../reverse/campaign-pointer-fixed-input-ledger.json`, `asset_archive_identity`). ISO-only runs are marked as such. The label "(ISO+patch)" means the patched scripts were driving the game.

Labels:

- **CONFIRMED**: direct evidence.
- **HIGH CONFIDENCE**: strong indirect evidence.
- **HYPOTHESIS**: plausible but not checked.
- **UNKNOWN**: the evidence needed to decide is missing.

## 1. Startup and bootstrap

| | Statement | Evidence | Label |
|---|---|---|---|
| Original (static) | The engine compiles scripts, then enumerates plugins (`004133c0` called from `00413990`), then queues MAIN first and STARTER functions in reverse first-creation order. MAIN runs until its first yield, then the starters run. | `CONTRACT.txt:475-499` (§13) | CONFIRMED (static) |
| Original (script) | `K22.wdl main()` runs in this order: `sleep(1)`; `anactrl_ok` gate (defined through `IFDEF defiae_d3d`); `wait(1)`; `GA_AyarlariYukle` (reads `options.k22`); `video_switch(GA_Cozunurluk+6,…)`; volume globals; `dll_open("RenkAyar.dll")` with `dl_PaKaGa`; `d3d_*` settings; `Level_Load(analevel_wmb)` (`level0.wmb`); `fps_max=72`, `fps_min=24`; `Menu_AcilisEkrani()`. | `../../reverse/extracted/original/K22.wdl:646-689` | CONFIRMED |
| Original (static) | `level_load` only records a pending command (bit 8). The load runs after the current frame's script phase and does not yield. | `CONTRACT.txt:501-508` | CONFIRMED (static) |
| Native observed | ISO-only installation, 600 frames: 179 WDL files, 1857 functions and 93139 statements parsed. The run exits 0 after showing the authentic publisher bitmap PANEL ("FIP PUBLISHING") at 1024×768. | `CONTRACT.txt:1773-1779`, `:2099-2104` (receipts in a private cache, not in the repository) | CONFIRMED |
| Native observed | Before the logo, the screen is black because `Menu_AcilisEkrani` sleeps before showing the logo. A GDB snapshot at frame 239 shows the process waiting in that `SLEEP`, with no movie and no UI. | `CONTRACT.txt:1691-1700` | CONFIRMED |
| Native observed | `../../reverse/native-iso-campaign-start.png` (1024×768) shows the "A SON ISIK Studios game" logo. `../../reverse/native-iso-menu.png` is entirely black and is **not** menu evidence. | image files | CONFIRMED (contents inspected) |
| Native design | `Engine::initialize_plugins` runs after `Runtime::load` and before `Engine::configure_language` and `Runtime::bootstrap` (`native/main.cpp`). The PE DLLs are replaced by compiled providers. | `CONTRACT.txt:480-486`; grep | CONFIRMED |
| Original observed (Wine) | ISO `K22.exe` under Wine 11.19/wined3d, 1024×768 windowed: FIP PUBLISHING fades in over 1.1 s, holds 2.9 s, fades out over 2.0 s; 0.9 s black; SON ISIK fades in 1.1 s, holds 1.9 s, fades out 2.0 s (mean-luma timeline of the recording). This matches the script arithmetic (12.5 s) and native (logo visible frame 177, menu frame 925). The main menu then appears ~7 s later under Wine (DirectShow start of `kn_arg.k22`), versus ~1 s natively. | `../../reverse/wine-reference/explore1/startup.mp4`, `startup-sheet.png`, `acklog.txt` | CONFIRMED |
| Original observed (Wine) | Main menu layout (logo, NEW GAME…EXIT, eyes) matches native `--display authored` 1024×768; the red background is the looping movie, so frames differ by loop phase. | `../../reverse/wine-reference/menus/pair-*.png` | CONFIRMED (inspected) |

The logo sequence comes from `Menu_AcilisEkrani` (`K22.wdl:586`) on PANEL `Menu_Acilis` (layer 100). It shows `Vestel_Kabus22` (`Vestel_sunar.tga`) and then `LastLight_Kbs22` (`SONISIK_LOGO.tga`), with fades driven by `sleep` and `wait` (`K22.wdl:511-515`, `:586-645`). The patch variant does the same in `K22Widescreen.wdl:566-624` (`CONTRACT.txt:1691-1694`). **CONFIRMED**

## 4. Difficulty

- **Original (script).** `YeniMenu.wdl:135 YeniOyunBaslat(_Zorluk)` takes 0 for Normal and 1 for Hard. Enemy health and damage scale by `(OyunZorluk+1)`. See [Gameplay systems §11](../GAMEPLAY_SYSTEMS.md#11-difficulty). **CONFIRMED**
- **Native observed.** The Normal selection screen and the chosen Normal path were captured: `../../reverse/campaign-checkpoint-normal-difficulty.png`, `../../reverse/native-gl-resume2-difficulty.png`. **CONFIRMED**
- **Hard.** No run recorded. **UNKNOWN**

## 5. FIP publisher panel at 1024×768

- **Native observed, ISO-only historical artifact.** The installed engine kept the scripts' authored 4:3 mode and captured a 1024×768 framebuffer showing the FIP bitmap PANEL (`CONTRACT.txt:1776-1782`, `:2103-2104`). **CONFIRMED**
- **Native observed, v0.1.1 and later.** Native desktop borderless display captured the same panel at 2560×1440 in GL, Vulkan raster and Vulkan RT (`CONTRACT.txt:2253-2256`, `:2091-2094`). With the patch, 5120×2880 and 3840×2160 captures were also made (`:1592-1593`, `:1624`). **CONFIRMED**
- **Assumed.** 1024×768 comes from `GA_Cozunurluk` in the shipped `options.k22` (31 bytes in the installed game directory) through `video_switch(GA_Cozunurluk+6,…)`. **HIGH CONFIDENCE**: the script path is confirmed, but the value decoded from that file is not recorded in this repository.

## 6. Frame pacing and time

| | Statement | Evidence | Label |
|---|---|---|---|
| Original (static) | The nominal tick is 1/16 s. The raw quantum is 1/1024 tick, derived from QPC with a `timeGetTime` fallback. TIME is clamped between 51 raw and 16/FPS_MIN, scaled by TIME_FACTOR, and smoothed with TIME_SMOOTH (default 0.5 in this binary). | `CONTRACT.txt:103-123` (§3) | CONFIRMED (static) |
| Original (static) | `WAIT(n<=0)` is a one-frame yield. `freeze_mode` ≥1 lets only MY==NULL records run; ≥2 stops scheduling. | `CONTRACT.txt:71-133` | CONFIRMED (static) |
| Original (static) | `00414650` sleeps and rechecks against FPS_MAX before publishing TIME_FRAME, whether or not FPS_LOCK is set. | `CONTRACT.txt:1526-1528` (§38) | CONFIRMED (static) |
| Original (script) | The campaign sets `fps_max=72` and `fps_min=24`. | `K22.wdl` `main` | CONFIRMED |
| Original observed (Wine) | The campaign runs at the FPS_MAX 72 cap (TIME 0.223 every frame in cam1/kriz). Player run speed (~9.9 quants/tick), turn rate (12.6°/tick) and atilgan contact damage (4·TIME·(OyunZorluk+1) per wing trace) are per tick and equal to native at 60 fps (TIME 0.268); with the same pan, cam1 glide legs end within 0.6 quants of native. Under Wine every key hold reaches the game about one frame long (release latency); the driver compensates. | Per-frame `diag` instrumentation, [GAMEPLAY_TESTING](../GAMEPLAY_TESTING.md#bugs-fixed) fix 18 | CONFIRMED (Wine) |
| Native | `native/main.cpp` sleeps until `floor(1000·1024·1024 / max(FPS_MAX raw,1024))` raw milliseconds after the frame start, without accumulating catch-up debt. `Engine::tick` reproduces the TIME arithmetic. | grep; `CONTRACT.txt:1528-1534` | CONFIRMED |
| Native observed | An asset-free consumer gave 50.049 ms at FPS_MAX 20, 25.024 ms at FPS_MAX 40, and saturated at 1000 ms for zero or negative values. A dynamic change from 20 to 40 was exercised. The packaged build was also checked. | `CONTRACT.txt:1566-1569`, `:1686-1689`, `:2106-2108`; tool `tools/check_frame_pacing.py` | CONFIRMED |
| Not established | Steady campaign FPS and CPU use; comparison with Windows frame timing. | `CONTRACT.txt:1549-1551`, `:1861-1863` | UNKNOWN |

## 8. Input

| | Statement | Evidence | Label |
|---|---|---|---|
| Original (static) | Keyboard state uses scancode = `(lParam>>16)&0x7f`. A down edge fires only when the key goes from up to held, so auto-repeat is ignored. A short tap is published as 1024 for one frame. Joystick codes are 256-279; mouse codes are 280-282. | `CONTRACT.txt:433-449` (§12) | CONFIRMED (static) |
| Original (static) | Embedded `engine_internal.wdl` binds F2 save, F3 load, F5 video, F6 screenshot, F10/ESC/CLOSE exit, F12 sound toggle and ENTER screen toggle. Game scripts may replace these bindings. | `CONTRACT.txt:468-470`; `../../reverse/extracted/engine_internal.wdl` | CONFIRMED (static) |
| Original (script) | Keys can be remapped through `GA_Tuslar`. The default map key is slot 8, scancode 35 (H). | `GenelAyarlar.wdl:37,50,115` | CONFIRMED; H mapping HIGH CONFIDENCE |
| Native observed | Holding H set native `Input` bit 11, then `KEY_H`=`Key_Harita`=1024 one frame later, and the original map opened (`h_menu_aktifmi`=1, `freeze_mode`=1). | `../../reverse/native-gl-input-debug-held-map.png`; `CONTRACT.txt:926-931` | CONFIRMED |

| Test-method limit | Short synthetic key taps (xdotool `--delay`) often missed the original held/release loops. This is not evidence of an input defect. | `CONTRACT.txt:892`, `:904-906`, `:936-937` | CONFIRMED (methodology) |
| Original (static) | Joystick polling `00422000` (`ev_f91758961be5402cfccd9f4a5eff19d358738d56a3a07a9dd4273842401e3008`; keyword table: `JOY_FORCE` → `0x665d98`, `JOY_RAW` → `0x665864`, `JOY_ROT` → `0x665850`, `JOY_SENSE` → `0x665d60`, default 1). `JOY_RAW`/`JOY_ROT` axes are `(pos·255)/range − 255`, i.e. −255…255. `JOY_FORCE.x` = trunc(dz(raw)·`JOY_SENSE`·0.02f) (constant `0x5d63ac` = 0.02f), `.y` the same negated, with a dead zone dz of 32 (raw − 32 sign-wise, 0 inside), then clamped to ±2·`JOY_SENSE`. `.z` is never written. A full stick gives 2.0, so `Joy_Takip`'s `JOY_Ileri = joy_force.y/2` (`GenelAyarlar.wdl:75`) is exactly 1 and `Key_Ileri==1` walks; below about 52% deflection (raw < 132) it is fractional and does not. | REA ID at left; `K22.exe` keyword table at file offset `0x1d5500` | CONFIRMED (static) |
| Native observed | Live virtual pad, original mode: half stick (raw −102) gives `JOY_Ileri` 0.699 and no movement; full stick gives `JOY_Ileri` 1 and walks within 3 frames (fix 24). | `tools/virtual-gamepad/live/original.k22s`; `check_engine --input-saves` | CONFIRMED |

## 14. Physics and collision behavior in the campaign

- **Native observed.** In Start4, held A+Up stopped against a corpse entity. Against a wall with normal (0,-1,0) the player glided. At a two-plane corner the velocity dropped to zero with no passthrough, and Down escaped the corner (`CONTRACT.txt:2312-2324`). **CONFIRMED**
- **Original A6.** The `c_trace USE_BOX` input preparation was recovered from `00472030` and `00470a50` (`CONTRACT.txt:1988-1993`). A static replay of the legacy BSP reproduces a Start6 trace result of raw -1024 with Normal 0 (`:1999-2002`). **CONFIRMED (static)**. Bit-level parity of the oriented solver is not claimed.
```

`docs/reverse-engineering/RESOURCE_FORMATS.md`:

```md
# Resource formats (original on-disk layouts)

Purpose: byte-level description of every file format shipped with or written by the original Kabus 22 (K22.exe, Acknex A6 6.31.4 campaign; A7 Bonus mode in `Kabus 22 Mode/`), with the evidence behind each statement.

Related: [REVERSE_ENGINEERING index](../REVERSE_ENGINEERING.md) · [ASSET_FORMATS (native consumption)](../ASSET_FORMATS.md) · [DATA_STRUCTURES](DATA_STRUCTURES.md) · [FUNCTION_MAP](FUNCTION_MAP.md) · [SCRIPT_SYSTEM](SCRIPT_SYSTEM.md) · [ORIGINAL_BEHAVIOR](ORIGINAL_BEHAVIOR.md) · [ENGINE_ARCHITECTURE](../ENGINE_ARCHITECTURE.md)

Confidence labels: **CONFIRMED** = decompiled code/ASM, file bytes or a recorded run; **HIGH CONFIDENCE** = strong indirect evidence; **HYPOTHESIS** = plausible, unverified; **UNKNOWN** = what is missing is stated. Addresses are K22.exe virtual addresses unless prefixed `acknex.dll` (A7 Bonus engine). "Census" means a read-only Python walk of the installed ISO-derived files in `~/.local/share/kabus22/game/` done while writing this document (2026-10-09); numbers quoted are its output.

All integers are little-endian unless stated otherwise.

---

## 1. Inventory: what each shipped file is

Census of every `.k22` / `.wrs` in the installed game root (ISO-extracted; installer allowlist `installer/media.cpp:selected`).

| File(s) | Actual format | Confidence / evidence |
|---|---|---|
| `K22.wrs` | WRS2 archive, 182 members, all `.wdl` scripts | CONFIRMED (census) |
| `Kaynak.k22` | WRS2 archive, 3005 members: 970 `.wmb`, 795 `.mdl`, 521 `.ogg`, 321 `.tga`, 247 `.pcx`, 103 `.wav`, 45 `.bmp`, 1 `.hmp`, 1 `.wdl`, 1 `PALETTE.RAW` | CONFIRMED (census; also `reverse/extracted/Kaynak.k22.index.json`, `reverse/extracted/recovery.json:archives`) |
| `yazi_tr.k22`, `yazi_en.k22`, `yazi_de.k22` | WRS2 archives, 52 members each (localized UI `.tga`/`.pcx`/`.bmp`, one `.wdl`, `PALETTE.RAW`) | CONFIRMED (census) |
| `ses_tr.k22`, `ses_en.k22` | WRS2 archives, 14 members (12 `.ogg` voice, one `.wdl`, `PALETTE.RAW`) | CONFIRMED (census) |
| `ve*.k22` (17 files), `vt*.k22` (24 files), `vkt.k22`, `kn_arg.k22` | RIFF/AVI movies (not archives) | CONFIRMED (`RIFF....AVI LIST` header bytes; §8) |
| `nti.k22`, `bti1.k22`, `bti2.k22` / `nei.k22`, `bei1.k22`, `bei2.k22` / `ndi.k22`, `bdi1.k22`, `bdi2.k22` | Plain CRLF text, one string per line (TR / EN / DE item and interaction texts) | CONFIRMED bytes; consumer `dil_ceviri_tr.wdl:dosyayukle_strng0..2` → `GenelAyarlar.wdl` `txt_load` (§11) |
| `options.k22` | 31-byte (original) or 32-byte (patched) binary settings | CONFIRMED (§10) |
| `ftz.k22` (written at runtime) | 3 bytes: playtime day/hour/minute | CONFIRMED (§11) |
| `mdc.k22`, `msc.k22` | 3 ASCII bytes `000` | Bytes CONFIRMED; consumer UNKNOWN (no reference found in extracted original/patch scripts, native code, CONTRACT.txt or the patched K22.exe) |
| `yoldata.DAT` | 117960-byte path-routing table | CONFIRMED layout (§12) |
| `Kabus 22 Mode/K22_mode.wrs` | WRS3 archive, 435 members (A7 Bonus) incl. 3 nested WRS3 `mode_*.k22` | CONFIRMED (census) |

| `Kabus 22 Mode/mode_ayarlar.k22` | 5 CRLF text lines (Bonus settings) | CONFIRMED (§10.2) |
| `Kabus 22 Mode/ygm.k22` | 3 ASCII digits (Bonus launcher locale marker) | CONFIRMED bytes (§10.3) |
| `kayit<N>.sav`, `kysd.sav` (runtime) | Script-written save slot / save index | CONFIRMED writer (§11) |
| `K22.ini` | Text INI — community-patch artifact, not on the ISO | HIGH CONFIDENCE (§13) |

Not WRS: every census file whose first 4 bytes are not `WRS2`/`WRS3` is listed above with its real type. The `.k22` extension therefore carries no format meaning by itself.

## 2. WRS resource archives

### 2.1 Original A6 index loader (campaign)

Evidence: `reverse/decompiled/loaders/K22.exe.0041fd20.c` (index), `K22.exe.0041ff20` (open/register; summarized in `reverse/decompiled/RECOVERY.txt:42-57`), `reverse/decompiled/loaders/K22.exe.00420120.c` (lookup), `reverse/decompiled/decoder/K22.exe.00414bc0.c` (payload codec).

| Item | Value | Confidence / evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Registration | `RESOURCE` directive in parser `0041aef0` (`0x0041b4ab` refs string `0x005d4728`) → `0041ff20` opens the file, stores `FILE*` in table `0x006bafb8` | CONFIRMED, `RECOVERY.txt:39-46` |
| Archive limit | error after count `0x006bb1bc` exceeds `0x7f` → 128 archives | CONFIRMED, `RECOVERY.txt:45` |
| Magic | first 4 bytes compared (`_stricmp`) to `"WRS2"` | CONFIRMED, `K22.exe.0041fd20.c:36` |
| WRS2 name key / width | XOR `0xa5` (`DAT_006bb5f0`), pad constant `0x1f` | CONFIRMED, `0041fd20.c:38-39` |
| Legacy (no magic) | `rewind`, XOR key 0, pad constant `0x0c` | CONFIRMED, `0041fd20.c:34-35,42` |
| Name field size | WRS2 32 bytes, legacy 13 bytes: name read to on-disk NUL, then `fseek(pad - len)` | CONFIRMED (derived from control flow, `0041fd20.c:47-61`; `RECOVERY.txt:52`) |
| Size fields | two big-endian u32 built from four `getc`: stored (packed) length, then decoded length | CONFIRMED, `0041fd20.c:69-80` |
| Payload offset | `ftell` immediately after the header | CONFIRMED, `0041fd20.c:81-82` |
| Entry table | 0x30-byte records at `0x00665ea8`: name, +0x20 archive slot, +0x24 offset, +0x28 stored, +0x2c decoded | CONFIRMED, `0041fd20.c:63-84` |
| Entry limit | error `0x3ee` ("Too many WRS resources (%d max)!" at `0x005d72b8`) when total `0x006bb1b8` > `0xfff` → 4096 entries total | CONFIRMED, `0041fd20.c:85-87`, `reverse/decompiled/K22.exe.recovery.txt:1727` |
| Termination | name loop returns on `getc == -1` (EOF); loop condition tests the last byte read of the decoded-size field against `0xffffffff` (i.e. EOF from `getc`) | CONFIRMED code (`0041fd20.c:51-53,89`). `RECOVERY.txt:53` calls this a "0xffffffff termination marker"; **no on-disk sentinel record exists in any shipped archive** — every census archive is consumed exactly by 40-byte headers + payloads to EOF (CONFIRMED, census) |
| Lookup order | forward linear `_stricmp` scan of the entry table; **first (earliest-mounted) match wins**; decoded size must be ≤ the caller's limit, else "invalid size" | CONFIRMED, `K22.exe.00420120.c:99-126` |

### 2.2 On-disk layout

```
offset 0      : "WRS2" | "WRS3"        (absent in the legacy variant)
repeat until EOF:
  name[32]    : bytes XOR key until the first raw 0x00; rest raw zero padding   (legacy: name[13], key 0)
  u32be stored: packed payload length
  u32be size  : decoded length
  u8  payload[stored]
```

| Variant | Magic | Name key | Name bytes | Used by | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Legacy | none | 0 | 13 | no shipped file | `0041fd20.c` (CONFIRMED code path); no instance in census |
| WRS2 | `WRS2` | `0xa5` | 32 | all campaign archives | CONFIRMED (code + census) |
| WRS3 | `WRS3` | `0xb5` | 32 | all Bonus archives | CONFIRMED, A7 index `acknex.dll.10024860` (`MOV byte ptr [0x101ea600],0xb5` at `0x10024903`), `reverse/decompiled/runtime/bonus-core/CORE_CONTRACT.txt:47,67` |

Name padding is zero in every census header (CONFIRMED; native rejects nonzero padding). Names may contain `/` (directory-like). Every census member has `stored > 0` and `stored != decoded` — no member is stored raw (CONFIRMED, census: `pk==dec` count 0 for every archive).

### 2.3 Payload codec: LZSS

Every member payload is LZSS-coded, including already-compressed OGG (which therefore grows: `ses_en.k22` stored/decoded ratio 1.113, CONFIRMED census).

| Parameter | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Window | 4096 bytes, pre-filled with `0x20` (space) | CONFIRMED, `00414bc0.c:21-29` (`0x3fb` dwords of `0x20202020` + one `0x2020` word) |
| Initial write cursor | `0xfee` (4078) | CONFIRMED, `00414bc0.c:26-28` |
| Flag byte | 8 flags, consumed LSB first; bit 1 = literal byte, bit 0 = back-reference | CONFIRMED, `00414bc0.c:40-56` |
| Reference | 2 bytes `lo, hi`: position = `lo | ((hi & 0xf0) << 4)`; length = `(hi & 0x0f) + 3` (code stores `+2`, copies `<=`) | CONFIRMED, `00414bc0.c:70-89` |
| Bounds | input counted against stored length (`param_4`), output against decoded length (`param_3`) | CONFIRMED, `00414bc0.c:52,69,87,104` |

Independent confirmation: `reverse/extracted/recovery.json:lzss` (initial cursor 4078 and space fill proven by original `K22.wdl`/`sub_titles_tr.wdl` decoding; all entries decode to their declared sizes) — CONFIRMED.

### 2.4 Known archive contents

| Archive | Notes | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| ISO `K22.wrs` | 182 entries, 862026 bytes, SHA-256 `c9e32008…85c5` (installed inventory) | CONFIRMED (census, `~/.local/share/kabus22/.kabus22-inventory.json`) |
| Lutris `K22.wrs` | 179 entries, 804591 bytes, MD5 `7d8bad41…` — a different (older, Turkish-script) build; it is the source of `reverse/extracted/original/*.wdl` | CONFIRMED (`reverse/extracted/recovery.json:archives`); relationship to ISO HYPOTHESIS |
| `PALETTE.RAW` | present in `Kaynak.k22`, every `yazi_*.k22`, every `ses_*.k22`; 768 decoded bytes | CONFIRMED (census) |
| `K22_mode.wrs` nested | `mode_tr/en/de.k22` (WRS3) and `mode_ayarlar.k22` inside; RESOURCE mounts the **loose** same-named files, nested members are ordinary bytes | CONFIRMED, `bonus-core/CORE_CONTRACT.txt:46-48` |
| Patch `K22Widescreen.wrs` | WRS2, 190 entries (188 `.wdl`, 1 `.tga`, 1 `.bmp`) — community patch, not ISO | CONFIRMED, `reverse/extracted/recovery.json:archives` |

## 3. WMB6 world (`.wmb`)

Census: 970 `WMB6` in `Kaynak.k22`, 3 `WMB6` in `K22_mode.wrs`; **no `WMB7` file is shipped** (CONFIRMED; `reverse/extracted/recovery.json:native_3d_magic_counts` agrees).

### 3.1 Header

| Offset | Size | Field | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 4 | `"WMB6"` | CONFIRMED |
| 4 | 17 × 8 | `(u32 offset, u32 length)` per section; header ends at 140, first data (`legacy7`) starts at 140 | CONFIRMED, `reverse/extracted/asset_headers.json` (`header_layout_evidence`), bytes of `reverse/extracted/assets/level0.wmb` |

Section order (index: name as used by `asset_headers.json`): 0 palettes, 1 planes, 2 textures, 3 vertices, 4 pvs, 5 bsp_nodes, 6 materials, 7 faces, 8 legacy4, 9 aabb_hulls, 10 bsp_leafs, 11 bsp_blocks, 12 edges, 13 edgelist, 14 legacy7 (160-byte legacy hull records), 15 objects, 16 lightmaps — CONFIRMED (header bytes; native `Assets::decode_world` consumes the same indices). Reading WMB7-only trailing pairs would misinterpret section data (CONFIRMED, `asset_headers.json`).

### 3.2 Texture records (section 2)

Offset table (`u32 count`, `count × u32 offset`), then per record: `name[16]`, `u32 width`, `u32 height`, `u32 mip[4]` (offsets relative to the record), pixels.

| Profile | Pixel encoding | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Campaign A6 | base-level size `mip[1]-mip[0]` = 2×w×h (16-bit 565) or 3×w×h (24-bit); `width=height=0` → external image by name | HIGH CONFIDENCE (native `Assets::decode_world` accepts exactly these for all 970 shipped worlds; original reader body not exported here) |
| Bonus A7 | `+24` = format (`10` → 16-bit, `12` → 24-bit), pixels start at `+40`, exactly four mip levels; missing entries `0xffffffff` | CONFIRMED by citation in native source comment to `acknex.dll.10059e90` and uploader `1002cd4d..7a`; A7 export path not separately listed here |

### 3.3 Object records (section 15)

Offset table as above; record type is the first u32.

| Type | Content | Confidence / evidence |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | position, angle, 8 skipped bytes, `name[20]` | HIGH CONFIDENCE (native decoder; matches libgamestudio `wmb6.spec` cited in `asset_headers.json:sources`) |
| 2 | light: position, RGB (0–100 scale), range, flags | HIGH CONFIDENCE (as above) |
| 3 | legacy entity; native struct padded to 136 bytes | CONFIRMED, CONTRACT §24 (`CONTRACT.txt:810-826`) |
| 4 | sound: position, volume, range, flags, `file[33]` | HIGH CONFIDENCE |
| 5 | level info: sun azimuth/elevation floats at `+0x10/+0x14`, info flags, compiler version, gamma, lightmap size, packed sun colour at `+0x24`, ambient, fog colours | Layout HIGH CONFIDENCE; consumption CONFIRMED §19 |
| 6 | path: `name[20]`, point count (float), 36-byte points (position + 6 skills), 24-byte edges (1-based node pair, length, bezier, weight, skill) | HIGH CONFIDENCE |
| 7 | entity, verbatim 372-byte copy: `name` at 40, `file` at 73, `action` at 106 (33-byte slots), skills from 140 | CONFIRMED, CONTRACT §24 (`0045a358`) |
| 8 | region: min, max, 8 skipped bytes, `name[32]` | HIGH CONFIDENCE |

**Type 3 legacy filename rule** (CONFIRMED, `CONTRACT.txt:813-826`; `reverse/decompiled/runtime/entity-file-layout/contract.txt`, `original-asm.txt`): branch `0045a15a` of `00459eb0` uses name 40/20 bytes, filename 60/13, action 73/20. Byte 72 is tested at `0045a17d`: if zero, file (13) and action (20) are copied separately; if nonzero, `0045a1cc` calls `0045ccf0` with source 60, capacity 33 (≤32 chars + NUL) — the filename consumes the action slot and the action stays empty (zero-allocated by `0043a77a`). Skills 96..127 (8 floats), flags 128, ambient 132. Creation `004315f6` uses internal filename 73; `0043186e` checks internal action 106 and copies ≤19 chars for dispatch.

**Sun globals** (CONFIRMED, CONTRACT §19, `CONTRACT.txt:723-739`; `reverse/decompiled/runtime/sun-header-asm/contract.txt`): type-5 branch `0045a696-0045a6f2` assigns only `SUN_ANGLE` pan/tilt = record floats `+0x10/+0x14` × 1024, under load-mode predicate `007192e0`; the third SUN_ANGLE word is untouched. Packed sun colour `+0x24` is **not** consumed; `SUN_COLOR` (slot `00665c50`, zero xrefs) and `SUN_LIGHT` (`00665c1c`) are not assigned from the WMB.

### 3.4 Lightmaps (section 16)

Atlases of `256 << lightmapSize` square, 3 bytes per texel (`lightmapSize ≤ 2`). HIGH CONFIDENCE (native decoder accepts every shipped world). CPU storage and 565/mono LUTs: CONTRACT §20, §22 (`CONTRACT.txt:741-794`, `tex-lightmap-lut/contract.txt`) — CONFIRMED static.

## 4. MDL models (`.mdl`)

Census (first skin of each MDL4/MDL5 in `Kaynak.k22`): MDL4 334 (all skin format 2), MDL5 309 (format 2: 228, 4: 78, 5: 3), MDL7 152. `K22_mode.wrs`: MDL4 17, MDL5 35, MDL7 69. CONFIRMED.

### 4.1 MDL4 / MDL5 header (84 bytes)

| Field (order) | Evidence |
|---|---|
| magic `MDL4`/`MDL5`, version, scale vec3, offset vec3, (bounding/eye fields), `numskins`, `skinwidth`, `skinheight`, `numverts`, `numtris`, `numframes`, `numskinverts`, `flags`, `unused` | CONFIRMED values in `reverse/extracted/asset_headers.json` (e.g. `et_ari.MDL` MDL4 128×128, 145 verts; `yasin_deniz.mdl` MDL5 `skinwidth=0`, per-skin 512×512); layout per Conitec `prog_mdlhmp.html` (listed in `asset_headers.json:sources`) |

MDL4 skin dimensions come from the header; MDL5 stores width/height per skin (CONFIRMED by `yasin_deniz.mdl`: header 0×0, first skin 512×512).

### 4.2 Skin record type word

| `type & 7` | Meaning | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 8-bit indexed (palette) | HIGH CONFIDENCE (native; none observed as a first skin in census) |
| 1 | reference to an earlier skin index | HIGH CONFIDENCE |
| 2 | 16-bit RGB565 | CONFIRMED (census, decoded images) |
| 3 | 16-bit ARGB4444 | HIGH CONFIDENCE |
| 4 | 24-bit (B,G,R; `type & 128` swaps R/B) | CONFIRMED census |
| 5 | 32-bit BGRA (`type & 128` swap) | CONFIRMED census |
| 6 | embedded DDS of `width` bytes | HIGH CONFIDENCE |
| 7 | external filename, NUL-terminated | HIGH CONFIDENCE |
| flag 8 | 3 extra mip levels follow (dims must be multiples of 8) | HIGH CONFIDENCE |
| flag 16 / 32 | material block (4 colours + power) / length-prefixed extra data | HIGH CONFIDENCE (MDL7) |

### 4.3 UV and skin-selection rules (A6)

- Legacy signed pixel UVs are normalized by the **first raw skin's** dimensions rounded up to a power of two, minimum 8 (`00426aa0`, initialized `00413eaf`), in `00458500`. MDL7 float UVs are multiplied by raw/padded dimension. — CONFIRMED, CONTRACT §25 (`CONTRACT.txt:828-847`), `reverse/decompiled/runtime/model-uv-contract/contract.txt`.
- Empty skin descriptors consume zero bytes; zero skin count is malformed. — CONFIRMED §25.
- MDL4/5/7 and HMP5 use one model-wide skin bank; `004349f0` (`bmap_for_entity`) truncates/clamps the selector without mutating `ENTITY.SKIN`; draw preparation `0044a590` clamps and writes `ENTITY+0x40`. — CONFIRMED, CONTRACT §26 (`CONTRACT.txt:849-864`), `entity-skin-contract/contract.txt`.
- Raw MDL/HMP low-3 formats 0/2/3/4/5 map to CPU storage 1/2/2/3/4; formats 6/7 after MDL7 preprocessing give CPU4 (`00458b3b`); their decoding algorithm is UNKNOWN. — CONFIRMED §20.

### 4.4 MDL7

48-byte header (`version`, `bones_num`, `groups_num`, `mdl7data_size`, `entlump_size`, `medlump_size`) followed by declared structure sizes (bone 36, skin 28, colorvalue 16, material 68, skinpoint 8, triangle 12/16/26, mainvertex 16, framevertex 16, bonetrans 68, frame 24) and groups. CONFIRMED values for `bullet.mdl` in `asset_headers.json`; spec `libgamestudio/docs/mdl7.spec` (cited there).

A7 (Bonus) face reader `acknex.dll.101589eb` widens only UV index `0xffff` to `0xffffffff` (absent UV, float bytes `00000000` at `10187124`); other u16 values stay unsigned. — CONFIRMED, CONTRACT §30 (`CONTRACT.txt:1253-1260`), `reverse/decompiled/runtime/bonus-model-layout/contract.txt`.

## 5. HMP5 terrain (`.hmp`)

One shipped file (`yr.hmp` in `Kaynak.k22`). 84-byte header: scale, offset (−255.5), triangle size 15.96875, `mesh_vertices_x = 33`, `numskins 1`, `numverts 1089` (=33×33), `numframes 1`. CONFIRMED (`asset_headers.json`). Frames: packing word must be 2, then 4 bytes per vertex height (HIGH CONFIDENCE, native decoder). HMP generated UVs are separate from MDL UV normalization; loader `0045b630` reaches `00458500` for skins (CONFIRMED, §25–26).

### 10.2 `mode_ayarlar.k22` (Bonus, text)

### 10.3 `ygm.k22` (Bonus launcher locale)

Three ASCII digits. The packed Bonus launcher embeds `rms0.txt='000'`, `rms1.txt='111'`, `rms2.txt='222'` and copies one to `ygm.k22` by `menu_dil`; contract mapping `000=en, 111=tr, 222=de` — CONFIRMED, `bonus-core/entry/entry-contract.txt:33`, `bonus-core/CORE_CONTRACT.txt` item 3. **Discrepancy:** native `installer/launcher_settings.cpp` accepts only `111` (tr), `222` (de), `333` (en) and rejects `000` (CONFIRMED code). Installed file is `111`.

## 11. Save and progress files (script-defined)

These formats are defined entirely by WDL scripts; no engine save format (`game_save`) is used for them (no `game_save`/`game_load` call found in extracted original scripts — CONFIRMED grep).

| File | Layout | Evidence / confidence |
|---|---|---|
| `kayit<N>.sav`, N = 0..98 | Ordered byte stream, one byte per `file_asc_write` in `Yeni_Oyun_Deger.wdl:YD_OyunuKaydet` (270 call sites incl. fixed loops of 4–150 iterations); read back by `YD_OyunuYukle`. First fields: `save_versiyon` (=100, `K22.wdl`), `LY_AktifLevelID`, `Aktif_Player`, `Aktif_Silah`, `akt_music_idno`, …; later `loc_gun`, `loc_saat`, `loc_dakka`, `aktif_kayit_sayisi`, `aktif_oldurme_sayisi`, `aktif_enerji_sayisi`, … | Writer order CONFIRMED (script). Behaviour for values > 255 in the original engine: UNKNOWN |
| `kysd.sav` | Text: `file_var_write(Aktif_SaveNo)`, `file_var_write(SLG_KayitSayisi)`, then `SLG_KayitSayisi` label strings each followed by `"\n"`; max 99 slots (`YukleMenu.wdl: SLG_MaxKayit`) | CONFIRMED (`YukleMenu.wdl:SLG_Kaydet`); native regression expects e.g. `"1 1 <label>\n"` (`native/check_engine.cpp`) |
| `ftz.k22` | 3 bytes: day, hour, minute (`file_asc_write` in `CikisMenu.wdl`, read in `GenelAyarlar.wdl`) | CONFIRMED (script) |

TXT_LOAD / FILE_STR_READ tokenization of text files (initial bytes ≤ 0x1f skipped; token ends at EOF, any byte ≤ 0x1f, or `delimit_str[0]` = `,`; spaces kept; no comment handling; buffer `0063bc30`, limit 4095): CONFIRMED, CONTRACT §14 (`CONTRACT.txt:522-551`).
```

`docs/reverse-engineering/SCRIPT_SYSTEM.md`:

```md
# WDL Script System

Purpose: how Kabus 22's WDL/C-Script is compiled and executed by the original engines and how `native/wdl.cpp` reimplements it.

Related: [REVERSE_ENGINEERING.md](../REVERSE_ENGINEERING.md) (index) · [ENGINE_ARCHITECTURE.md](../ENGINE_ARCHITECTURE.md) · [FUNCTION_MAP.md](FUNCTION_MAP.md) · [DATA_STRUCTURES.md](DATA_STRUCTURES.md) · [RESOURCE_FORMATS.md](RESOURCE_FORMATS.md) · [ORIGINAL_BEHAVIOR.md](ORIGINAL_BEHAVIOR.md) · [../GAMEPLAY_SYSTEMS.md](../GAMEPLAY_SYSTEMS.md)

## Scope and conventions

- **Campaign engine.** The evidence comes from `Kabus22Patch/K22.exe` (SHA256 `1a6a0dbc…7bed`), which identifies itself as "A6 engine" "6.31.4" (`0x0061dda8`/`0x0061ddb4`). See [`CONTRACT.txt:1-10`](../../reverse/decompiled/runtime/CONTRACT.txt) and [`RECOVERY.txt:31-35`](../../reverse/decompiled/RECOVERY.txt). This is the *patched* executable. The ISO `K22.exe` (`cc193c6b…`) is not packed and differs from it in only six `.text` bytes (start-up/archive branches) with identical `.rdata`, so the recovered addresses and code apply to the ISO build (**CONFIRMED** byte comparison, [EXECUTABLE_ANALYSIS](EXECUTABLE_ANALYSIS.md#community-patch-binaries-not-part-of-the-iso), `CONTRACT.txt:2147-2154`). Runtime parity with the original on Windows was never observed (**UNKNOWN**).
- **Bonus mode.** Bonus mode ("Kabus 22 Mode", `K22_mode.wrs`) runs on a separate A7 `acknex.dll` (SHA256 `f96c7645…227b`). See [`bonus-core/CORE_CONTRACT.txt:1-4`](../../reverse/decompiled/runtime/bonus-core/CORE_CONTRACT.txt). Native code selects it with `SemanticProfile::BonusA7` ([`native/value.hpp`](../../native/value.hpp) `SemanticProfile`).
- **Citations.** `CONTRACT §N` means [`reverse/decompiled/runtime/CONTRACT.txt`](../../reverse/decompiled/runtime/CONTRACT.txt) section N. Bare addresses are K22.exe VAs. Decompiled paths are relative to `reverse/decompiled/runtime/` unless they start with `../`. The CONTRACT writes "bitN" for a mask value N; for example, `006446e8` "bit1" is `|1` in [`trace/K22.exe.00404b60.c:16`](../../reverse/decompiled/runtime/trace/K22.exe.00404b60.c).
- **Extracted scripts.** Script identifiers come from `reverse/extracted/original/*.wdl` (179 files). [`recovery.json`](../../reverse/extracted/recovery.json) `archives[0]` records that these were extracted from the Lutris install's `K22.wrs` (SHA256 `5bae0b5e…c14f`). The ISO copies are in `reverse/media/iso/scripts/` (182 entries). [`script-comparison.json`](../../reverse/media/iso/script-comparison.json) marks 173/182 as identical. The 9 that differ are `K22.wdl`, `dil_ceviri_{tr,en,de}.wdl`, `sub_titles_en.wdl`, `kotu_koruyucu.wdl`, `cinematic.wdl`, `YeniMenu.wdl` and `Yeni_Oyun_Deger.wdl`. `GenelAyarlar.wdl`, `YukleMenu.wdl`, `CikisMenu.wdl`, `Ses_Sistemi.wdl`, `oyuncu2.wdl` and `LevelYonetim.wdl` are identical (CONFIRMED). Line numbers quoted here for the differing files (for example `cinematic.wdl`) refer to the extracted Lutris copy. Patch scripts are under `reverse/extracted/patch/` (188 files). Bonus scripts are under `reverse/media/iso/mode/scripts/K22_mode.wrs/`.
- **Confidence labels.** **CONFIRMED** means decompiled code, assembly, bytes or an actual run. **HIGH CONFIDENCE** means strong indirect evidence. **HYPOTHESIS** and **UNKNOWN** carry their usual meanings.

## 1. Pipeline overview

| Stage | Original (A6 K22.exe) | Native | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Archive mount | `RESOURCE` directive → `FUN_0041ff20` opens the archive and indexes it via `FUN_0041fd20` (WRS2, XOR-0xA5 names). See `RECOVERY.txt:37-57` and [`../loaders/K22.exe.0041ff20.c`](../../reverse/decompiled/loaders/K22.exe.0041ff20.c). | `Runtime::load(entry, Source, Resource)` forwards `resource "x"` to the `Resource` callback. `native/main.cpp` binds that callback to `Assets::mount` ([`native/assets.cpp`](../../native/assets.cpp)). | CONFIRMED |
| Text fetch | `FUN_00420120` is the shared file/archive loader. | Engine-internal script | `FUN_0041b5d0` parses the embedded C-Script text at `0x005d3348` (`RECOVERY.txt:68`). The extracted copy is [`reverse/extracted/engine_internal.wdl`](../../reverse/extracted/engine_internal.wdl). | Native has no embedded text; defaults come from `Engine::initialize_globals` ([`native/engine.cpp`](../../native/engine.cpp)). | CONFIRMED (original); native equivalence HIGH CONFIDENCE |

| Plugin enumeration | `004133c0` runs after compilation and before MAIN (§13 `:475-479`, §17 `:630-637`). | `Engine::initialize_plugins` runs after `Runtime::load`, before `configure_language` and `bootstrap` (§13 `:480-486`, `native/main.cpp`). | CONFIRMED |

| Per-frame | `00414650` frame → `004125e0` (input/events/scheduler) → level command dispatch `0041de10` (§13 `:504-508`). | `Engine::tick` → `Engine::update_input`/`update_ui` → `Runtime::tick` → deferred `load_level` | CONFIRMED |

## 2. Compiler directives and preprocessing

| Feature | Original evidence | Native implementation | Confidence / gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| INCLUDE | `0041aef0:163-189` → `00419cb0`. No include-once set; filename must be under 32 bytes; suppressed when `006633c0 & 2` (§9 `:333-340`). | `Runtime::Impl::preprocess` calls `preprocess(file, source(file))` unconditionally. Native adds a recursion bound of 256 and no 32-byte filename limit. | CONFIRMED; the 32-byte limit is not enforced natively. |
| RESOURCE | `0041aef0:211-215` → `FUN_0041ff20`. Duplicate names are suppressed case-insensitively; at most 128 archives (`RECOVERY.txt:40-46`). | Same `preprocess` branch → `Resource` callback. `Assets::mount` dedups by resolved path (`mounted_`). | CONFIRMED |
| IFDEF/IFNDEF/IFELSE/ENDIF, DEFINE | Macro expansion `0041a0e0`; text macros registered by `00419d20` (§6 `:273-281`, §9 `:356-362`). | `preprocess` keeps a condition stack. `append_expanded` expands macros up to depth 64. Protected compiler macros come from `State::compilerMacros`. | CONFIRMED for the shape; native depth limit is its own choice. |
| Predefined macros | 79 numeric startup macros, as integer text, in `00413990` ([`numeric-constants.json`](../../reverse/decompiled/runtime/numeric-constants.json), §6 `:266-278`). | BIND / LEVEL | Consume one parameter with no side effect (§17 `:622-625`). | `Runtime::Impl::parse` stores them in `CompilerSettings::bindings`/`levels` only. | CONFIRMED |
| PLUGINDIR | Must be ≤126 bytes; copied to `0x006c7488` when `006633c0` bit 2 is clear (§17 `:626-628`). | `parse` rejects >126 bytes and stores it in `CompilerSettings::plugin_directory`. `Engine::initialize_plugins` supports only the empty or `.` directory. | CONFIRMED |
| SAVEDIR, PRINT, HALT | Listed in the `0041aef0` dispatch (`RECOVERY.txt:39`). | No dedicated handling in `parse` (no match in `native/wdl.cpp`). | Original CONFIRMED. Their semantics are **UNKNOWN** (not recovered). No top-level use was found in the extracted original scripts. |
| WINDOW block | `00419c40` sets a handler that discards every token (`00419c20`: `*DAT_006633a8=0; return 1`). No object is built (§15 `:570-581`; [`window-properties/K22.exe.00419c20.c`](../../reverse/decompiled/runtime/window-properties/K22.exe.00419c20.c)). Example source: `K22.wdl:WINSTART`. | `parse` parses it and emits the diagnostic "obsolete WINDOW … parsed without object construction"; `initialize` skips `type=="window"`. | CONFIRMED |
| Identifiers spanning whitespace | In expression context, `0041a250` concatenates tokens without separators. `0040c090:17` strips SP/LF/TAB/FF/BS/CR/BEL. Declaration names stay single-token (§16 `:603-618`). Example: `materials.wdl` (mode) `Mtl_ arkakum`. | `Runtime::Impl::expression_token` concatenates adjacent Word/Number tokens while `compactExpressions` is true. That flag is set only while compiling function bodies (`parse`, function branch). | CONFIRMED (original). Native coverage of initializers and properties outside function bodies is **UNKNOWN**. |
| Repeated ACTION/FUNCTION bodies | The later body replaces the earlier one and descriptor identity is kept (`00403a00`, `00403b10`; §9 `:342-354`). Example: `cinematic.wdl:video_ebrudusme_maz`. | `parse` clears the code of an already-defined function and records the diagnostic "replacing function …". `FunctionId` is unchanged. | CONFIRMED |
| Scalar VAR initializer | `00420990` with `0041a1b0(0)` applies `atof` to the token, so an unresolved word becomes 0 (§10 `:366-387`). | `parse` declaration branch + `initialize`. | Original CONFIRMED; native token-to-0 parity not audited (UNKNOWN). |
| BMAP `name,<file>` | Same path as `name="file"` (`0040ef40`/`0040ee60`, §17 `:639-650`). | `parse` accepts `,` as an initializer for font/bmap/sound/string. | CONFIRMED |

## 3. Values and fixed-point arithmetic (§5 `:172-224`)

| Rule | Original | Native (`native/wdl.cpp` `Runtime::Impl::evaluate`, `Expr::Binary` branch; `native/value.hpp` `Value`) | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Representation | Signed 32-bit raw/1024 (22.10). Pointers share the word unscaled. | `Value{kind,bits}` with `Kind::Number/Object/Function/NativeText`. Object handles are `ObjectId`s, not machine pointers. | CONFIRMED |
| `+ - unary-` | Wrap mod 2³² | `raw(x.bits+y.bits)` | CONFIRMED |
| `*` | `floor((P+C)/1024)`, with C=1023 only when −2³² ≤ P < 0. The high word is compared to −1. | `if(n<0&&n>=-4294967296LL)n+=1023; n>>10` | CONFIRMED |
| `/` | `trunc((L·1024)/R)`. Division by zero or overflow raises an x86 #DE, and the engine's handling of that is **UNKNOWN**. | Throws a WDL diagnostic ("fixed-point division by zero/overflow"). | Native diverges at the fault boundary: it reports an error and does not reproduce a crash. |
| `%` | `0040bfb0` negative-L adjustment using `0xf424000000/R` | Same formula, plus diagnostics on overflow. | CONFIRMED for the formula. The `0040bfb0` export is not present under `numeric/`; the source is §5 `:198-202`. |
| Comparisons | Signed raw compare; result is 1024 or 0. | `Value::from_int(x.raw()<y.raw())` etc. | CONFIRMED |
| `&&`, `\|\|` | Both operands are evaluated eagerly, left then right. | `arg(0)` then `arg(1)` are both evaluated before the test. | CONFIRMED |
| `INT` | `00403d60` truncates toward zero and returns a scaled value. | `Engine::service_builtin` `int`: `Value::from_int(integer(0))`. | CONFIRMED |
| Literals | `atof×1024` → `005b72cc` truncation to int64, low word kept (`abi/K22.exe.00402770.asm.txt:46-54`). | `Value::from_double` truncates toward zero; it throws outside the int64 range. | CONFIRMED in range; out-of-range behaviour differs (original policy UNKNOWN). |
| DLL conversion | `FLOAT 00406fc0`, `FLOATR 00406fe0`, `FLOATD 00407010` pack float bits. Plugins decode arguments with `SAR 10`. | `Engine::service_builtin` `float` etc. | CONFIRMED (original); native per-builtin parity not audited. |

## 4. Coroutines: creation, WAIT/WAITT, scheduling

### 4.1 WAIT/WAITT binding (§1 `:16-38`)
- **CONFIRMED.** WAIT row `0061d538` → handler `00404b60`; WAITT row `0061d548` → `00404be0`; SLEEP → `00404ca0`; proc_kill → `00404cd0`. These rows are in the 317-row API descriptor table `0061c408..0061d7d8` ([`api-descriptors.json`](../../reverse/decompiled/runtime/api-descriptors.json)). Calls compile to `MOV EBX,handler; CALL EBX` (`numeric/K22.exe.0040aba0.c:181-192`). A handler yields by setting `006446e8 |= 1`. The interpreter `00410a80` checks that flag after the expression (`interpreter/K22.exe.00410a80.c:849-850`). There is no OS-level wait.
- **Native.** `Runtime::Impl::evaluate`, `Expr::Call` branch: `name=="wait"||"waitt"||"sleep"` sets `Process::countdown`, calls `capture(*p)` and sets `p->yielded=true`.

### 4.2 Timing (§3 `:71-142`)
| Item | Original | Native | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| WAIT(n) | Clamp the raw value to [1024, 1048575] and store `n-1024` (`trace/K22.exe.00404b60.c:8-17`). | `std::clamp(n,1024,1048575)`; `countdown=clamped-1024` | CONFIRMED |
| WAITT(n) | `t=TIME` (`*00665cf4`); `chosen=max(t, min(n, 1048575))`; store `t-chosen` (`00404be0.c:11-19`). | Identical expression. | CONFIRMED. The CONTRACT branch for TIME > cap is "preserve exact branch". Native uses `n<t?t:min(n,cap)`; the edge case where TIME itself exceeds the cap is not separately verified (HYPOTHESIS that they agree). |
| SLEEP | Handler `00404ca0` (`clock-instructions/K22.exe.00404ca0.c`) | Native shifts the argument `<<4` (seconds→ticks) and reuses the WAITT path. | Native formula: HIGH CONFIDENCE. Original body not summarised in CONTRACT, so parity is UNKNOWN. |
| Wake rule | c ≥ 1024: subtract 1024 and keep. Otherwise resume iff `c > -min(TIME,1024)`; if not, `c += TIME`, capped at 0 (`trace/K22.exe.00412080.c:35-65`). | `Runtime::Impl::tick`: the same three branches. | CONFIRMED |
| freeze_mode | <1024: all records run. 1024–2047: only records with `my==NULL` run. ≥2048: the scheduler is skipped (`00412080`, `004125e0:16-18`). | `tick` re-reads `freeze_mode` for each record (comment cites A6 `004120ec`/A7 `10016710`). | CONFIRMED |
| Pass order | Double-buffered queues; pass 1 runs records whose function has `+0x1c & 2` clear, pass 2 the rest (PROC_LATE, legacy opcode 38). | Two passes on `functions[].schedulerFlags & 2`. A7 uses three passes ("bit1 first, neither second, bit2 third"; the code comment cites [`bonus-core/load-bonus/order/acknex.dll.10016710.c`](../../reverse/decompiled/runtime/bonus-core/load-bonus/order/acknex.dll.10016710.c)). | A6 CONFIRMED. A7 ordering is HIGH CONFIDENCE (native comment; not re-derived here). |
| TIME computation | `00414650`: QPC ticks/64000·1024; FPS_LOCK/FPS_MIN clamp to ≥51; `TIME_FACTOR` and then `TIME_SMOOTH` (default 0.5) with rounded multiply `floor((P+512)/1024)` (§3 `:103-123`). | `Engine::tick`: `fps_lock`/`fps_max`/`fps_min`, clamp to 51, rounded `mul`, `time_smooth`. | CONFIRMED |

### 4.3 Continuation record, first yield, locals, MY/YOU (§2 `:40-69`, §10 `:389-394`)
- **CONFIRMED.** `00410390` appends a record of `44+12·locals` bytes to the destination queue (layout in [DATA_STRUCTURES.md §3](DATA_STRUCTURES.md#3-scheduler-and-continuation-records)). `00410350` snapshots three words per local, and `00410310` restores them (`trace/K22.exe.00410350.c`, `interpreter/K22.exe.00410310.c`).
- **CONFIRMED.** A call into a script function is synchronous until that function's first yield. The caller then continues, and the callee resumes later on its own (`abi/K22.exe.00412220.c:12-37`). The caller receives the value of the yielding expression (`00410a80:848-853` stores it in `006445b4`). For example, `wait(3)` returns raw 3072, and `wait(0)` returns 1024.
- **Native.** `Runtime::Impl::start` runs `prepare` and then `run` on a stack `Process`. On yield, `capture` copies the `Process`, saving `savedLocals` per owned local object, and pushes it onto `queued`. `run` restores the snapshots before resuming. The call returns `p.result`, which holds the WAIT return value.
- **CONFIRMED.** MY/YOU are stored in the record and restored on resume (`00411fe0`). DLL interface `+0xa34`/`+0xa38` point at `my` (`006441d8`) and `you` (`006441dc`) (`registry/K22.exe.0040c290.c:19-23`). Native: `ProcessContext{processId,my,you}`, plus `value_slot("my")`/`("you")` locals and `_arg1.._arg4` in `Runtime::Impl::prepare`.

### 4.4 proc_kill / proc_status / proc_late (§4 `:144-170`, §10 `:396-401`)
| Mode bit | Original (`trace/K22.exe.00410660.c:8-20`) | Native (`evaluate`, `proc_kill`) | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Cancel suspended records whose `my` equals the current `my` | same | CONFIRMED |
| 2 | Cancel records whose **my** equals the current `you`. This is not kill-all. | same | CONFIRMED |
| 4 | Cancel records of the current function | same | CONFIRMED |
| 8 | Set `006446e8 \|= 2`. This blocks all continuation insertion until the next frame start (`004125e0:14` clears it). | `suppressContinuations=true`; reset at `tick` entry | CONFIRMED |
| 16 / proc_status / proc_kill2 | Absent from the 317-row table. The resolver `0040c200` returns NULL. | Not implemented, by design | CONFIRMED absent. No extracted WDL calls proc_kill/proc_status. |
| proc_late | Sets function descriptor `+0x1c \|= 2` (`00410a80:819-821`) | `Instruction::Late` and builtin `proc_late` set `schedulerFlags \|= 2` | CONFIRMED |

Entity removal: `00431920` calls `00410550(entity,1)`, but only when entity `+0x60` (event_flags) is nonzero. That call cancels records whose MY is the entity and clears matching YOU (§13 `:510-516`). Native `Runtime::kill_for_entity` always cancels and clears YOU; it applies the event-mask gate only to registered-pointer cleanup (§27 `:1149-1156`). That divergence is deliberate and documented (CONFIRMED).

## 5. Locals: three words per declaration (§11 `:403-423`)
- **CONFIRMED.** `00420b30` preallocates the shared locals `_loc255`…`_loc0` (head `006bb1c4`). Each is a 28-byte object with values at `+0x10/+0x14/+0x18`. The compiler (`00402fe0:22-74`) maps each `VAR` declaration to one `_locN`. Scalars, VECTORs and small arrays all get exactly three words, and `x/pan`, `y/tilt`, `z/roll` map to `+0x10/+0x14/+0x18`. For example, the two `Ses_Sistemi.wdl` angle locals cannot alias each other.
- **Native.** `Runtime::Impl::local_storage` allocates a per-process `Object::Kind::Vector` with `array.resize(size)`. `size` is 3 for scalars and VECTORs and the declared count for arrays (`statement`/`local` → `localDefinitions`). The divergence is that native local arrays larger than 3 get their declared length, while the original gives every declaration three words. The original's behaviour for out-of-bounds indices is **UNKNOWN**.

## 6. Global registry and object member tables (§6 `:226-281`)
- **CONFIRMED.** 330 numeric registry rows at `0061ec80..00620b70`, stride 24, are listed in [`global-registry.json`](../../reverse/decompiled/runtime/global-registry.json). Each is registered as WDL type 9 with three words of storage, and flags are ORed into object `+0x14` (`registry/K22.exe.0041e060.c`, `0041e180.c`). Example defaults: VERSION 0x1941, TIME 1024, TIME_SMOOTH 512, FREEZE_MODE 0, MAX_LOOPS 5120000.
- **Native.** `nativeDefaults[]` has 334 rows: 330 A6 rows plus 4 `bonusOnly`. For example, `{"VERSION",{6465,0,0}}`. `Engine::initialize_globals` adds `delimit_str`, the callback globals, and masks such as VISIBLE/CENTER_X. Native-only normalisations such as Bonus `FILTER` are labelled in-code as not original (§28 `:1179-1186`).
- **CONFIRMED.** Member tables for 8 kinds (entity 141, text 28, vector 10, numeric_array 14, string 1, view 46, panel 16, material 36) are in [`member-descriptors.json`](../../reverse/decompiled/runtime/member-descriptors.json). Native uses the named field maps `Object::fields` and `nativeMasks[]` (108 rows) and does not use byte offsets. Details are in [DATA_STRUCTURES.md §5](DATA_STRUCTURES.md#5-script-visible-object-members).

## 7. Input query, named slots and edges (§12 `:425-471`)
| Item | Original | Native | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Name table | 89 names → 80 distinct slots at `0061b108`, stride 8 ([`input-contract.json`](../../reverse/decompiled/runtime/input-contract.json)) | `nativeKeys[]` has 89 rows. Aliases share a slot through `keyboard_`/`keyboardCallbacks_`, plus compiler alias macros. | CONFIRMED |
| `key_pressed(code)` | `00404d30`: 0..126 → keyboard; 256..267 JOY_1..12; 268..279 JOY2_1..12; 280/281/282 mouse L/R/M; anything else → 0. Edges are not consumed. | `Engine::service_builtin` `key_pressed`: same ranges; 0..126 → `Engine::key_state` | CONFIRMED |
| Edge capture | `0042ddd0` scan = `(lParam>>16)&0x7f`; a down edge only from held=0. `00422000` publishes held OR fresh-down, so a tap lasts one frame. | SDL scancode → `legacy_scancode`. `Input.keys` / `Input.pressed` are ORed in `key_state`. | CONFIRMED (original). Native edge parity was observed for held keys in actual runs (memory/CONTRACT §42 `:2312`). |
| Event dispatch | `004125e0.asm:54-276`: per edge, the key handler runs and then ON_ANYKEY, with MY/YOU=0 and `_arg1` set/restored. `ON_MOUSE_STOP` fires each still frame. | `Engine::update_input` lambda `edge`: saves `_arg1`, then `runtime.start(fn,args,0,0)`, then `anykey`. | CONFIRMED |
| Defaults | `engine_internal.wdl` binds F2_save, F3_load, F5_toggle_video, F6_sshot, F10/ESC/CLOSE_exit, F12_tog_sounds, ENTER_toggle_screen. | Not embedded; game scripts override. | Original CONFIRMED; native default binding set **UNKNOWN** (not audited). |

The game's own mapping layer is `GenelAyarlar.wdl:Tuslari_Esitle`, a STARTER that polls once per frame. It maps `GA_Tuslar[0..9]` (indices `GA_Ileri`…`GA_Buyu`) through `key_pressed`, ORs in joystick buttons `GA_JTuslar[0..5]`, and writes globals `Key_Ileri`… (CONFIRMED by script source).

## 8. Bootstrap order and deferred level transitions (§13 `:473-520`)
1. Compile → plugin enumeration `004133c0` → `00414650` queues MAIN, then STARTERs (`+0x1c & 4`, `TEST [ESI+0x1c],BL` with `BL=4` at `004146c0`). The descriptor list `0063b9b4` is built by prepending, so starters run in reverse order of first creation. **CONFIRMED.** Native `Runtime::bootstrap`: `enqueue(main)` and then `for id-->1` over `starter&&defined`.
2. `004104f0` only appends a countdown-0 record; nothing runs immediately. MAIN runs first in the FIFO pass. For example, `K22.wdl:main` calls `GA_AyarlariYukle` and yields `sleep(1)`/`wait(1)` before `level_load`. **CONFIRMED.**
3. `level_load` (`00404f00`) stores the filename at `65580` and pending command mask 8 at `6557c`, then returns 1024 without yielding. `0041de10` executes the load after the frame's script phase, when INKEY_ACTIVE==0. **CONFIRMED.** Native: `Engine::world_builtin` `level_load` sets `pendingLevel`/`pendingLevelLoad`. `Engine::tick` calls `load_level` after `runtime.tick` and `worldFrameEvents`.
4. Level teardown `00434670` → `004341a0` → `00431920` for each entity, which cancels by MY and clears YOU. New entity actions are queued with `00410520` and first run in the *next* scheduler phase. STARTERs are not re-run. **CONFIRMED.**

## 9. Strings, files and media handoff (§14 `:522-568`)
- **CONFIRMED.** TXT_LOAD (`00408890`) and FILE_STR_READ (`00408470`) share the reader `00405e20`. The reader skips leading bytes ≤0x1F, stops at a byte ≤0x1F or at `delimit_str[0]` (default `,`), and keeps spaces. TXT_LOAD has no comment handling and returns `count<<10`.
- **CONFIRMED.** MEDIA_PLAY (`00405d10`→`00405ca0`→`00425730`) passes the filename through `MultiByteToWideChar(CP_ACP)` to DirectShow with no engine path rewriting.
- **CONFIRMED.** STR_CLIP (`00404780`) removes a prefix. A negative count is undefined memory behaviour. Native `str_clip` throws on a negative count.
- **Native.** `Engine::service_builtin` handles `txt_load` (reads `delimit_str`), `file_str_read` (skips `<32`), `file_asc_read/write` (one byte, `raw>>10`), `file_var_read/write` (text `"%d "` / `"%.3f "`) and `media_play`. File paths go through `svc_private(saveRoot,…)`, which writes to private XDG data, and fall back to read-only archive assets.

## 10. VECTOR temporaries (§18 `:661-721`)
- **CONFIRMED.** VECTOR (`00403eb0`) and `_vec` (`00407040`) share a 64-slot ring `[0063ce30,0063d130)` with cursor `0061d7e8`. The cursor is pre-incremented, so the first slot returned is `0063ce3c`. `_vec` converts float bits to scaled raw. Returned pointers are borrowed, and the 64th later producer overwrites the same slot. WAIT does not capture the ring contents.
- **CONFIRMED.** Native-call arguments are evaluated right-to-left (`0040aba0.c:202-223`).
- **Native.** `Engine` member `vectorTemps_` (`std::array<Object*,64>`) and `vectorTempCursor_` (pre-increment) in `native/engine.hpp`; the `vector`/`_vec` builtin is in `Engine::service_builtin`. The `Expr::Call` evaluation loop runs `for(i=e.args.size(); i-->1;)`, which is right-to-left. The two gaps §18 recorded at `:705-710` (a fresh allocation per call, and left-to-right evaluation) are therefore closed in current source (CONFIRMED by code reading; no run performed for this document).

## 11. Raw pointer words in VAR arrays (§29–31 `:1201-1311`)
- **CONFIRMED.** The original stores bitmap/object addresses as unscaled words in VAR arrays. For example, `CikisMenu.wdl` computes `bmap_width(DMIL_CikisSoru[DD_Dil]+Cer_Kenar)` with `Cer_Kenar=0`. The A6 emitter does `ADD EAX,EBX` on the raw words (`0040aba0`, §30 `:1246-1247`).
- **Native.** Arithmetic returns `Value::Kind::Number`, so the object tag is lost. `svc_bitmap(Engine&, Value)` (`native/engine.cpp`) therefore accepts either Object or Number. It then runs `State::require` and checks for a live `Object::Kind::Bmap`, rejecting NULL, unknown, dead and wrong-kind handles (§30 `:1241-1245`). The actual Main EXIT→NO→Main and EXIT→YES path was verified (§31 `:1273-1283`). Native does **not** emulate arbitrary machine-pointer arithmetic (by design).

## 12. Native callable/data namespaces (§41 `:1630-1667`)
- **CONFIRMED.** The A6 resolver `0040a300` (C 74-153) searches the native table `0061c408` *before* ordinary symbols. A7 `1000bf40` does the same with `101a8200`. A call to `str_len(...)` is therefore a native call even when a numeric global `STR_LEN` exists.
- **Native.** [`native/native_calls.inc`](../../native/native_calls.inc) defines `commonNativeCalls` (312 names), `campaignNativeCalls` (5) and `bonusNativeCalls` (80), generated from `api-descriptors.json` and `bonus-physics/api-descriptors.json`. `native_call_name(SemanticProfile, name)` in `native/wdl.cpp` binds plain-name calls to `Expr::Native` when the AST is built. Bare data reads still resolve through the ordinary symbol path.

## 13. Plugin DLL calls
| Plugin | Origin | Exports used by WDL | Native provider | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `RenkAyar.dll` | Shipped with the original game | `dl_PaKaGa`, `dl_Reset` (`RECOVERY.txt:110-112`, [`../RenkAyar.behavior.txt`](../../reverse/decompiled/RenkAyar.behavior.txt)) | `svc_plugin_open` sets `pluginGamma=true` | CONFIRMED |
| `kabus_dll.dll` | Kabus22Patch, a community patch artifact that is not on the ISO | `INI_*`, `Parse_EscapeChar`, `DiscordRPC_*`; `A6_DLLAPI` at `0x100871d0` returns 630 (`RECOVERY.txt:94-108`, [`../final/kabus_dll.dll.100871d0.c`](../../reverse/decompiled/final/kabus_dll.dll.100871d0.c)) | `Engine::service_builtin` implements `ini_getvariable` (returns `"undefined"` for a missing key), `ini_setvariable`, `parse_escapechar` (9 pairs) and `discordrpc_*` over a Unix socket | CONFIRMED |
| Handshake | `0040c330`: `A6_DLLAPI(interface 006438b0)` result must be <631, else `A5_DLLAPI` result <512. At most 64 modules (`00644730..0064482c`) (§17 `:630-659`). | `Engine::initialize_plugins` chooses a compiled provider from `dllfunction` imports (`Runtime::external_import`). No PE loading. | CONFIRMED |
| proc_status lookup | The patch DLL asks for it, and the resolver returns NULL (§4 `:164-170`). | Not provided | CONFIRMED |

## 14. Worked example: a STARTER polling once per frame

Identifiers only: `GenelAyarlar.wdl:Tuslari_Esitle`, a STARTER whose body is `while(1){ Key_* = key_pressed(GA_Tuslar[...]) | ...; wait(1); }`.

1. **Load.** `parse` sees `starter`, so `ensure_function` creates a descriptor and sets `f.starter=true`. In the original, `00403b10` passes `1` to `00403a00` and the descriptor carries `+0x1c & 4`.
2. **Bootstrap.** `Runtime::bootstrap` enqueues MAIN and then this STARTER. In the original, `004104f0` appends a record with countdown 0.
3. **Frame N.** `Runtime::tick` runs the FIFO pass. The countdown is 0, which is greater than `-min(TIME,1024)`, so the process runs. `run` evaluates the assignments, which call native `key_pressed` (right-to-left argument evaluation). It then reaches `wait(1)`: `n=1024` → clamp → `countdown=0`, `capture` copies the locals and context, and `yielded=true` makes `run` return.
4. **Frame N+1.** The pending queue is swapped. The countdown is 0, so the process resumes at the instruction after `wait` (`p.pc`). The while loop repeats, so each `Key_*` global is refreshed exactly once per frame.
5. **Freeze.** With `freeze_mode` ≥ 1024 the STARTER still runs, because `my==NULL`. Records whose MY is an entity are copied forward unchanged. With `freeze_mode` ≥ 2048 nothing runs.

## 15. Known gaps (§8 `:312-329` plus current source)
| Gap | Status |
|---|---|
| ISO `K22.exe` vs analysed patched `K22.exe` | Code identical except six start-up/archive-path `.text` bytes (CONFIRMED, [EXECUTABLE_ANALYSIS](EXECUTABLE_ANALYSIS.md)); Windows runtime parity UNKNOWN |
| Special input/pointer waits (`00412080:38-46`, statement opcode `0x19`) | UNKNOWN semantics; not implemented natively |
| Queue capacity/allocation (`006446e4`) | UNKNOWN; native queues are unbounded `std::deque` |
| x87 exception policy for `/`, `%`, `_vec`, NaN | UNKNOWN; native raises diagnostics |
| SAVEDIR/PRINT/HALT directive semantics | UNKNOWN; native has no dedicated handling |
| Complete dynamic object/event/key defaults; all 317 API side effects | UNKNOWN (§8) |
| Local arrays wider than 3 words | Native diverges (§5 above) |
| Native universal MY cancellation on entity removal (not gated by event_flags) | Intentional divergence (§27) |
| Extracted `original/` scripts come from the Lutris `K22.wrs`; 9 of 182 differ from the ISO copies | Provenance caveat. The identifiers cited here were re-checked in the ISO copies (`K22.wdl:main`, `WINSTART`, `save_versiyon`). |

```
