}

void implicit_declaration_initializers_and_callback_bindings() {
    Fixture f;
    f.state.global("on_esc").value = Value::from_int(99);
    for (auto name : {"on_esc", "on_space", "render_world"}) f.state.global(name).callback = true;
    f.load(R"wdl(
        var positions[3]
        -7,+8,-9;
        var_nsave separated[4] -1 +2 -3;
        var signed_scalar -5;
        ON_ESC NULL;
        ON_SPACE escape;
        RENDER_WORLD = escape;
        function escape() {
            check(separated[0],-1); check(separated[1],2);
            check(separated[2],-3); check(separated[3],0);
            emit(positions[0],positions[1],positions[2],signed_scalar);
        }
        function main() { check(on_esc,null); on_space(); render_world(); }
    )wdl");
    assert(f.events.empty()); // Binding a function must not invoke it during load.
    f.start("main");
    assert(f.events.size() == 2 && f.runtime.processes() == 0);
    f.expect(0, {raw(-7), raw(8), raw(-9), raw(-5)});
    f.expect(1, {raw(-7), raw(8), raw(-9), raw(-5)});
    Fixture invalid;
    invalid.state.global("on_made_up");
    bool rejected = false;
    try {
        invalid.load("function escape() {} ON_MADE_UP escape;");
    } catch (const std::runtime_error&) {
        rejected = true;
    }
    assert(rejected); // A name or ON_* prefix is not a callback catalogue entry.
}

void text_string_property_reads_whitespace_separated_names() {
    Fixture f;
    f.load(R"wdl(
        string line0 = "zero"; string line1 = "one";
        string line2 = "two"; string line3 = "three";
        string line4 = "four"; string line5 = "five";
        string line6 = "six"; string line7 = "seven";
        text caption {
            strings = 8;
            string = line0,line1,line2,line3,line4,line5
                line6,line7;
        }
        function main() {
            caption.index = 7; check(caption.string,line6);
            caption.index = 8; check(caption.string,line7);
            emit(caption.index);
        }
    )wdl");
    const auto& caption = f.state.require(f.state.global("caption").value.bits);
    assert(caption.array.size() == 8);
    const char* names[] = {"line0", "line1", "line2", "line3",
                           "line4", "line5", "line6", "line7"};
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < caption.array.size(); ++i) {
        const auto actual = caption.array[i].value, expected = f.state.global(names[i]).value;
        assert(actual.kind == expected.kind && actual.bits == expected.bits);
    }
    f.start("main");
    assert(f.events.size() == 1 && f.runtime.processes() == 0);
    f.expect(0, {raw(8)});
    Fixture invalid;
    bool rejected = false;
    try {
        invalid.load("function main() { emit(1)\nemit(2); }");
    } catch (const std::runtime_error&) {
        rejected = true;
    }
    assert(rejected); // A newline still cannot replace an executable statement's semicolon.
}

void material_birth_defaults_reach_script_consumers() {
    for (auto profile : {SemanticProfile::CampaignA6, SemanticProfile::BonusA7}) {
        Fixture f;
        f.state.profile = profile;
        f.load(R"wdl(
            MATERIAL ordinary {};
            MATERIAL edited { ambient_red=17; diffuse_blue=0; alpha=0; albedo=0; cycle=3; }
            MATERIAL *born;
            function defaults(m) {
                emit(m.ambient_blue,m.ambient_green,m.ambient_red);
                emit(m.diffuse_blue,m.diffuse_green,m.diffuse_red);
                emit(m.map_blue,m.map_green,m.map_red);
                emit(m.alpha,m.albedo,m.cycle,m.power,m.scale1,m.scale2);
                emit(m.specular_blue,m.specular_green,m.specular_red,
                     m.emissive_blue,m.emissive_green,m.emissive_red,m.skill1,m.skill20);
            }
            function consumer() {
                defaults(ordinary);
                emit(edited.ambient_red,edited.diffuse_blue,edited.alpha,edited.albedo,edited.cycle);
                defaults(born);
            }
        )wdl");
        const auto retired = f.state.create(Object::Kind::Material).id;
        f.state.member(retired, "ambient_red").set(Value::from_int(-17));
        f.state.member(retired, "albedo").set(Value::from_int(-3));
        f.state.member(retired, "skill1").set(Value::from_int(9));
        f.state.retire(retired);
        f.state.global("born").value = Value::object(f.state.create(Object::Kind::Material).id);
        f.start("consumer");
        assert(f.events.size() == 11 && f.runtime.processes() == 0);
        for (auto offset : {0u, 6u}) {
            for (auto channel = 0u; channel < 3; ++channel)
                f.expect(offset + channel, {raw(255), raw(255), raw(255)});
            f.expect(offset + 3, {raw(100), 0xc8df, raw(480), 0, 0, 0});
            f.expect(offset + 4, {0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0});
        }
        f.expect(5, {raw(17), 0, 0, 0, raw(3)});
    }
}

void native_expression_compaction_and_compiler_metadata() {
    Fixture f;
    f.load(R"wdl(
        PLUGINDIR = ".";
        BIND <korublood.bmp>;
        LEVEL <map.wmb>;
        material Mtl_arkakum {};
        STRING phrase = "two words";
        function main() {
            Mtl_ arkakum.ambient_ red = 172;
            check(Mtl_ arkakum.ambient_red,172);
            emit(1 2);
        }
    )wdl");
    const auto& settings = f.runtime.compiler_settings();
    assert(settings.plugin_directory == ".");
    assert(settings.bindings == std::vector<std::string>{"korublood.bmp"});
    assert(settings.levels == std::vector<std::string>{"map.wmb"});
    assert(f.runtime.metrics().directives == 3);
    f.start("main");
    const auto material = f.state.global("Mtl_arkakum").value.bits;
    assert(f.state.member(material, "ambient_red").get().raw() == raw(172));
    const auto phrase = f.state.global("phrase").value.bits;
    assert(f.state.require(phrase).text == "two words");
    assert(f.events.size() == 1 && f.runtime.processes() == 0);
    f.expect(0, {raw(12)});
}

void split_operator_expression_compaction() {
    Fixture f;
    const auto entity = f.entity(7);
    f.load(R"wdl(
        var kursun_hizi = 100;
        var time_scale = 0.5;
        var other = 2;
        var vals[3] = (1 2 3);
        STRING phrase = "two words";
        Entity* focus;
        function main() {
            kursun_hizi*		=time_scale;
            check(kursun_hizi,50);
            other + = 2; check(other,4);
            other - = 2; check(other,2);
            other / = 2; check(other,1);
            other = 7;
            other % = 2; check(other,1);
            other = 7;
            other & = 3; check(other,3);
            other | = 4; check(other,7);
            other ^ = 2; check(other,5);
            check(2 = = 2,1);
            check(2 ! = 3,1);
            check(2 < = 2,1);
            check(2 > = 2,1);
            check(1 & & 1,1);
            check(0 | | 1,1);
            check(2 < < 1,4);
            check(4 > > 1,2);
            other = 2;
            check(+ + other,3); check(other,3);
            check(other + +,3); check(other,4);
            check(- - other,3); check(other,3);
            check(other - -,3); check(other,2);
            check(focus - > skill1,7);
            check(vals[0],1); check(vals[1],2); check(vals[2],3);
            emit(kursun_hizi,other);
        }
    )wdl");
    f.state.global("focus").value = Value::object(entity);
    f.start("main");
    const auto phrase = f.state.global("phrase").value.bits;
    assert(f.state.require(phrase).text == "two words");
    assert(f.events.size() == 1 && f.runtime.processes() == 0);
    f.expect(0, {raw(50), raw(2)});
}

void yielded_child_retains_parameter_and_builtin_argument() {
    Fixture f;
    f.load(R"wdl(
        function child(&value) {
            wait(1); emit(value); value += 7; wait(1); emit(value);
        }
        function value_parent(value) { child(value); }
        function argument_parent() { child(_arg1); }
        function churn() { var local = 999; check(local,999); }
    )wdl");
    f.start("value_parent", {raw(5)});
    assert(f.events.empty() && f.runtime.processes() == 1);
    for (int i = 0; i < 100; ++i) f.start("churn");
    f.runtime.tick(64, 0);
    assert(f.events.size() == 1 && f.runtime.processes() == 1);
    f.expect(0, {raw(5)});
    for (int i = 0; i < 100; ++i) f.start("churn");
    f.runtime.tick(64, 0);
    assert(f.events.size() == 2 && f.runtime.processes() == 0);
    f.expect(1, {raw(12)});
    f.start("argument_parent", {raw(9)});
    for (int i = 0; i < 100; ++i) f.start("churn");
    f.runtime.tick(64, 0);
    assert(f.events.size() == 3 && f.runtime.processes() == 1);
    f.expect(2, {raw(9)});
    for (int i = 0; i < 100; ++i) f.start("churn");
    f.runtime.tick(64, 0);
    assert(f.events.size() == 4 && f.runtime.processes() == 0);
    f.expect(3, {raw(16)});
}

void object_parameter_members_and_arrays() {
    Fixture f;
    const auto entity = f.state.create(Object::Kind::Entity).id;
    f.state.member(entity, "skill27").set(Value::from_int(17));
    auto& vector = f.state.create(Object::Kind::Vector);
    for (auto value : {2, 3, 4}) vector.array.push_back({Value::from_int(value)});
    std::vector<ObjectId> strings;
    for (const auto word : {"first", "second", "third"}) {
        auto& string = f.state.create(Object::Kind::String);
        string.text = word;
        strings.push_back(string.id);
    }
    auto& text = f.state.create(Object::Kind::Text);
    for (auto id : strings) text.array.push_back({Value::object(id)});
    f.state.member(text.id, "index").set(Value::from_int(3));
    f.load(R"wdl(
        function read_entity(e) { emit(e.skill27); }
        function read_array(a) { emit(a[1],a.y); }
        function read_text(t) { return(t.string[1]); }
        function bad_numeric(value) { emit(value.unknownmember); }
    )wdl");
    std::vector<Argument> args{{Value::object(entity), {}}};
    f.runtime.start("read_entity", args);
    args[0].value = Value::object(vector.id);
    f.runtime.start("read_array", args);
    assert(f.events.size() == 2 && f.runtime.processes() == 0);
    f.expect(0, {raw(17)});
    f.expect(1, {raw(3), raw(3)});
    args[0].value = Value::object(text.id);
    const auto returned_string = f.runtime.start("read_text", args);
    assert(returned_string.kind == Value::Kind::Object && returned_string.bits == strings[1]);
    bool rejected = false;
    try {
        f.start("bad_numeric", {raw(5)});
    } catch (const std::runtime_error& error) {
        const std::string_view message(error.what());
        assert(message.find("wdl_regression.wdl:") != std::string_view::npos);
        assert(message.find("member") != std::string_view::npos);
        rejected = true;
    }
    assert(rejected && f.events.size() == 2);
}

void call_arguments_are_captured_right_to_left() {
    Fixture f;
    f.load(R"wdl(
        var i = 0;
        function pair(a,b) { emit(a,b); }
        function main() { pair(i=1,i=2); emit(i++,i++); }
    )wdl");
    f.start("main");
    assert(f.events.size() == 2 && f.runtime.processes() == 0);
    f.expect(0, {raw(1), raw(2)});
    f.expect(1, {raw(2), raw(1)});
    assert(f.state.global("i").value.raw() == raw(3));
}

void resolved_null_callbacks_return_zero_after_arguments() {
    Fixture f;
    f.load(R"wdl(
        FUNCTION* hook;
        VAR table[2] = NULL, enter;
        VAR side_effect = 0;
        FUNCTION accessibility;
        FUNCTION call_shadow(accessibility) { return accessibility(7); }
        FUNCTION main() {
            hook = accessibility;
            check(hook(0),0);
            hook = table[0];
            check(hook(side_effect=1,side_effect=2),0);
            check(side_effect,1);
            check(table[0](side_effect+=1),0);
            check(call_shadow(NULL),0);
            hook = table[1];
            hook(side_effect);
            forward();
        }
        FUNCTION accessibility(old_level) { emit(10,old_level); return 0; }
        FUNCTION enter(old_level) { emit(20,old_level); }
        FUNCTION forward() { emit(30); }
        FUNCTION invalid() { hook=3; hook(); }
        FUNCTION unknown_native() { missing_native(); }
    )wdl");
    f.start("main");
    assert(f.events.size() == 3 && f.runtime.processes() == 0);
    f.expect(0, {raw(10),0});
    f.expect(1, {raw(20),raw(2)});
    f.expect(2, {raw(30)});
    for (auto name : {"invalid", "unknown_native"}) {
        bool rejected = false;
        try { f.start(name); }
        catch (const std::runtime_error& error) {
            assert(std::string_view(error.what()).find("wdl_regression.wdl:") != std::string_view::npos);
            rejected = true;
        }
        assert(rejected);
    }
}

void panel_digits_numeric_binding_warning_policy() {
    Fixture f;
    f.state.global("warn_level").value = Value::from_int(1);
    f.load(R"wdl(
        VAR live_counter = 7;
        STRING wrong_type = "wrong";
        FONT debug_font = "Arial", 1, 14;
        PANEL debug_panel {
            DIGITS = 0,0,"JOY_BUTTONS - %.0f",debug_font,1,JOY_BUTTONS;
            DIGITS = 0,14,"loc_sik - %.0f",debug_font,1,loc_sik;
            DIGITS = 0,28,"live_counter - %.0f",debug_font,1,live_counter;
            DIGITS = 0,42,"wrong_type - %.0f",debug_font,1,wrong_type;
            DIGITS = 0,56,"JOY2_BUTTONS - %.0f",debug_font,1,JOY2_BUTTONS;
            DIGITS = 0,70,"loc_oldmap - %.0f",debug_font,1,loc_oldmap;
        }
        FUNCTION main() { live_counter = 19; }
    )wdl");
    assert(f.state.globals.find("JOY_BUTTONS") == f.state.globals.end());
    assert(f.state.globals.find("loc_sik") == f.state.globals.end());
    assert(!f.state.globals.contains("JOY2_BUTTONS") && !f.state.globals.contains("loc_oldmap"));
    auto& panel = f.state.require(f.state.global("debug_panel").value.bits);
    assert(panel.properties.size() == 6);
    const std::string_view formats[] = {
        "JOY_BUTTONS - %.0f", "loc_sik - %.0f",
        "live_counter - %.0f", "wrong_type - %.0f",
        "JOY2_BUTTONS - %.0f", "loc_oldmap - %.0f"
    };
    assert(panel.properties[0].arguments.size() == 6);
    const auto* fallback = panel.properties[0].arguments[5].ref.slot;
    assert(fallback);
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < panel.properties.size(); ++i) {
        const auto& property = panel.properties[i];
        assert(property.name == "digits" && property.arguments.size() == 6);
        const auto format = property.arguments[2].current();
        assert(format.kind == Value::Kind::Object);
        assert(f.state.require(format.bits).text == formats[i]);
        if (i == 2) continue;
        const auto& target = property.arguments[5];
        assert(target.current().kind == Value::Kind::Number && target.current().raw() == 0);
        assert(target.ref.slot == fallback);
        assert(target.ref.owner == 0 && target.ref.field.empty() && target.ref.bitMask == 0);
    }
    for (const auto& [name, slot] : f.state.globals) {
        (void)name;
        assert(&slot != fallback);
    }
    const auto& live = panel.properties[2].arguments[5];
    assert(live.ref.slot == &f.state.global("live_counter"));
    assert(live.current().raw() == raw(7));
    f.start("main");
    assert(live.current().kind == Value::Kind::Number && live.current().raw() == raw(19));
    panel.properties[0].arguments[5].ref.set(Value::from_int(31));
    for (auto i : {0u,1u,3u,4u,5u})
        assert(panel.properties[i].arguments[5].current().raw() == raw(31));

    const auto rejects = [](int warning_level, std::string_view source,
                            std::string_view unresolved) {
        Fixture strict;
        strict.state.global("warn_level").value = Value::from_int(warning_level);
        bool rejected = false;
        try {
            strict.runtime.load_text("wdl_regression.wdl", source);
        } catch (const std::runtime_error& error) {
            const std::string_view message(error.what());
            assert(message.find("wdl_regression.wdl:") != std::string_view::npos);
            assert(message.find(unresolved) != std::string_view::npos);
            rejected = true;
        }
        assert(rejected);
    };
    rejects(2, R"wdl(
        FONT debug_font = "Arial", 1, 14;
        PANEL debug_panel { DIGITS = 0,0,"loc_sik - %.0f",debug_font,1,loc_sik; }
    )wdl", "loc_sik");
    rejects(2, R"wdl(
        STRING wrong_type = "wrong";
        FONT debug_font = "Arial", 1, 14;
        PANEL debug_panel { DIGITS = 0,0,"wrong_type - %.0f",debug_font,1,wrong_type; }
    )wdl", "wrong_type");
    rejects(2, R"wdl(
        STRING* wrong_pointer;
        PANEL debug_panel { DIGITS = 0,0,4,NULL,1,wrong_pointer; }
    )wdl", "wrong_pointer");
    rejects(2, R"wdl(
        BMAP track = <track.tga>;
        PANEL controls { HSLIDER = 0,0,100,track,0,100,missing_slider; }
    )wdl", "missing_slider");
    rejects(2, R"wdl(
        BMAP track = <track.tga>;
        PANEL controls { WINDOW = 0,0,20,20,track,missing_x,missing_y; }
    )wdl", "missing_x");
    rejects(1, R"wdl(
        PANEL debug_panel { DIGITS = 0,0,4,NULL,1,unknown_expression+1; }
    )wdl", "unknown_expression");
    rejects(1, "FUNCTION main() { emit(undeclared); }", "undeclared");
    rejects(1, R"wdl(
        VAR live_counter = 7;
        PANEL debug_panel { DIGITS = 0,0,"%.0f",unknown_font,1,live_counter; }
    )wdl", "unknown_font");
    rejects(1, R"wdl(
        VAR live_counter = 7;
        FONT debug_font = "Arial", 1, 14;
        PANEL debug_panel { DIGITS = unknown_x,0,"%.0f",debug_font,1,live_counter; }
    )wdl", "unknown_x");
}

void numeric_control_bindings_preserve_references_and_flags() {
    Fixture f;
    f.state.global("warn_level").value = Value::from_int(2);
    f.load(R"wdl(
        VAR counter = 7;
        VAR numbers[2] = 3,4;
        PANEL subject { VISIBLE = ON; }
        BMAP track = <track.tga>;
        FONT face = "Arial",1,14;
        PANEL controls {
            DIGITS = 0,0,"%.0f",face,1,numbers[1];
            DIGITS = 0,0,"%.0f",face,1,counter.y;
            DIGITS = 0,0,"%.0f",face,1,subject.visible;
            HSLIDER = 0,0,100,track,0,100,counter;
            WINDOW = 0,0,20,20,track,numbers[1],counter.y;
        }
        FUNCTION main() { numbers[1]=9; counter.y=11; counter=13; subject.visible=OFF; }
    )wdl");
    auto& properties = f.state.require(f.state.global("controls").value.bits).properties;
    assert(properties.size() == 5);
    auto& array = properties[0].arguments[5];
    auto& member = properties[1].arguments[5];
    auto& flag = properties[2].arguments[5];
    assert(array.ref.slot && array.ref.index == 1);
    assert(member.ref.slot && member.ref.field == "y");
    assert(flag.ref.slot && flag.ref.bitMask == 0x4000u);
    assert(properties[3].arguments[6].ref.slot == &f.state.global("counter"));
    assert(properties[4].arguments[5].ref.slot == array.ref.slot);
    assert(properties[4].arguments[6].ref.slot == member.ref.slot);
    f.start("main");
    assert(array.current().raw() == raw(9) && member.current().raw() == raw(11));
    assert(flag.current().raw() == 0 && properties[3].arguments[6].current().raw() == raw(13));
    flag.ref.set(Value::from_int(1));
    assert(flag.current().raw() == raw(1));

    f.state.global("warn_level").value = Value::from_int(1);
    f.load(R"wdl(
        BMAP track = <track.tga>;
        PANEL controls {
            HSLIDER = 0,0,100,track,0,100,missing_slider;
            WINDOW = 0,0,20,20,track,missing_x,missing_y;
        }
    )wdl");
    auto& fallback = f.state.require(f.state.global("controls").value.bits).properties;
    const auto& slider = fallback[0].arguments[6];
    const auto& x = fallback[1].arguments[5];
    const auto& y = fallback[1].arguments[6];
    assert(slider.ref.slot == &f.state.numericBindingFallback);
    assert(x.ref.slot == slider.ref.slot && y.ref.slot == slider.ref.slot);
    slider.ref.set(Value::from_int(17));
    assert(x.current().raw() == raw(17) && y.current().raw() == raw(17));
    assert(!f.state.globals.contains("missing_slider") && !f.state.globals.contains("missing_x")
           && !f.state.globals.contains("missing_y"));
    const auto persistent = slider.ref;
    f.load("PANEL reader { DIGITS=0,0,4,NULL,1,another_unknown; }");
    const auto& reloaded = f.state.require(f.state.global("reader").value.bits).properties[0].arguments[5];
    assert(reloaded.ref.slot == persistent.slot && reloaded.current().raw() == raw(17));
    assert(persistent.get().raw() == raw(17));
}

void obsolete_window_is_parsed_without_finalizing() {
    Fixture f;
    f.runtime.load_text("wdl_regression.wdl", R"wdl(
        WINDOW WINSTART { BG_COLOR RGB(0,0,0); MODE IMAGE; };
    )wdl");
    f.runtime.tick(64, 0); // Evaluating RGB would trigger the fixture's unknown-builtin error.
    assert(f.state.globals.find("WINSTART") == f.state.globals.end());
    bool native_diagnostic = false;
    for (const auto& diagnostic : f.runtime.diagnostics())

The packager tools/package_kabus_appimage.py assembles a genuine x86-64 Type-2
ELF AppImage with a SquashFS payload. It does not build the engine, execute any
Windows game/setup program, or include original game data, scripts, proprietary
SDKs, mod archives or game artwork. The generic SVG icon is packaging artwork;
the installer obtains original game artwork only from user-supplied media.

  The native engine, not installer flags or copied WDL, owns the default for
  an automatically selected, recognized original K22.wdl campaign. ISO-only
  installation includes recovered resolution and state-dependent menu/HUD/text
  geometry with original media artwork, including its illustration/eye animation.
  No proprietary community-patch scripts, replacement artwork or Windows DLLs

innoextract 1.9 (2020-08-09)
 - Added preliminary support for Inno Setup 6.1.0
 - Added support for a modified Inno Setup 5.4.2 variant
 - Fixed output directory being created for unsupported installers
 - Fixed some safe non-ASCII characters being stripped from filenames
 - Fixed handling of path separators in Japanese and Korean installers
 - Fixed build with newer Boost versions
 - Windows: Fixed heap corruption
 - Windows: Fixed garbled output

innoextract 1.8 (2019-09-15)
 - Added support for Inno Setup 6.0.0 installers
 - Added support for pre-release Inno Setup 5.6.2 installers used by GOG
 - Added support for two modified Inno Setup 5.5.7 variants
 - Added support for Inno Setup 1.3.0 to 1.3.23
 - Added support for My Inno Setup Extensions installers older than 3.0.6.1
 - Added support for modified Inno Setup variants using an alternative setup loader magic
 - Added support for using boost_{zlib,bzip2} when statically linking Boost
 - Added support for automatically reading external setup.0 files
 - Encoding for non-Unicode installers is now determined from the languages supported by the installer, overridable using the --codepage option
 - Implemented parsing of GOG Galaxy architecture constraints
 - The architecture-specific suffixes @32bit and @64bit are now used to disambiguate colliding files
 - Fixed extracting files from slices larger than 2 GiB with 32-bit builds
 - Fixed output path for files with absolute paths (canonicalization now strips all unsafe characters)
 - Fixed output directory being created even when not extracting files
 - Fixed a hang when using the --language option
 - Improved checksum verification for files reconstructed from GOG Galaxy file parts
 - Changed header parsing to select the first version without warnings and failing that the first without errors
 - Changed filesystem and output encoding to WTF-8 (extended UTF-8) to represent broken UTF-16 data

innoextract 1.7 (2018-06-12)
 - Added support for Inno Setup 5.6.0 installers
 - Added support for new GOG installers with GOG Galaxy file parts
 - Added support for encrypted installers with the --password (-P) and --password-file options
 - Added a --show-password option to print password check information
 - Added a --check-password option to abort if the provided password does not match the stored checksum
 - Added a --info (-i) convenience option to print information about the installer
 - Added a --list-sizes option to print file sizes even with --quiet or --silent
 - Added a --list-checksums option to print file checksums
 - Added a --data-version (-V) option to print the data version and exit
 - Added a --no-extract-unknown (-n) option to abort on unknown Inno Setup data versions
 - Fixed building in paths that contain regex expressions
 - Fixed case-sensitivity in parent directory when creating subdirectories
 - Fixed .bin slice file names used with Inno Setup versions older than 4.1.7
 - Fixed build with newer libc++ versions
 - Made loading of .bin slice files case-insensitive
 - The --test option can now be combined with --extract to abort on file checksum errors
 - Now compiles in C++17 mode if supported

innoextract 1.6 (2016-03-24)
 - Added support for Inno Setup 5.5.7 (and 5.5.8) installers
 - Added a --collisions=rename-all option
 - Changed --collisions=rename to omit the suffix for the file that would have been extracted with --collisions=overwrite instead of the first encountered file
 - Fixed @lang suffix sometimes missing for the first file with the --collisions=rename option
 - Fixed build error with CMake 3.5
 - Now compiles in C++14 mode if supported
 - Unsafe characters in special constant strings (ie ':' in {code:…}) are now replaced with '$'
 - Windows: Fixed error message if the source file could not be opened
 - Windows: Fixed progress bar flickering while printing extracted filenames
 - Windows binaries: Fixed crash on platforms without AVX support

innoextract 1.5 (2015-09-24)
 - Added support for Inno Setup 5.5.6 installers
 - Added support for a modified Inno Setup 5.5.0 variant
 - Added support for building without iconv (Windows-1252 and UTF-16LE only)
 - Added warnings for .bin files that are not part of the installer
 - Added a simple --include (-I) option to filter files thanks to Alexandre Detiste
 - Added a --list-languages option to list available languages
 - Added a --exclude-temp (-m) option to not extract temporary files
 - Added a --language-only option to skip language-independent files
 - Added a --collisions option to abort or rename files on collision
 - Added a --default-language option to prefer a language in case of file collisions
 - Added a --gog-game-id option to print the GOG.com game ID for Galaxy-ready installers
 - Added a --gog (-g) option to extract additional .bin files using unrar or unar
 - Fixed handling of spaces in the --data-dir option
 - Fixed an infinite loop with truncated LZMA streams
 - Fixed handling of forward slashes in stored file paths
 - Fixed size display for powers of 1024
 - Fixed loading headers if there are encrypted chunks
 - Fixed file collisions not being handled case-insensitively
 - Files will now be extracted into the same directory even if the stored case differs
 - Empty directories are now created correctly when extracting
 - Skipped files in encrypted chunks are now listed individually
 - Temporary files are now marked in file listings
 - Error summary is now written to stderr when using --quiet
 - Colors are now only enabled automatically if $TERM is set to something other than "dumb"
 - Improved error and warning messages
 - Build system improvements
 - Debug output can now be enabled separately from debug builds
 - Windows: Added support for using the Win32 API for string encoding conversion
 - Windows: Fixed unicode console output

`packaging/helper-innoextract/README`:

```

=================================================================
 innoextract - A tool to unpack installers created by Inno Setup
=================================================================

Inno Setup (https://jrsoftware.org/isinfo.php) is a tool to create installers for Microsoft
Windows applications. innoextract allows to extract such installers under non-Windows systems
without running the actual installer using wine. innoextract currently supports installers
created by Inno Setup 1.2.10 to 6.0.5.

In addition to standard Inno Setup installers, innoextract also supports some modified Inno
Setup variants including Martijn Laan's My Inno Setup Extensions 3.0.6.1 as well as GOG.com's
Inno Setup-based game installers.

innoextract is available under the ZLIB license - see the LICENSE file.

See the website for Linux packages (https://constexpr.org/innoextract/#packages).


 Contact
=========

Website: https://constexpr.org/innoextract/

Author: Daniel Scharrer (https://constexpr.org/)


 Requirements
==============

i686: glibc 2.6+
amd64: glibc 2.6+
armv6j-hardfloat: glibc 2.14+


 Run
=====

To extract a setup file to the current directory run:

    $ ./innoextract <file>

A list of available options can be retrieved using

    $ ./innoextract --help

Documentation is also available as a man page:

    $ man doc/innoextract.1}


 Limitations
=============

 - There is no support for extracting individual components and limited support for filtering
   by name.

 - Included scripts and checks are not executed.

 - The mapping from Inno Setup variables like the application directory to subdirectories
   is hard-coded.

 - Names for data slice/disk files in multi-file installers must follow the standard naming scheme.

A perhaps more complete, but Windows-only, tool to extract Inno Setup files is innounp
(http://innounp.sourceforge.net/).

Extracting Windows installer executables created by programs other than Inno Setup is out of
the scope of this project. Some of these can be unpacked by the following programs:

 - cabextract: https://cabextract.org.uk/

 - unshield: https://github.com/twogood/unshield


 Disclaimer
============

This project is in no way associated with Inno Setup or https://jrsoftware.org/.

```

Command: readelf --wide --file-header --program-headers --dynamic --notes --version-info --dyn-syms bin/amd64/innoextract

ELF Header:
  Magic:   7f 45 4c 46 02 01 01 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 
  Class:                             ELF64
  Data:                              2's complement, little endian
  Version:                           1 (current)
  OS/ABI:                            UNIX - System V
  ABI Version:                       0
  Type:                              EXEC (Executable file)
  Machine:                           Advanced Micro Devices X86-64
  Version:                           0x1

`packaging/helper-innoextract/upstream/gcc-bindist-x86-64_lto-options.txt`:

```txt
export CFLAGS="-Wno-odr -static-libgcc -flto"
export CXXFLAGS="-Wno-odr -static-libgcc -flto -static-libstdc++"
export LDFLAGS="-static-libgcc -static-libstdc++ -flto -fuse-linker-plugin"
cmake --no-warn-unused-cli innoextract/ -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/ "-DCMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE=Toolchains/x86_64-bindist-linux-gnu-toolchain.cmake" -DUSE_STATIC_LIBS=1 "-DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=Deps/Qt-5.1-64"
make --keep-going --no-print-directory

`packaging/runtime-uruntime/crates/memfd-exec-0.2.6/upstream/README.md`:

```md
# memfd_exec ![crates.io](https://img.shields.io/crates/v/memfd-exec.svg)

This is a very simple crate that allows execution of in-memory only programs. Simply
put, if you have the contents of a Linux executable in a `Vec<u8>`, you can use
`memfd_exec` to execute the program without it ever touching your hard disk. Use
cases for this may include:

* Bundling a static executable with another program (for example, my motivation to
  create this package is that I want to ship a statically built QEMU with
  [cantrace](https://github.com/novafacing/cannoli))
* Sending executables over the network and running them, to reduce footprint and increase
  throughput
* Really hacky stuff that I haven't thought of, if you have a cool use case, feel free
  to make a PR to the README or add an example in [examples](examples)

## Using

Just include `memfd-exec = "0.2.5"` in your `Cargo.toml` file.

## Features

* Feature-parity API with `process::Command`, the only difference is we don't execute
  anything from disk.
* Only two dependencies

## Examples

### Run an executable downloaded over the network

For redteamers, this example will download and run an executable without ever writing it
to disk. It may not bypass Advanced Threat Protection, but it at least won't leave
a huge disk footprint!

```rust
use memfd_exec::{MemFdExecutable, Stdio};
use reqwest::blocking::get;

const URL: &str = "https://novafacing.github.io/assets/qemu-x86_64";
let resp = get(URL).unwrap();

// The `MemFdExecutable` struct is at near feature-parity with `std::process::Command`,
// so you can use it in the same way. The only difference is that you must provide the
// argv[0] to use as well as the executable contents as a byte slice.
let qemu = MemFdExecutable::new("qemu-x86_64", resp.bytes().unwrap().to_vec())
    // We'll just get the version here, but you can do anything you want with the
    // args.
    .arg("-version")
    // We'll capture the stdout of the process, so we need to set up a pipe.
    .stdout(Stdio::piped())
    // Spawn the process as a forked child
    .spawn()
    .unwrap();

// Get the output and status code of the process (this will block until the process
// exits)
let output = qemu.wait_with_output().unwrap();
assert!(output.status.into_raw() == 0);
// Print out the version we got!
println!("{}", String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout));
```

### Bundle and run a local static executable

The motivating example for this project is to bundle an executable along with a rust
program and be able to run the executable straight from memory instead of going
through the tedious and slow process of writing the executable file to disk and then
invoking it as a command.

This example creates an executable with a bundled [program](tests/test_static.c) that
opens a socket, reads a bit of input, and then prints out the input. Of course, the
logical extension of the idea would be to use a static
[netcat](https://github.com/openbsd/src/blob/master/usr.bin/nc/netcat.c) build or some
such thing.

```rust

use memfd_exec::{MemFdExecutable, Stdio};

const EXECUTABLE_FILE: &[u8] = include_bytes!("tets/test_static");

fn main() {
    const PORT = 1234;
    // We create an in-memory executable with an argv[0] "test" and an executable file
    // that we embedded in our rust binary
    let exe = MemFdExecutable::new("test", EXECUTABLE_FILE.to_vec())
        // We pass one arg, the port number to listen on
        .arg(format!("{}", PORT))
        // We tell it to use a pipe for stdout (stdin and stderr will default to Stdio::inherit())
        .stdout(Stdio::piped())
        // We spawn the child process as a forked child process
        .spawn()
        .expect("Failed to create process!");

    // Wait until the process finishes and print its output
    let output = exe.wait_with_output().unwrap();
    println!("Got output: {:?}", output.stdout);
}
```

## Testing

For testing purposes, you need to install:

- `clang`
- `glibc-static`
- `glibc`

You should also have `/bin/cat` and `/bin/ls` on your system. This is default on the
vast majority of Linux systems, but don't panic if this test fails if they are missing.

`packaging/runtime-uruntime/xz-COPYING`:

```

XZ Utils Licensing
==================

    Different licenses apply to different files in this package. Here
    is a summary of which licenses apply to which parts of this package:

      - liblzma is under the BSD Zero Clause License (0BSD).

      - The command line tools xz, xzdec, lzmadec, and lzmainfo are
        under 0BSD except that, on systems that don't have a usable
        getopt_long, GNU getopt_long is compiled and linked in from the
        'lib' directory. The getopt_long code is under GNU LGPLv2.1+.

      - The scripts to grep, diff, and view compressed files have been
        adapted from GNU gzip. These scripts (xzgrep, xzdiff, xzless,
        and xzmore) are under GNU GPLv2+. The man pages of the scripts
        are under 0BSD; they aren't based on the man pages of GNU gzip.

      - Most of the XZ Utils specific documentation that is in
        plain text files (like README, INSTALL, PACKAGERS, NEWS,
        and ChangeLog) are under 0BSD unless stated otherwise in
        the file itself. The files xz-file-format.txt and
        lzma-file-format.xt are in the public domain but may
        be distributed under the terms of 0BSD too.

      - Translated messages and man pages are under 0BSD except that
        some old translations are in the public domain.

      - Test files and test code in the 'tests' directory, and
        debugging utilities in the 'debug' directory are under
        the BSD Zero Clause License (0BSD).

      - The GNU Autotools based build system contains files that are
        under GNU GPLv2+, GNU GPLv3+, and a few permissive licenses.
        These files don't affect the licensing of the binaries being
        built.

      - The 'extra' directory contains files that are under various
        free software licenses. These aren't built or installed as
        part of XZ Utils.

    The following command may be helpful in finding per-file license
    information. It works on xz.git and on a clean file tree extracted
    from a release tarball.

        sh build-aux/license-check.sh -v

    For the files under the BSD Zero Clause License (0BSD), if
    a copyright notice is needed, the following is sufficient:

        Copyright (C) The XZ Utils authors and contributors

    If you copy significant amounts of 0BSD-licensed code from XZ Utils
    into your project, acknowledging this somewhere in your software is
    polite (especially if it is proprietary, non-free software), but
    it is not legally required by the license terms. Here is an example
    of a good notice to put into "about box" or into documentation:

        This software includes code from XZ Utils <https://tukaani.org/xz/>.

    The following license texts are included in the following files:
      - COPYING.0BSD: BSD Zero Clause License
      - COPYING.LGPLv2.1: GNU Lesser General Public License version 2.1
      - COPYING.GPLv2: GNU General Public License version 2
      - COPYING.GPLv3: GNU General Public License version 3

    If you have questions, don't hesitate to ask for more information.
    The contact information is in the README file.

case, there is little to gain by limiting the free library to free

`reverse/scripts/ExportEmbeddedPcx.java`:

```java
// Export an embedded PCX verbatim without modifying the Ghidra program.
// @category Kabus22
// Usage: ExportEmbeddedPcx.java OUTPUT_DIRECTORY IMAGE_ADDRESS [POINTER_ADDRESS [PE_FILE ...]]
// Headless: analyzeHeadless PROJECT_DIRECTORY PROJECT_NAME -process K22.exe -noanalysis -readOnly
//           -scriptPath SCRIPT_DIRECTORY -postScript ExportEmbeddedPcx.java OUTPUT_DIRECTORY 0062130c 00627310
// Single-plane images require the original 0x0c + 768-byte palette immediately after RLE.

import java.io.BufferedInputStream;
import java.io.InputStream;
import java.io.IOException;
import java.io.OutputStream;
import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets;
import java.nio.file.Files;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.nio.file.StandardCopyOption;
import java.security.MessageDigest;
import java.util.HexFormat;

import ghidra.app.script.GhidraScript;
import ghidra.program.model.address.Address;
import ghidra.program.model.address.AddressOverflowException;
import ghidra.program.model.mem.MemoryAccessException;

public class ExportEmbeddedPcx extends GhidraScript {
    private static final long MAX_DECODED_BYTES = 64L * 1024 * 1024;

    @Override
    public void run() throws Exception {
        String[] args = getScriptArgs();
        if (args.length < 2) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException(
                "Expected OUTPUT_DIRECTORY IMAGE_ADDRESS [POINTER_ADDRESS [PE_FILE ...]]");
        }
        if (currentProgram == null) {
            throw new IllegalStateException("An open program is required");
        }
        Address image = toAddr(args[1]);
        if (image == null) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Invalid image address: " + args[1]);
        }
        byte[] header = new byte[128];
        readBytes(image, 0, header, header.length, "128-byte PCX header");
        require((header[0] & 255) == 10, "PCX manufacturer must be 10");
        require((header[2] & 255) == 1, "Only PCX RLE encoding 1 is supported");
        require((header[3] & 255) == 8, "Only 8 bits per pixel per plane are supported");
        int width = u16(header, 8) - u16(header, 4) + 1;
        int height = u16(header, 10) - u16(header, 6) + 1;
        int planes = header[65] & 255;
        int bytesPerLine = u16(header, 66);
        require(width > 0 && height > 0, "PCX dimensions must be positive");
        require(planes == 1 || planes == 3, "Only 1-plane or 3-plane PCX is supported");
        require(bytesPerLine >= width, "PCX bytesPerLine must be at least width");
        long expected = (long) height * planes * bytesPerLine;
        require(expected <= MAX_DECODED_BYTES,
            "Decoded PCX size " + expected + " exceeds the 64 MiB limit");

        // Count decoded bytes, including scanline padding; never allocate a decoded bitmap.
        long offset = 128;
        long decoded = 0;
        long nextCancellationCheck = 0;
        while (decoded < expected) {
            if (decoded >= nextCancellationCheck) {
                monitor.checkCancelled();
                nextCancellationCheck = decoded + 65536;
            }
            long tokenOffset = offset;
            int token = readByte(image, offset++, "PCX RLE token");
            int count = 1;
            if ((token & 0xc0) == 0xc0) {
                count = token & 0x3f;
                require(count != 0, "Zero-length PCX RLE run at image offset " + tokenOffset);
                require(count <= expected - decoded,
                    "PCX RLE run at image offset " + tokenOffset + " exceeds decoded size " + expected);
                readByte(image, offset++, "PCX RLE run value");
            }
            decoded += count;
        }
        long rleEndOffset = offset;
        Address rleEnd = addressAt(image, rleEndOffset, "PCX RLE end (exclusive)");
        String palette;
        if (planes == 1) {
            require(readByte(image, offset, "PCX palette marker") == 0x0c,
                "Single-plane PCX without an immediate 0x0c + 768-byte palette is unsupported; no palette is invented");
            byte[] trailer = new byte[769];
            readBytes(image, offset, trailer, trailer.length, "original PCX 256-color palette trailer");
            offset += trailer.length;
            palette = "original 0x0c marker and 768 RGB palette bytes retained";
        } else {
            palette = "none (3-plane RGB)";
        }

        String pointerReport = "";
        if (args.length >= 3) {
            Address pointer = toAddr(args[2]);
            if (pointer == null) {
                throw new IllegalArgumentException("Invalid pointer address: " + args[2]);
            }
            int size = currentProgram.getDefaultPointerSize();
            require(size >= 1 && size <= 8, "Unsupported pointer width: " + size);
            byte[] bytes = new byte[size];
            readBytes(pointer, 0, bytes, size, "image pointer value");
            long value = 0;
            boolean bigEndian = currentProgram.getLanguage().isBigEndian();
            for (int i = 0; i < size; i++) {
                int index = bigEndian ? i : size - 1 - i;
                value = (value << 8) | (bytes[index] & 255L);
            }
            pointerReport = "pointerVA=" + pointer + "\npointerBytes=" + size +
                "\npointerValue=0x" + String.format("%0" + (size * 2) + "x", value) + "\n";
        }

        Path directory = Path.of(args[0]);
        Files.createDirectories(directory);
        String stem = currentProgram.getName().replaceAll("[^A-Za-z0-9._-]", "_") + "." +
            image.toString().replaceAll("[^A-Za-z0-9._-]", "_");
        Path pcx = directory.resolve(stem + ".pcx");
        Path report = directory.resolve(stem + ".pcx.txt");
        Path temporary = Files.createTempFile(directory, stem + ".", ".pcx.tmp");
        MessageDigest digest = MessageDigest.getInstance("SHA-256");
        String sha256;
        StringBuilder provenance = new StringBuilder();
        try {
            try (OutputStream output = Files.newOutputStream(temporary)) {
                byte[] buffer = new byte[16384];
                for (long copied = 0; copied < offset;) {
                    monitor.checkCancelled();
                    int length = (int) Math.min(buffer.length, offset - copied);
                    readBytes(image, copied, buffer, length, "validated encoded PCX bytes");
                    output.write(buffer, 0, length);
                    digest.update(buffer, 0, length);
                    copied += length;
                }
            }
            sha256 = HexFormat.of().formatHex(digest.digest());
            for (int i = 3; i < args.length; i++) {
                provenance.append(scanFile(Path.of(args[i]), header, expected, planes, sha256));
            }
            Files.move(temporary, pcx, StandardCopyOption.REPLACE_EXISTING);
        } finally {
            Files.deleteIfExists(temporary);
        }
        String text = "program=" + currentProgram.getName() + "\nimageVA=" + image +
            "\nwidth=" + width + "\nheight=" + height + "\nplanes=" + planes +
            "\nbytesPerLine=" + bytesPerLine + "\ndecodedBytes=" + expected +
            "\nrleStartVA=" + addressAt(image, 128, "PCX RLE start") +
            "\nrleEndVAExclusive=" + rleEnd + "\nrleEncodedLength=" + (rleEndOffset - 128) +
            "\npcxLength=" + offset + "\npalette=" + palette +
            "\nsha256=" + sha256 + "\n" + pointerReport + provenance;
        Files.writeString(report, text, StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
        println("Embedded PCX exported to " + pcx.toAbsolutePath());
        println("Extraction report: " + report.toAbsolutePath());
    }

    private record Candidate(long fileOffset, long rleLength, long payloadLength, String sha256) {}

    private String scanFile(Path file, byte[] header, long expected, int planes, String imageSha)
            throws Exception {
        int headerMatches = 0;
        int validCandidates = 0;
        Candidate candidate = null;
        String lastFailure = "no exact header found";
        // Preserve 127 bytes between chunks so headers crossing chunk boundaries are found once.
        byte[] buffer = new byte[65536 + 127];
        long base = 0;
        int carry = 0;
        try (InputStream input = Files.newInputStream(file)) {
            while (true) {
                monitor.checkCancelled();
                int fresh = input.readNBytes(buffer, carry, 65536);
                if (fresh == 0) {
                    break;
                }
                int length = carry + fresh;
                for (int start = 0; start <= length - header.length; start++) {
                    if (buffer[start] != header[0]) {
                        continue;
                    }
                    int matched = 1;
                    while (matched < header.length && buffer[start + matched] == header[matched]) {
                        matched++;
                    }
                    if (matched != header.length) {
                        continue;
                    }
                    headerMatches++;
                    try {
                        Candidate found = validateFileCandidate(file, base + start, header, expected, planes);
                        validCandidates++;
                        candidate = found;
                    } catch (IOException e) {
                        lastFailure = "candidate at 0x" + Long.toHexString(base + start) + ": " + e.getMessage();
                    }
                }
                carry = Math.min(127, length);
                base += length - carry;
                System.arraycopy(buffer, length - carry, buffer, 0, carry);
            }
        }
        require(validCandidates == 1, "Expected one validated PCX in " + file +
            ", found " + validCandidates + " (exact header matches " + headerMatches +
            "; last rejected candidate: " + lastFailure + ")");
        return "\nsourceFile=" + file.toAbsolutePath() +
            "\nsourceHeaderMatches=" + headerMatches +
            "\nsourceValidCandidateCount=" + validCandidates +
            "\nsourcePhysicalFileOffset=0x" + Long.toHexString(candidate.fileOffset()) +
            "\nsourceRleEncodedLength=" + candidate.rleLength() +
            "\nsourcePayloadLength=" + candidate.payloadLength() +
            "\nsourceSha256=" + candidate.sha256() +
            "\nsourceMatchesExport=" + candidate.sha256().equals(imageSha) + "\n";
    }

    private Candidate validateFileCandidate(Path file, long start, byte[] header, long expected, int planes)
            throws Exception {
        MessageDigest digest = MessageDigest.getInstance("SHA-256");
        digest.update(header);
        long encodedLength = 0;
        long decoded = 0;
        long nextCancellationCheck = 0;
        try (InputStream input = new BufferedInputStream(Files.newInputStream(file))) {
            input.skipNBytes(start + header.length);
            while (decoded < expected) {
                if (decoded >= nextCancellationCheck) {
                    monitor.checkCancelled();
                    nextCancellationCheck = decoded + 65536;
                }
                int token = input.read();
                require(token >= 0, "Truncated RLE token after " + encodedLength + " encoded bytes");
                digest.update((byte) token);
                encodedLength++;
                int count = 1;
                if ((token & 0xc0) == 0xc0) {
                    count = token & 0x3f;
                    require(count > 0, "Zero-length RLE run");
                    require(count <= expected - decoded, "RLE run exceeds decoded size " + expected);
                    int value = input.read();
                    require(value >= 0, "Truncated RLE run value");
                    digest.update((byte) value);
                    encodedLength++;
                }
                decoded += count;
            }
            long payloadLength = header.length + encodedLength;
            if (planes == 1) {
                int marker = input.read();
                require(marker == 0x0c, "Missing original 256-color palette marker");
                digest.update((byte) marker);
                for (int i = 0; i < 768; i++) {
                    int color = input.read();
                    require(color >= 0, "Truncated original 256-color palette");
                    digest.update((byte) color);
                }
                payloadLength += 769;
            }
            return new Candidate(start, encodedLength, payloadLength, HexFormat.of().formatHex(digest.digest()));
        }
    }

    private static int u16(byte[] bytes, int offset) {
        return (bytes[offset] & 255) | ((bytes[offset + 1] & 255) << 8);
    }

    private static void require(boolean valid, String message) throws IOException {
        if (!valid) {
            throw new IOException(message);
        }
    }

    private Address addressAt(Address base, long offset, String purpose) throws IOException {
        try {
            return base.addNoWrap(offset);
        } catch (AddressOverflowException e) {
            throw new IOException("Address overflow reading " + purpose + " at " + base +
                " + " + offset, e);
        }
    }

    private int readByte(Address base, long offset, String purpose) throws IOException {
        Address address = addressAt(base, offset, purpose);
        try {
            return currentProgram.getMemory().getByte(address) & 255;
        } catch (MemoryAccessException e) {
            throw new IOException("Missing/uninitialized memory reading " + purpose + " at " +
                address + " (image offset " + offset + ")", e);
        }
    }

    private void readBytes(Address base, long offset, byte[] buffer, int length, String purpose)
            throws IOException {
        Address address = addressAt(base, offset, purpose);
        addressAt(base, offset + length - 1L, purpose);
        try {
            int actual = currentProgram.getMemory().getBytes(address, buffer, 0, length);
            require(actual == length, "Truncated " + purpose + " at " + address +
                ": expected " + length + " bytes, read " + actual);
        } catch (MemoryAccessException e) {
            throw new IOException("Missing/uninitialized memory reading " + purpose + " at " +
                address + " (offset " + offset + ", length " + length + ")", e);
        }
    }
}

`reverse/scripts/RecoverKabus.java`:

```java
// Export address-backed loader/scheduler/plugin evidence without modifying the program.
// @category Kabus22
// Usage: RecoverKabus.java OUTPUT_DIRECTORY [MAX_FUNCTIONS=120] [TIMEOUT_SECONDS=20] [ADDRESS ...]
// Headless: analyzeHeadless PROJECT_DIRECTORY PROJECT_NAME -process '*' -noanalysis -readOnly
//           -scriptPath SCRIPT_DIRECTORY -postScript RecoverKabus.java OUTPUT_DIRECTORY

import java.io.BufferedWriter;
import java.io.IOException;
import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets;
import java.nio.file.Files;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.Comparator;
import java.util.LinkedHashMap;
import java.util.LinkedHashSet;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.Set;
import java.util.regex.Pattern;

import ghidra.app.decompiler.DecompInterface;
import ghidra.app.decompiler.DecompileResults;
import ghidra.app.script.GhidraScript;
import ghidra.program.model.address.Address;
import ghidra.program.model.address.AddressIterator;
import ghidra.program.model.data.StringDataInstance;
import ghidra.program.model.listing.Data;
import ghidra.program.model.listing.DataIterator;
import ghidra.program.model.listing.Function;
import ghidra.program.model.listing.FunctionIterator;
import ghidra.program.model.symbol.ExternalLocation;
import ghidra.program.model.symbol.Reference;
import ghidra.program.model.symbol.ReferenceIterator;
import ghidra.program.model.symbol.Symbol;
import ghidra.program.model.symbol.SymbolIterator;
import ghidra.program.util.DefinedStringIterator;

public class RecoverKabus extends GhidraScript {
    private static final Pattern RELEVANT = Pattern.compile(
        "(?i)(wrs|wdl|acknex|gamestudio|_a4font|txt_load|str_read|delimit_str|resource|archive|pars(?:e|er|ing)|script|compil|" +
        "(?:^|[^a-z])(?:wait|proc|execute|version)(?:[^a-z]|$)|video_set|Direct3DCreate9|\\b[67]\\.\\d{2}\\b)");
    private final Map<Address, Function> candidates = new LinkedHashMap<>();
    private final Map<Address, Set<String>> reasons = new LinkedHashMap<>();
    private final Map<Address, Integer> priorities = new LinkedHashMap<>();
    private BufferedWriter report;

    @Override
    public void run() throws Exception {
        String[] args = getScriptArgs();
        if (args.length == 0) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Expected OUTPUT_DIRECTORY [MAX_FUNCTIONS] [TIMEOUT_SECONDS] [ADDRESS ...]");
        }
        int maxFunctions = args.length > 1 ? Integer.parseInt(args[1]) : 120;
        int timeout = args.length > 2 ? Integer.parseInt(args[2]) : 20;
        if (maxFunctions < 1 || timeout < 1 || timeout > 300) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("MAX_FUNCTIONS must be positive; TIMEOUT_SECONDS must be 1..300");
        }
        Path directory = Path.of(args[0]);
        Files.createDirectories(directory);
        String name = currentProgram.getName().replaceAll("[^A-Za-z0-9._-]", "_");
        Path target = directory.resolve(name + ".recovery.txt");
        try (BufferedWriter writer = Files.newBufferedWriter(target, StandardCharsets.UTF_8)) {
            report = writer;
            metadata();
            imports();
            exports();
            strings();
            symbols();
            for (int i = 3; i < args.length; i++) {
                Address address = toAddr(args[i]);
                Function function = currentProgram.getFunctionManager().getFunctionContaining(address);
                if (function == null) {
                    line("EXPLICIT_ADDRESS_NOT_IN_FUNCTION " + address);
                    Data data = currentProgram.getListing().getDataContaining(address);
                    line("EXPLICIT_DATA " + address + " defined=" + (data == null ? "none" : data.toString()));
                    byte[] bytes = new byte[64];
                    int read = currentProgram.getMemory().getBytes(address, bytes);
                    StringBuilder hex = new StringBuilder();
                    for (int j = 0; j < read; j++) hex.append(String.format("%02x", bytes[j] & 255));
                    line("EXPLICIT_BYTES " + address + " " + hex);
                    references(address, "EXPLICIT_XREF", true, "explicit data address " + address, 500);
                } else {
                    select(function, "explicit address " + address, 1000);
                }
            }
            decompile(directory, name, maxFunctions, timeout);
            line("EXPORT_FINISHED cancellation=false");
        }
        println("Kabus recovery exported to " + target.toAbsolutePath());
    }

    private void metadata() throws IOException {
        line("PROGRAM " + currentProgram.getName());
        line("EXECUTABLE " + currentProgram.getExecutablePath());
        line("FORMAT " + currentProgram.getExecutableFormat());
        line("MD5 " + currentProgram.getExecutableMD5());
        line("SHA256 " + currentProgram.getExecutableSHA256());
        line("LANGUAGE " + currentProgram.getLanguageID());
        line("COMPILER_SPEC " + currentProgram.getCompilerSpec().getCompilerSpecID());
        line("IMAGE_BASE " + currentProgram.getImageBase());
        int external = 0, internal = 0, thunks = 0;
        FunctionIterator functions = currentProgram.getFunctionManager().getFunctions(true);
        while (functions.hasNext()) {
            Function function = functions.next();
            if (function.isExternal()) external++; else internal++;
            if (function.isThunk()) thunks++;
        }
        FunctionIterator externalFunctions = currentProgram.getFunctionManager().getExternalFunctions();
        int externalFunctionCount = 0;
        while (externalFunctions.hasNext()) { externalFunctions.next(); externalFunctionCount++; }
        line("FUNCTION_COUNTS internal=" + internal + " external_iterator=" + externalFunctionCount +
            " external_in_address_iterator=" + external + " thunks=" + thunks);
        line("SCOPE Existing Ghidra analysis; no binary edits. Candidates are evidence, not confirmed loader identities.");
        line("ADDRESS_KIND Program virtual addresses; EXTERNAL addresses are Ghidra synthetic, not runtime VAs.");
        line("DECOMPILATION Pseudocode is approximate; failures and omissions are reported explicitly.");
    }

    private void imports() throws Exception {
        line("\n=== IMPORTS ===");
        SymbolIterator symbols = currentProgram.getSymbolTable().getExternalSymbols();
        int count = 0;
        while (symbols.hasNext()) {
            monitor.checkCancelled();
            Symbol symbol = symbols.next();
            ExternalLocation location = currentProgram.getExternalManager().getExternalLocation(symbol);
            line("IMPORT " + symbol.getName(true) + " synthetic=" + symbol.getAddress() +
                " library=" + (location == null ? "unknown" : location.getLibraryName()) +
                " original_address=" + (location == null ? "unknown" : location.getAddress()));
            references(symbol.getAddress(), "IMPORT_XREF", false, "import " + symbol.getName(), 20);
            if (matches(symbol.getName())) {
                references(symbol.getAddress(), "TARGET_IMPORT_XREF", true, "import " + symbol.getName(), 80);
            }
            count++;
        }
        line("IMPORT_SYMBOL_COUNT " + count);
    }

    private void exports() throws Exception {
        line("\n=== EXTERNAL ENTRY POINTS / EXPORTS ===");
        AddressIterator entries = currentProgram.getSymbolTable().getExternalEntryPointIterator();
        int count = 0;
        while (entries.hasNext()) {
            monitor.checkCancelled();
            Address address = entries.next();
            Symbol symbol = currentProgram.getSymbolTable().getPrimarySymbol(address);
            Function function = currentProgram.getFunctionManager().getFunctionAt(address);
            line("EXPORT_OR_ENTRY " + address + " symbol=" + (symbol == null ? "none" : symbol.getName(true)) +
                " function=" + describe(function));
            for (Symbol alias : currentProgram.getSymbolTable().getSymbols(address)) {
                line("ENTRY_SYMBOL " + address + " name=" + alias.getName(true));
            }
            select(function, "external entry/export " + address, 200);
            if (function != null) {
                // One call edge only: exported wrappers often delegate plugin behavior.
                Function implementation = function.isThunk() ? function.getThunkedFunction(true) : function;
                if (implementation == null) implementation = function;
                for (Function called : implementation.getCalledFunctions(monitor)) {
                    select(called, "direct callee of export " + address, 100);
                }
            }
            count++;
        }
        line("EXTERNAL_ENTRY_COUNT " + count);
    }

    private void strings() throws Exception {
        line("\n=== RELEVANT DEFINED STRINGS ===");
        DataIterator data = DefinedStringIterator.forProgram(currentProgram);
        int all = 0, relevant = 0;
        while (data.hasNext()) {
            monitor.checkCancelled();
            Data value = data.next();
            String text = StringDataInstance.getStringDataInstance(value).getStringValue();
            if (text == null) continue;
            all++;
            if (!matches(text)) continue;
            relevant++;
            line("STRING " + value.getAddress() + " length=" + value.getLength() + " text=" + quote(text));
            references(value.getAddress(), "STRING_XREF", true, "string " + value.getAddress() + " " + quote(text), 150);
        }
        line("STRING_COUNTS defined=" + all + " relevant=" + relevant);
    }

    private void symbols() throws Exception {
        line("\n=== RELEVANT SYMBOLS ===");
        SymbolIterator symbols = currentProgram.getSymbolTable().getAllSymbols(true);
        while (symbols.hasNext()) {
            monitor.checkCancelled();
            Symbol symbol = symbols.next();
            if (symbol.isExternal() || !matches(symbol.getName())) continue;
            Function function = currentProgram.getFunctionManager().getFunctionContaining(symbol.getAddress());
            line("SYMBOL " + symbol.getAddress() + " name=" + symbol.getName(true) + " function=" + describe(function));
            select(function, "symbol " + symbol.getName(true), 150);
            references(symbol.getAddress(), "SYMBOL_XREF", true, "symbol " + symbol.getName(true), 90);
        }
    }

    private void references(Address address, String label, boolean select, String reason, int priority) throws Exception {
        ReferenceIterator references = currentProgram.getReferenceManager().getReferencesTo(address);
        int count = 0;
        while (references.hasNext()) {
            monitor.checkCancelled();
            Reference reference = references.next();
            Address from = reference.getFromAddress();
            Function function = currentProgram.getFunctionManager().getFunctionContaining(from);
            line(label + " from=" + from + " to=" + address + " type=" + reference.getReferenceType() +
                " function=" + describe(function));
            if (select) select(function, reason + " via " + from, priority);
            // Resolve one level of pointer-table/IAT indirection; never invent a containing function.
            if (select && function == null && reference.getReferenceType().isData()) {
                ReferenceIterator indirect = currentProgram.getReferenceManager().getReferencesTo(from);
                while (indirect.hasNext()) {
                    monitor.checkCancelled();
                    Reference second = indirect.next();
                    Function owner = currentProgram.getFunctionManager().getFunctionContaining(second.getFromAddress());
                    line(label + "_INDIRECT from=" + second.getFromAddress() + " via=" + from +
                        " to=" + address + " type=" + second.getReferenceType() + " function=" + describe(owner));
                    select(owner, reason + " indirect via " + from, priority);
                }
            }
            count++;
        }
        if (count == 0) line(label + " to=" + address + " count=0");
    }

    private void select(Function function, String reason, int priority) {
        if (function == null || function.isExternal()) return;
        Address address = function.getEntryPoint();
        candidates.put(address, function);
        reasons.computeIfAbsent(address, key -> new LinkedHashSet<>()).add(reason);
        priorities.merge(address, priority, Math::max);
        if (function.isThunk()) {
            Function implementation = function.getThunkedFunction(true);
            if (implementation != null && !implementation.isExternal() && implementation != function) {
                Address target = implementation.getEntryPoint();
                candidates.put(target, implementation);
                reasons.computeIfAbsent(target, key -> new LinkedHashSet<>())
                    .add(reason + " resolved thunk " + address);
                priorities.merge(target, priority, Math::max);
            }
        }
    }

    private void decompile(Path directory, String name, int maximum, int timeout) throws Exception {
        line("\n=== TARGETED DECOMPILATION ===");
        List<Function> selected = new ArrayList<>(candidates.values());
        selected.sort(Comparator.<Function>comparingInt(f -> priorities.get(f.getEntryPoint())).reversed()
            .thenComparing(Function::getEntryPoint));
        line("CANDIDATE_COUNT " + selected.size() + " limit=" + maximum + " timeout_seconds=" + timeout);
        DecompInterface decompiler = new DecompInterface();
        int completed = 0, failed = 0, omitted = 0;
        try {
            if (!decompiler.openProgram(currentProgram)) {
                throw new IOException("Decompiler could not open program: " + decompiler.getLastMessage());
            }
            for (int i = 0; i < selected.size(); i++) {
                monitor.checkCancelled();
                Function function = selected.get(i);
                Address entry = function.getEntryPoint();
                line("CANDIDATE " + describe(function) + " priority=" + priorities.get(entry));
                for (String reason : reasons.get(entry)) line("  REASON " + reason);
                if (i >= maximum) {
                    line("  STATUS OMITTED_SELECTION_LIMIT");
                    omitted++;
                    continue;
                }
                DecompileResults result = decompiler.decompileFunction(function, timeout, monitor);
                if (!result.decompileCompleted() || result.getDecompiledFunction() == null) {
                    line("  STATUS FAILED timed_out=" + result.isTimedOut() + " cancelled=" + result.isCancelled() +
                        " error=" + quote(result.getErrorMessage()));
                    failed++;
                    continue;
                }
                Path output = directory.resolve(name + "." + entry + ".c");
                Files.writeString(output, "/* Ghidra approximation: " + describe(function) +
                    "\n * Source program: " + currentProgram.getName() + "\n */\n" +
                    result.getDecompiledFunction().getC(), StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
                line("  STATUS COMPLETED output=" + output.getFileName() + " diagnostic=" + quote(result.getErrorMessage()));
                completed++;
            }
        } finally {
            decompiler.dispose();
            line("DECOMPILE_COUNTS completed=" + completed + " failed=" + failed + " omitted=" + omitted);
        }
    }

    private boolean matches(String text) { return RELEVANT.matcher(text).find(); }
    private String describe(Function function) {
        return function == null ? "none" : function.getName(true) + "@" + function.getEntryPoint();
    }
    private String quote(String text) {
        if (text == null) return "null";
        return "\"" + text.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace("\"", "\\\"")
            .replace("\r", "\\r").replace("\n", "\\n").replace("\t", "\\t") + "\"";
    }
    private void line(String text) throws IOException { report.write(text); report.newLine(); }
}

`tests/levels/sweep.cmake`:

```cmake
# level_sweep CTest driver: cmake -DK22=kabus22 -DGAME=GAME_ROOT -DSAVES=WINDOWS_GAME_DIR -DOUT=DIR [-DONLY=id;id] [-DARGS=--renderer;opengl;...] -P sweep.cmake
# For every row of levels.tsv (level N, entered from level M): load the row's original save through YukleMenu, then make two
# transitions the way an LY_Kapi door does (LevelYonetim.wdl LY_Tarama sets LY_HedefLevel=my.LevelID; LY_YuklemeTakip ->
# LevelYukle runs Acikmi(old)/Cikis(old)/level_load/Giris(old)): first into M, claiming M's own entry level as the origin
# (LY_AktifLevelID), then from M into N through the original path, so N's Acikmi/Giris see M's real state (harita_*).
# Then 600 frames of play (Up held for the first 120), checking that the player stays above the level geometry.
# Headless by default; ARGS replaces --headless (for example --renderer;opengl;--window-mode;windowed;--resolution;1280x720) and
# then each run writes OUT/<id>/out/level-<id>.ppm. Writes OUT/summary.tsv. Engine/script errors end the process (non-zero exit).
if(NOT ARGS)
  set(ARGS --headless)
endif()
file(STRINGS "${CMAKE_CURRENT_LIST_DIR}/levels.tsv" rows REGEX "^[0-9]")
foreach(row IN LISTS rows)
  string(REPLACE "\t" ";" f "${row}")
  list(GET f 0 id)
  list(GET f 4 from_${id})
  list(GET f 5 hold_${id})
endforeach()
file(REMOVE_RECURSE "${OUT}")
set(base "${OUT}/base")
file(MAKE_DIRECTORY "${base}/data" "${base}/config" "${base}/state")
set(ENV{XDG_DATA_HOME} "${base}/data")
set(ENV{XDG_CONFIG_HOME} "${base}/config")
set(ENV{XDG_STATE_HOME} "${base}/state")
execute_process(COMMAND "${K22}" --import-saves "${SAVES}" --data "${GAME}" RESULT_VARIABLE code OUTPUT_QUIET)
if(NOT code EQUAL 0)
  message(FATAL_ERROR "save import failed")
endif()
set(summary "id\twmb\tcharacter\tsave\tfrom\tresult\tframes\tcontrol\tdetail\n")
set(failed "")
foreach(row IN LISTS rows)
  string(REPLACE "\t" ";" f "${row}")
  list(GET f 0 id)
  list(GET f 1 wmb)
  list(GET f 2 who)
  list(GET f 3 save)
  if(ONLY AND NOT id IN_LIST ONLY)
    continue()
  endif()
  set(from ${from_${id}})
  set(via ${from_${from}})
  set(root "${OUT}/${id}")
  file(MAKE_DIRECTORY "${root}/runtime")
  file(COPY "${base}/data" "${base}/config" "${base}/state" DESTINATION "${root}")
  file(CHMOD "${root}/runtime" DIRECTORY_PERMISSIONS OWNER_READ OWNER_WRITE OWNER_EXECUTE)
  set(who_id 0)
  if(who STREQUAL "Ebru")
    set(who_id 1)
  elseif(who STREQUAL "Inzar")
    set(who_id 2)
  endif()
  set(checks "")
  foreach(i RANGE 1 6)
    if(i EQUAL 1)
      string(APPEND checks "down Up\nframes 100\n")
    elseif(i EQUAL 2)
      string(APPEND checks "frames 20\nup Up\nframes 80\n")
    else()
      string(APPEND checks "frames 100\n")
    endif()
    string(APPEND checks "assert player.z > $levelminz - 100\n")
  endforeach()
  # The settle waits keep a request from being lost (LY_YuklemeTakip clears LY_HedefLevel one second after LevelYukle starts)
  # and from racing the previous load's fade-out loop; a level whose entry keeps control (no_control) leaves the fade up.
  file(WRITE "${root}/level-${id}.k22s" "# level ${id} ${wmb} (${who}, kayit${save}.sav, via ${from} entered from ${via})
realtime off
load-save ${save}
wait until LY_HedefLevel == 0 && level_yuklendi_ok == 1 && LYP_Fade.visible == 0 timeout 6000
assert Aktif_Player == ${who_id}
set LY_AktifLevelID ${via}
set LY_HedefLevel ${from}
wait until LY_AktifLevelID == ${from} timeout 3000
wait until LY_HedefLevel == 0 && level_yuklendi_ok == 1 && LYP_Fade.visible == 0 || LY_HedefLevel == 0 && ${hold_${from}} timeout 1200
set LY_HedefLevel ${id}
wait until LY_AktifLevelID == ${id} timeout 3000
assert $level == \"${wmb}\"
wait until oyuncu_pasif == 0 && koruyucu_pasif == 0 && LYP_Fade.visible == 0 || ${hold_${id}} timeout 1200
store x0 player.x
store y0 player.y
print player.z
print $levelminz
${checks}print player.x - @x0
print player.y - @y0
print oyuncu_pasif
print LY_AktifLevelID
capture level-${id}
")
  set(ENV{XDG_DATA_HOME} "${root}/data")
  set(ENV{XDG_CONFIG_HOME} "${root}/config")
  set(ENV{XDG_STATE_HOME} "${root}/state")
  set(ENV{XDG_RUNTIME_DIR} "${root}/runtime")
  execute_process(COMMAND "${K22}" --data "${GAME}" ${ARGS} --scenario "${root}/level-${id}.k22s" --scenario-out "${root}/out"
    RESULT_VARIABLE code OUTPUT_FILE "${root}/log.txt" ERROR_FILE "${root}/stderr.txt" TIMEOUT 600)
  file(STRINGS "${root}/log.txt" last REGEX "^scenario: [^ ]+\\.k22s ")
  string(REGEX MATCH "frames=([0-9]+)" _ "${last}")
  set(frames "${CMAKE_MATCH_1}")
  file(STRINGS "${root}/log.txt" pasif REGEX "print oyuncu_pasif -- ")
  string(REGEX REPLACE ".*-- " "" pasif "${pasif}")
  set(control yes)
  if(NOT pasif STREQUAL "0")
    set(control "no (scripted)")
  endif()
  set(detail "")
  if(code EQUAL 0)
    set(result PASS)
  else()
    set(result FAIL)
    list(APPEND failed ${id})
    file(STRINGS "${root}/log.txt" bad REGEX " FAIL ")
    file(STRINGS "${root}/stderr.txt" fatal REGEX "^kabus22: ")
    string(REPLACE "\t" " " detail "${fatal} ${bad}")
  endif()
  message(STATUS "level ${id} ${wmb} ${who}: ${result} frames=${frames} control=${control} ${detail}")
  string(APPEND summary "${id}\t${wmb}\t${who}\t${save}\t${from}\t${result}\t${frames}\t${control}\t${detail}\n")
endforeach()
file(WRITE "${OUT}/summary.tsv" "${summary}")
if(failed)
  message(FATAL_ERROR "level sweep failed: ${failed} (logs under ${OUT})")
endif()

# Reference comparison with the original: Ebru, Ev (kayit6.sav). Loaded view after the original load menu.
realtime on
#wine: wait-log 1st

`tests/scenarios/combat_kriz_aa_gun.k22s`:

```k22s
# requires: saves
# Kız Kulesi (slot 10 = kayit9.sav): Demir runs round the café to the anti-aircraft gun, mounts it with D
# (dinamik_modeller.wdl ucakfish_Tarama → ucak_savar), and fires at the diving atilgan_ai enemies.
# Each new D press scans a 25° cone and slews onto the nearest target (ucakyakin_bul/ucakyakina_don); bullets
# (ucakkursun_gonder) take 20 health per hit, and an atilgan at 0 health plays its death fall and bumps
# atilgan_sayisi (atilgan_yara.wdl:566-635). The divers approach from the gun's right (world pan ≈ -80),
# so every cycle re-aims there, lifts the barrel and fires. Enemy knock-backs are random: waypoints avoid the café benches.

`tests/scenarios/combat_kriz_game_over.k22s`:

```k22s
# requires: saves
# Game over at Kız Kulesi (slot 10 = kayit9.sav): Demir stands still while the atilgan_ai divers strike him
# (atilgan_yara.wdl atilgan_atakveretex, 4*time per contact). Death is decided on player Enerji (skill1, klasik_yara.wdl:60):
# every oyuncu2.wdl state loop checks `if(my.enerji<=0){goto(d_olum_loop);}` (:778ff), and d_olum_loop sets game_over_start.
# oyn_yaralanma is only the last health copied by the d_yaralan_go branches (:1839ff), so at death it can still be the last
# positive value or already <= 0 (a hit during the hurt animation's final wait), depending on contact timing; it is not asserted.
# K22.wdl game_over_strtr fades to black, shows gameover_panel, returns to level0.wmb and the main menu (dismenuac).
# The run then loads the same slot again through the original load menu.
realtime off
load-save 9
wait until LY_AktifLevelID == 31 && level_yuklendi_ok == 1 && player != 0 && oyuncu_pasif == 0 timeout 7200
store hp oyn_yaralanma
assert @hp > 0
wait until game_over_start == 1 timeout 36000
assert player.skill1 <= 0
print oyn_yaralanma
wait until kararma_fon_pnl.visible == 1 timeout 600
wait until gameover_panel.visible == 1 && gameover_panel.alpha >= 100 timeout 1200
capture kriz_game_over_panel
wait until LY_AktifLevelID == 0 && game_over_start == 0 timeout 3000
assert $level == "level0.wmb"
wait until AMP_OyunYukle.visible == 1 || ParlaklikMenuAcik == 1 timeout 3000
frames 30
capture kriz_game_over_main_menu
load-save 9
wait until LY_AktifLevelID == 31 && level_yuklendi_ok == 1 && player != 0 && oyuncu_pasif == 0 timeout 7200
assert oyn_yaralanma == @hp
capture kriz_reloaded_after_game_over

```k22s
# requires: saves
# Native quicksave/quickload (docs/CONSOLE.md): F5 writes the next slot of the original save list through the original
# SLG_LevelKaydet/YD_OyunuKaydet/SLG_Kaydet and adds the player position to the slot sidecar; F9 loads the newest slot through
# Yukleme_Kontrol and puts the player back where it was saved. Demir, kizic2 (level 37), from original kayit10.sav.
# Continued by quicksave2_restart in the same private installation.

load-save 10
wait until LY_AktifLevelID == 37 && level_yuklendi_ok == 1 && player != 0 && oyuncu_pasif == 0 timeout 7200

store ammo S_Kursun_Sayisi[1]
store saves aktif_kayit_sayisi

print player.y

assert aktif_kayit_sayisi == @saves + 1
